Amiga: the credit scroller reads a hires glyph whole
events.author: ataribaby42

events.title: Amiga: the credit scroller reads a hires glyph whole
events.message:
Amiga: the credit scroller reads a hires glyph whole

W scrolls the version and score under the flight view. The scroller was built
around eight-pixel cells, one byte per plane with two characters to a word,
but in a 640 screen CHARSET_PTR names the sixteen-byte font. It indexed by
eight and read a byte a line, so it drew half of the wrong glyph, and it fed
a new character every eight pixels while the cell was sixteen wide, so what
did arrive was cut in half again.

A hires cell is now a whole word. SCROLL_CELL takes the cell's width as its
operand size, the way Q_PUSH does, so one line of pixels is written once
rather than once per screen width; the index steps by sixteen, a character
lasts twice as many scroll steps, and SCROLL_WORDS and SCROLL_STRIDE carry the
widths the loops and the buffer need. The 320 screens keep their layout.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: hold the blitter only while the clear runs
events.message:
Amiga: hold the blitter only while the clear runs

AMIGA_ENTRY took the blitter before the game started and kept it to the end.
Booting a fastdraw build from its ADF then hung with an empty screen on a
512 KB A500 under Kickstart 1.3. Holding it is what does it, not the call:
taking it and handing it straight back boots, and so does adding the WaitBlit
the documented sequence asks for while still holding it.

BEGIN_CLEAR takes it, waits for the system's last blit and WAIT_CLEAR hands it
back as the fill ends, so it spans the drawing and never a disk read. DISK.M68
reads a saved commander mid-game, which ownership held that long would hang
the same way.

events.title: Amiga: HORIZ_LINE reads the plane words once per span
events.message:
Amiga: HORIZ_LINE reads the plane words once per span

Both edge words went through MASK_PLOT, which fetched the four plane words
through A1 each time, and the fill loop fetched them a third time. HORIZ_LINE
now loads them into D1/D3/D4/D6 on entry and MASK_PLOT takes them from there,
which also shortens eight instructions per span from a displacement operand
to a register one.

Measured on an A500: docking 194 ms of frame work to 183, a planet 89 to 81.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: the radar blips and missile sprites follow the display scale
events.message:
Amiga: the radar blips and missile sprites follow the display scale

Two panel details stayed at 320-pixel width on a 640 screen. The main radar's
head and body masks were written out as literal tables, four and two pixels
wide; they are now generated from head_width and body_width, both scaled by
zoom_x. The missile indicators are the only sprites outside BITMAPS.IMG, so
nothing expanded them at load; the build now writes a copy at the display's
scale beside the objects and the cockpit includes that.

The mask of a missile cell is positional, not the OR of its planes, because
the ten opaque columns include black. Scaling keeps that split.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: HORIZ_LINE fills wide spans in longs
events.message:
Amiga: HORIZ_LINE fills wide spans in longs

The fill loop wrote the four plane words one word at a time. From
long_fill_min words up it doubles each plane word into a long and writes two
words per instruction, leaving an odd trailing word to the word path. The
same bytes reach the screen; what goes away is opcode fetch, which on an A500
shares the bus with them.

Narrow spans keep the word loop, because doubling the four words costs twelve
instructions and does not pay back under six.

Measured on an A500 against the same build with the long path disabled:
docking 180 ms of rasterising to 170, a planet 73 to 70.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: the circle path keeps the centre and the colour in registers
events.message:
Amiga: the circle path keeps the centre and the colour in registers

CIRCLE_HORIZ reloaded the colour pointer for every span and saved a register
the call chain never touches. CIRCLE_PLOTXY reread the centre from the
workspace three times per step. CIRCLE now passes the colour in A1 and the
sign extended centre in A3/A4, which also retires two dead instructions.

A planet on an A500 drops from 73 ms of rasterising to 71.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: the polygon row loop works out of registers
events.message:
Amiga: the polygon row loop works out of registers

SOLID_POLYGON kept the row address, the right arm pointer, the colour pointer
and the dither phase in the workspace, and reloaded them for every span. A4
now walks the row address, the right arm is read at a fixed displacement from
the left one, and A1 and A5 hold the two dither phases, swapped by EXG. Two
workspace words go away; nothing else read them.

Launch from the station on an A500 drops from 205 ms of rasterising to 173.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: shift instead of multiplying by two in BLOCK, BLITTER and XOR
events.message:
Amiga: shift instead of multiplying by two in BLOCK, BLITTER and XOR

Each turns a word count into a byte offset once per call. The ADDA.W that
follows uses the low word, which the shift leaves the same as the multiply
did, and a 68000 pays forty cycles for the MULU against four.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: Amiga: the blitter starts the clear as the present releases the buffer
events.message:
Amiga: the blitter starts the clear as the present releases the buffer

It ran from CLEAR_IMAGE, so it had only the game logic to finish in, and on
an A500 in hires the drawing still waited a few milliseconds for it.
SWAP_SCREEN now starts it on the buffer the present has just released, which
adds the sky update and the frame budget wait to its head start.

BEGIN_CLEAR programmes the registers for both callers. CLEAR_IMAGE leaves a
blit that is already filling the same buffer alone, and only a frame that
cleared hands the next one on, so a menu screen never inherits one. The frame
that opens a menu drains instead, since it will not clear.

The clear reading follows the wait: WAIT_CLEAR adds what it spends draining
BBUSY, so the number is the delay the clear caused rather than the cost of
programming the registers, which read zero on a 68000 whatever the blit did.
events.author: pulchart

events.title: aga: a palette write rides with the next present — the outgoing big picture no longer wears the incoming colours
events.message:
aga: a palette write rides with the next present — the outgoing big picture no longer wears the incoming colours

A1200 on v0.9.28: "almost 100% there", except a big picture "takes a second
or so to unload, like it leaves some pixels behind" before the next one or
the 3D view. Filmed at 25 fps in amiberry (-DFRUA_AUTOPLAY into a generated
design whose entry event is a bigpic, x11grab across the dismissing Return):
four frames before the screen settles — 1.4 s of the OUTGOING picture in the
DUNGEON's palette (black with magenta/orange speckle), the walk screen, then
1.6 s with the 3D view blacked out, then the final frame.

On a hardware-palette backend a CLUT write recolours the screen at once; the
pixels that want those colours arrive at the next present, a second or more
later here. #20 (sky/floor flash) was one instance fixed for one caller;
this is the rule. The #8 event-tail hold does not help — it holds pixels,
the palette still landed, and it is armed only for walk steps anyway.

dsp_backend_t.palette_with_present (last field; AGA sets it, video.cfg
agapalsync=off opts out for a hardware A/B): qd_set_palette keeps the
logical palette current and remembers a pending window, forwarded right
after the backend present, after a rect present, on a clean present, from
the engine's event pump when no hold is outstanding, and from jt1067 after
a colour-cycle commit. The title blackout supersedes anything pending, and
qd_set_palette_deferred routes straight through on such a backend. Not the
Nova (its ~0.5 s present is a different trade, untestable off the card);
TT is eligible and left alone.

After: picture in its own colours -> walk -> final. Both the recoloured
picture and the black view hole are gone; the picture's own cycling runs
throughout. The first version FROZE the SSI title's star animation — its
wait loop cycles the palette without presenting or pumping events — and the
title capture caught it (one colour-count signature where the release shows
five); hence the flush in jt1067. Title roll signature-identical to v0.9.28
again. Host tests green; ST and ECS build.

events.title: recreate_kit: the declared I/O map — one door for any I/O byte; the stack band ends at the frame
events.message:
recreate_kit: the declared I/O map — one door for any I/O byte; the stack band ends at the frame

Phase 15 (TRAP_MODEL.md): a case declares `io_seed={address: byte}` for any
byte of the I/O page. The named Phase-7 slots are routed into their model by
`emu.seed_split` and the YM2149 block is refused by name (register-keyed,
latch-dependent), so the case author has one door; both cores serve a declared
byte on every read as one ledger entry carrying the width (8/16/32 —
`io_read8/16/32` on the candidate), a read of a byte the run stored to refuses
(staleness), an undeclared I/O read still refuses by address, and the
untranslated 32-bit spellings ($ffff8260) are refused on both shores rather
than installed as rows no read can match. io_serve precedes the ROM window and
ROM_END/RAM_END are pinned below the I/O page (tos102us holds by zero bytes).
emu.run_bench takes io_seed and installs the map per run.

The stack band (befc249) broke two PRG projects: Bubble Ghost's Alcyon callees
write their arguments back above the sentinel, and Wonder Boy's blit cases
write the image's last word. One formula for both modes: the dropped band ends
at STACK_TOP + SENTINEL_SLOT_BYTES + STACK_ARGS_BYTES (24, the deepest unstaged
frame write measured across all seven projects, pinned as an equality), and
everything above it is COMPARED — wonderboy 6465 and bubbleghost 1909 green.

tools/hw_portability.py's PSG_BLOCK_END pin follows the constant to os.h
(OS_PSG_BLOCK_END; 16 reds → the 3 pre-existing stale-figure reds remain).
Docs: agent-playbook §13 names the remedy; docs/README routes to Phase 15.
Kit suite 941 → 961; the six PRG projects unchanged.
events.author: geogeo28

pixel value 255 as transparent, as the Mac's L2bfc does. Mac art never
puts a 255 in such a piece (0 pixels across all 185 mode-2 pieces of the
base art) and neither does SSI's DOS art (0 across 184 method-18 pieces),
so the key never did anything faithful. A fan module does: Curse of the
Fire Dragon's title art keeps its brightest yellow in slot 255, and the
port drew the base marble through 704 holes on the AD&D logo where DOS
FRUA 1.2 (DOSBox, same CURSE.DSN) shows the yellow. Drop the key in the
opaque arm only; the transparent methods keep theirs.

events.message:
aga: -DFRUA_PALTEST — a one-photo colour-path test for a real machine

Paints all 256 palette entries as a 32x8 grid (row = AGA bank) with ramps
whose low nibbles matter, through the game's own copper list, and holds
it 12 s after the display comes up. A photo then separates "the art's
colours" from "the machine's colour path": groups of identical swatches =
LOCT low nibbles ignored, a dead row = a bank's writes lost, a wrong hue =
a channel wired wrong. Built for the A1200 + IceDrake report that a
module's bright yellow came out pale where amiberry shows it right.

events.title: flyingshark perf: gated-blitter twin + pass-B codegen; light page at 3 blanks
events.message:
flyingshark perf: gated-blitter twin + pass-B codegen; light page at 3 blanks

Reconstruction
- src/asm/clipped.S: the original's four gated sprite blitters (0x14e1e /
  0x14f06 / 0x1505e / 0x15230) transcribed as 22 byte-identical segments with
  ONE declared substitution — each `btst #n,$16426.l` (an absolute the kit's
  twin runner cannot express, since the image base is a run-time argument)
  becomes `btst #n,(%a2)` on the same bit, %a2 = image + A_blit_clip_mask,
  loaded once in the glue. The gate byte is still read from memory at every
  group of every row, which the poked-destination case pins. 12,589 ->
  3,894 cycles a call against the original's 3,802.
- src/sprite.c: the BLIT_SPRITE_ROWS_GATED seam (register ABI, %a2 as an
  input); the C blitter and its glue compile only off target; pass B's record
  offset computed 32-bit (drops an andi.l per record) and SpriteBlitEntry at
  eight bytes (a shift instead of four adds per drawn record).

Harness
- test/test_asm_clipped.py (120 tests): the differential over the gate sweep,
  shift sweep, one row, a high-word count, a fuzz and a gate-overlap case;
  pins for the segments, their tiling of the original body, the substitution,
  the dbf displacement and the cost (twin == original - 8*groups*rows +
  FRAME, FRAME measured 314/330/346/344 = the unclipped frame + 36 for the
  gate register). Ten gate mutations proved red.
- atari/assert_twin_bytes.py: a name=lo:hi:sites form that derives the
  segments and asserts they tile, so the shipped gate is not a prefix compare.

Measured (atari/profile.py pace, from d424973): 4.321 -> 3.696 blanks a
frame (13.5 fps; the original is 4.000 flat). The light page went from 4
blanks to the game's own 3-blank budget; the heavy page stays at 5: its work
is 684,096 wall against the 641,039 four blanks need, and what is left is
outside src/sprite.c (the unclipped seam, the VBL tick, the text list, the
restore replay). Text 54,784 B, floppy free 16,384 B; 3,851 tests, guarded
11,523 runs, framebuffer identity green on both builds.

Docs
- STATUS.md levers 8/9, the segment table, the shipped-only %a2 gap row;
  src/asm/README.md "The first body that is not byte-identical";
  names.txt cmt at 0x14e1e naming the four shared tails.

events.title: 3d: a picture's colour-cycle range no longer outlives the picture — the ground stops cycling (#21)
events.message:
3d: a picture's colour-cycle range no longer outlives the picture — the ground stops cycling (#21)

A1200 report on v0.9.25, Curse of the Fire Dragon outdoors at night:
"color cycling is happening on the ground". Not the backdrop's doing — its
loader installs no cycle records. Five base-game pictures carry a cycle
record over CLUT 144..175, the backdrop band (BIGPIC entry 3: 144+8, PICB
27: 160+16, PICC 25: 144+16 and 160+16, PICE: 86+65), and jt993 -> jt1069
installs them when the picture shows. On the Mac they die when the walk's
palette comes back, because that install goes through jt1069 too and its
Phase 3a frees every range the request overlaps. The port's wall, backdrop
and UI bands are DIRECT installs (port_clut_install*), so nothing freed
them: jt1067 kept rotating slots 144..175 — by then the backdrop's mirrored
colours — and committing them every 11 ticks.

port_cycle_free_overlap does Phase 3a's bookkeeping (mark the slots used,
empty the entry, raise its -3162 flag) in both direct installers. The wall
sets' own fire cycles are freed with their band and re-armed by
dungeon_cycle_ensure before the next jt1067, exactly as after a picture.

Proved on the Falcon (Hatari), machine-independent since l6e58 writes
through qd_set_palette on every backend: mk_bigpic_design.py --picture 242
(id 240+k is BIGPIC entry k+1; entry 3 holds the 144+8 range), beginplay,
Return, eight stills standing still. v0.9.25: six of seven frames differ
from the first inside the view hole. This build: all identical, and the
FRUA_CYCTRACE log shows "direct install frees range base=144" at the
backdrop install. The plain fixed build's menu is byte-identical to the
release's.

  written as two 32-bit halves it compiled to a 70-cycle register shift per
  step; now the original's own lsr.l/roxr.l (20). fp_pack_double's
  normalise loop tests the top bit and takes the tail's +1 before the loop:
  40 -> 22 cycles a pass against the original's 24. fp_dispatch 8,959 ->
  5,368 cycles/call (x2.26 -> x1.36); the whole fp package 22.6K -> 14.6K
  cycles/frame (original 11.4K); game_frame_update x1.49 -> x1.24.

  the direct pack test, which had none past one; three rewrites brute-
  forced equivalent by the review's finders (2-4M cases each).

  to the pointer, so a corrupted base is tellable apart from the wrapped

Harness (atari/)
- bubble_backend.c: the GEM door's contrl accesses are d16(An) behind a
  CURSOR_BARRIER in the VDI arm (A_vdi_contrl is past a word displacement,
  so each slot cost a 32-bit immediate + indexed access).

  swallowed the value expression, so `& 15` passed it green), plus a check
  that the trapped gate still carries its andi.l #PSG_REG_MASK.

  original's five bare port pairs (0x14682..0x1487c); the trap handler

events.title: bubbleghost: XBIOS video door — the presentation palette is right during the speech
events.message:
bubbleghost: XBIOS video door — the presentation palette is right during the speech

Play-test defect: the "Welcome to Bubble Ghost" speech played under the
wrong palette. Setscreen/Setpalette/Setcolor/Vsync answered `return 0`
INSIDE the verified xbios wrapper, so the target shim could only reissue
Setpalette after the slice — whose next instruction is the jsr into the
LOA. Fix at depth:
- kit: os_setscreen / os_setpalette / os_setcolor / os_vsync doors, each
  an OS-event kind (TRAP_MODEL phase 14): no image effect, semantics
  unchanged, but the ORDER of the video calls is now a pinned surface;
  the oracle shim logs the same four from XBIOS 5/6/7/0x25. Joust and
  BuggyBoy model this group through their own seams and declare the
  `tos_xbios_video_unmodeled` waiver (a reconstruction pass they owe).
- bubbleghost cores: the four wrappers go through the door. The door
  immediately reddened 45 gameplay cases: frame_blow_or_recover and
  frame_death_sequence made NO Setcolor call — the ghost never turned
  pink when its breath ran out. Three os_setcolor lines added.
- target: the shim issues the real traps at the instant the core calls
  them (bases and the palette table translated); the "reissue one slice
  late" hack is gone. New smoke anchor at the jsr into the LOA: our pens
  equal the original's and GHOST.PRE's palette, on both sides.
- `smoke.py game`: press G then 1 (repeatedly — the player prompt's
  flush eats an early key), wait on the program's own frame counter,
  compare the first room frame's framebuffer + pens against the original
  at the breakpoint (photograph after the settle): identical. The
  reported "G returns to TOS" did not reproduce headless (57 room frames,
  no fault, no Pterm); the mouse is the input no headless run can move.

Kit 764, bubbleghost 1895, joust 4368, zynaps 4751+4s, wonderboy 6465,
buggyboy 296; 8 mutants killed.

bubbleghost atari: BUBBLE.PRG from the verified cores boots to the menu under Hatari

recreate/atari/ builds the game from the 132 verified cores, UNMODIFIED
(build.sh refuses a dirty or untracked core: git diff on src/include),
with the m68k-elf toolchain: the OS is real on target — trap #2 for the
VDI/AES (the game's own parameter blocks, pointers translated at the
seam), GEMDOS/XBIOS/BIOS wrappers in bubble_os.s (file I/O first, the
handle-0 note), the Timer C ISR and the trap #9 PSG gate installed for
real, GHOST.LOA executed for the speech with its sample pointer
translated, Mshrink to a 664 KiB image (75 KB spare on a 1 MB machine).

smoke.py judges the boot on the surfaces of docs/on-target-execution.md:
exit status + log, the trap ledger (call for call, lengths compared),
the hardware-state vector (pens, rez, video base), the displayed
framebuffer against a savebin of the SHIPPED binary anchored at the same
PC (all 32,000 bytes identical), the rendered capture, the program's own
43-field record (every field asserted), timelines reported. Three
negative controls (a moved pen, a poked word, an ISR that does not
chain) each redden exactly their surfaces; `floppy` boots disk/BUBBLE.ST
to the desktop.

Defects only the target could show, all fixed and written up: the trap
#9 gate installed one instruction late (bombs); no Mshrink, so TOS's VDI
got handle 0 and drew nothing while every self-check stayed green; the
conterm mirror was a no-op (0x7 at the anchor); the floppy opens no A:\
window (TOS 1.04 ignores the shipped DESKTOP.INF's #W and #Z lines — the
game is two double-clicks away, as the original's disk is).

Unpinned, stated in atari/README.md: play is unjudged (mouse-driven; the
headless protocol has no mouse motion), nothing on iron, the XBIOS group
has no seam under xbios_trap_call (Setcolor/Vsync not reissued), the
speech is not heard headless. hatari_headless gains settle_chain /

events.message:
tools: tree2adf.py — any directory tree onto 880 KB ADFs, for the Gotek

A bare file on the Gotek stick is invisible to the Amiga; only images are.
mkdatadisks.sh covers OpenUA data with manifests; this covers an arbitrary
tree (a driver, a package the user owns, a module) with no installer
semantics — directory structure kept on every disk so the disks merge back
into one drawer, files packed whole largest-first, writes checked.

First use: Roadshow 1.15 (4.7 MB, 263 files) -> 6 disks, every file read
back from the images and diffed against the source. Directory blocks are
charged once per DISK: charging them per file packed the same tree into 7
disks with the last one 91% empty.

events.title: recreate_kit: model the VDI/AES, console reads, Fseek, IKBD and console ledgers
events.message:
recreate_kit: model the VDI/AES, console reads, Fseek, IKBD and console ledgers

Bubble Ghost is a GEM application — every string, bar and sprite goes
through trap #2 — and reads keys with Cconis/Crawcin/Cnecin, so nothing
that draws could be differentially verified. The deterministic model now
covers it, identically on both sides (src/gem.c + src/raster.c are the
first stateless kit sources linked into liboracle.so AND every candidate;
the workstation state lives in the image so the byte diff owns it).

Model
- VDI (17 opcodes): v_opnvwk (honours work_in; zeroes all 45+6 outputs),
  v_clsvwk, v_clrwk, vst_*/vsf_*/vswr_mode, vr_recfl (hollow = colour 0,
  solid = fill colour, patterned refused), vro_cpyfm (ST device format,
  1-8 planes, all 16 logic ops, direction chosen on overlap, clipping only
  when fd_addr == 0 — the VDI's own rule), v_gtext through a synthetic 8x8
  font (pixel fidelity to TOS is an on-target matter, said so), vq_mouse /
  vq_key_s from the poke block, vs_clip, cursor calls. AES: appl_init,
  appl_exit, graf_handle, graf_mouse. Anything else refuses by opcode.
- GEMDOS Cconis/Crawcin/Cnecin over a queue of staged keys
  (harness.console_keys, 8 deep; refuse when empty — never block, never
  fabricate), Fseek modes 0/1/2 over the staged-file cursor, Crawio write,
  Cconws (returns the count), BIOS Bconout(4) as IKBD bytes.
- One ordered OFF-IMAGE EVENT LEDGER (CONOUT, IKBD, GEM_MOUSE, VDI_CURSOR)
  compared per run like the Dosound/PSG ledgers, armed for the poison
  re-run too (the attribution pass used to skip every new model).
- os_malloc: the candidate-side arena (base and limit installed, Malloc(-1)
  answers the free size, refuses past the ceiling); harness compares the
  two bump pointers per run.
- Parameter-block pointers bounded before wrapping; the raster core's
  per-pixel addressing hoisted (7x at identical semantics).

Tests: kit 631 -> 730 — an independent Python raster reference over all
16 ops incl. overlap, every modeled opcode driven through BOTH doors
(trap #2 vs os_vdi) with ledgers compared, refusal paths, 20 mutants
caught (one first-pass survivor, an unterminated Cconws, closed). Joust,
Zynaps, Wonder Boy, BuggyBoy, Bubble Ghost suites unchanged/green.

Docs: TRAP_MODEL phases 11-13 (with "reached by" per opcode and measured
mutation lines), README (eight groups, console keys, the poke-block
widening rule), docs/tos-os-calls.md pointer; Wonder Boy's poke-block
waiver rewritten for the widened block (0x600..0x65f).

  priority/stop_all, the 200 Hz Timer C ISR (entered directly; it chains

events.title: bubbleghost: bootstrap — cipher wrapper cracked, Ghidra in runtime layout, assets
events.message:
bubbleghost: bootstrap — cipher wrapper cracked, Ghidra in runtime layout, assets

New project projects/bubbleghost/ (Bubble Ghost, ERE 1987 / Accolade 1988, ST).

Loader / protection
- GHOST.PRG is not crunched: a copy-protection-keyed stream cipher (CRC of
  the fuzzy sectors on cyl 79 -> 16-bit key 0x586b; SR flags are part of the
  keystream; a self-modifying dbf displacement takes effect one iteration late
  through the 68000 prefetch queue). tools/depack_bubbleghost.py inflates it
  statically to GHOST_PLAIN.PRG, byte-identical to the image Hatari decrypts
  (boot_ghost.py finds the whole TEXT in RAM; the protection PASSES in Hatari
  from the Pasti dump). notes/loader.md has the annotated wrapper.
- GHOST.LOA is a standalone MFP Timer-A PCM player, not the loader.

Ghidra
- Alcyon/DRI small-model C: crt0 moves DATA above BSS and addresses every
  global n(a4). tools/prg_relayout.py rewrites the PRG into that runtime
  layout, SetRegisterValue.java pins a4 = 0x24f1a before analysis, and
  headless.sh gained optional extra pre-scripts. 10,031 `a4 + n` expressions
  -> 0; 8,166 globals resolve; Ghidra address == runtime address. 134
  functions, 38 named from body reads (names.txt), anchors in notes/anchors.md.

Assets
- GHOST.PRE / GHOST.DAT = 32x32 word-planar tiles (512 B) + trailing palette;
  extract_gfx.py writes the title and the 360-tile sheet. GHOST.VOI = one
  unsigned 8-bit phrase at 2457600/(4*41) = 14,985 Hz (rate index 3 in the
  LOA header, which the game never patches); extract_audio.py exports it.

events.title: instdisk: a backslash in a typed destination is not a separator on the Amiga — make it one
events.message:
instdisk: a backslash in a typed destination is not a separator on the Amiga — make it one

Field report, A1200, 2026-09-05: "I typed the path of Personal:Games\OpenUA\
but I didn't see it anywhere". AmigaDOS separates with '/' and treats '\' as
an ordinary filename character, so that destination was ONE component: the
module went into a drawer literally named "Games\OpenUA\" at the root of
Personal: — present, and invisible unless you knew to look for a drawer with
backslashes in its name.

Nobody means a backslash in an Amiga path. The console installer now turns
each one into '/', strips a trailing separator, and prints the path it will
actually use before doing anything. Atari builds are untouched: there '\' IS
the separator and '/' is accepted too. The Workbench Install icon route never
types a path at all (askdir), so it was never exposed.

Test: a destination typed as "<tmp>\Games\OpenUA\" lands in <tmp>/Games/OpenUA,
no directory with a backslash in its name is created, and the final line names
the normalised path. The Curse disk set on the stick was rebuilt so its disk 1
carries this instdisk.

events.title: installer: fan-module disk sets that say what they are and where they went
events.message:
installer: fan-module disk sets that say what they are and where they went

A1200 report, 2026-09-05: the Curse of the Azure Bonds disk set "is using the
older one that is text based and I have no clue where it put the files". Both
halves were real.

WHERE IT WENT. The set was built as plain OpenUA-Data-N disks, so disk 1
carried the console installer (instdisk) and that is what got run. Its
default destination is DH0:OpenUA, taken on a bare RETURN — and CREATED if
absent, so on a machine whose real OpenUA drawer lives elsewhere the module
lands in a brand-new drawer on DH0: that looks empty. The destination was
printed once, at the top, before five disks of file names scrolled it away.
instdisk now ENDS with two lines that cannot be missed: the design's final
path ("The design Curse.dsn is now in <dest>/Curse.dsn - pick it with SELECT
A DESIGN"), and, when the destination had to be created, a NOTE saying so and
what to do about it. The design is taken from the FIRST manifest path only,
so a base-game set (root files first) never calls its bundled HEIRS a design.

THE OLDER ONE. mkdatadisks.sh grows MODULE=<Name>: volumes are labelled
<Name>-Data-N (instdisk matches disks by the DISK.LST header, never by volume
name, so nothing else changes — and the set can no longer be mistaken for the
base game's), the manifest is titled "<Name> module", and disk 1 carries a
Workbench Install icon like the engine disk's: IconX opens a console that
says this installs a module INTO an existing OpenUA drawer, then the OS
Installer asks the one question that matters — "Where is your OpenUA drawer?"
(default DH0:OpenUA, warns if there is no frua there) — copies the module into
it, and exits naming the destination. Workbench 3.1 has no Installer, so the
same icon falls back to instdisk, as the engine disk does.

instdisk also had no host test until now, and its first run under one was
KILLED mid-spin: the "insert an engine disk (s to skip)" prompt re-prompted
forever on a stdin that could never answer. EOF is now "s".
tests/test_instdisk.py pins the design line, the created-destination note as
the LAST thing printed, and the base-game control.

Rebuilt the Curse set with MODULE=Curse (Curse-Data-1..5, 5 disks, Install on
disk 1, disk 4 still carries the module's own MUSIC.SLB) and put it on the
Gotek stick with a README that matches; the instdisk on disk 1 is the one
built here.

events.title: 3d: the sky/floor flash was the PALETTE landing before the pixels (#20, the visible half)
events.message:
3d: the sky/floor flash was the PALETTE landing before the pixels (#20, the visible half)

The v0.9.22 fix memoised load_backdrop's 160 KB re-read (7 loads -> 2 on a
walk). It did not fix the report: the user still saw the flash on 0.9.23,
crossing outside <-> inside. Two reasons, and the second is the whole story:
a one-entry memo cannot help alternating between two zones, and the disk
read was never the VISIBLE part.

On a live-palette backend (AGA, TT: hw_palette) qd_set_palette lands in the
hardware CLUT immediately — aga_set_palette writes the copper words and "the
copper replays both every frame". So the instant load_backdrop installed the
NEW zone's band, the display, still showing the OLD backdrop's pixels,
rendered them through the new colours for the whole render until the
present. That is the flash: exactly the sky/floor region, one render long,
longer on a stock A1200. Same family as the ECS titles (#165), where the fix
was "planes and palette change together at the flip".

qd_set_palette_deferred: on a hw_palette backend the band is queued and
installed right after the backend present, so pixels and palette change
together; on quantiser and true-colour backends it installs immediately (the
ECS cut needs the palette before it runs). The clean-present skip will not
swallow a pending band. Only load_backdrop uses it — colour cycling and
every other palette write are untouched.

Proof in both directions, in amiberry, using the stretch-the-race trick from
FRUA_SLOWPRESENT: -DFRUA_BACKFLASH=40 holds the engine for 40 ticks right
after the band is queued, so what the display shows in that window can be
screenshotted. BEFORE: the sky pixels wearing the indoor band, held still
(frame f10). AFTER, the same sky -> indoor transition (zone 19 -> 8,
confirmed in DBG.LOG): no such frame — the sky keeps its own colours through
the hold and the indoor view appears whole. The probe stays under #ifdef.
Falcon (immediate arm) and TT (deferred arm) boot and walk in Hatari; all
four targets build; 557 host tests pass.

events.title: uaconv: build MUSIC.SLB for hand-copied installs too — root and each .DSN
events.message:
uaconv: build MUSIC.SLB for hand-copied installs too — root and each .DSN

The last gap in design-first music. uainst converts a module's music when it
installs from a ZIP (v0.9.23); a module — or a whole DOS install — copied by
hand had no path to a bank at all and played the base game's soundtrack, or
nothing. uaconv already walks the OpenUA drawer and every .DSN under it for
the art pass, so the music pass rides the same walk: per directory, classify
the .XMI present, prefer Tandy > PC > Roland > AdLib > DQK, build the bank
with the shared core (byte-identical to the Python by test) and write
<dir>/MUSIC.SLB.

★ AN EXISTING MUSIC.SLB IS NEVER OVERWRITTEN. The Mac release's root bank
holds EIGHT songs; a DOS conversion holds three. Replacing one with the other
would silently lose five songs on every Mac-sourced install that ran uaconv,
so the tool reports "already there, kept" and moves on. The root scan is also
non-recursive, so a module's soundtrack cannot become the base game's — the
same trap stage_dos needed --skip-designs for.

uaconv had NO TESTS before this, despite its header calling the convert path
host-testable. tests/test_uaconv.py builds it with the host compiler and pins
six behaviours: the art pass still converts a .tlb (touched, so pinned), root
and design banks match the reference byte for byte, design music does not
leak into the root, an existing bank is kept byte for byte, driver preference
and the Q1..Q3 filter, and the no-XMI control (no bank, no "music:" line).

Verified ON AN EMULATED A1200 against an isolated tree (never the real
drawer — -d deletes .tlb originals after converting): the Amiga uaconv wrote
a root bank from TYDQ1..3 that is byte-identical to the host build AND to the
MUSIC.SLB stage_dos stages from the same files (5024 bytes, Tandy 3 of 3),
and a design bank from curse's Dqk*.xmi identical to the host (4878 bytes,
DQK 2 of 3, reported partial). The drawer README's uaconv line now says so.

events.title: installer: a module's music now converts ON THE MACHINE — xmi2slb ported to C
events.message:
installer: a module's music now converts ON THE MACHINE — xmi2slb ported to C

Yesterday's design-first MUSIC.SLB work left one gap it named itself: the
XMI -> SLB conversion was host-side Python, so a module installed by uainst on
the Amiga or Atari still played the BASE game's soundtrack — working audio,
wrong music. This is the port.

src/convert/xmi2slb.c mirrors tools/xmi2slb.py the way artconv.c mirrors
art_convert.py: the Python stays the byte-exact REFERENCE, and
tests/test_xmi2slb_c.py holds the C to IDENTICAL bytes — ten synthetic files
chosen for the tie rules a "close enough" port gets wrong (two notes on one
tick, channel-count ties broken by FIRST APPEARANCE, more than three channels,
percussion on 9, rest gaps, a note long enough to need tied grid codes, a
non-default tempo, a half-even period), full and partial sets, plus every
module in the corpus and the retail Tandy set. 30 checks, all identical. The
one 64-bit operation (tempo -> period) is done as an exact rational with
half-to-even rounding so it cannot disagree with Python's float by a unit.

uainst runs a third pass over the ZIP listing: classify every .XMI (the
retail ??DQ<n> naming, and the fan modules' dqkQ<n> / Dqk<n> shapes), prefer
Tandy > PC > Roland > AdLib > DQK, read Q1..Q3 from the design folder, build
the bank into <design>/MUSIC.SLB with the arena it already has for art. A
partial set converts what exists and says so on the console.

★ THE FIRST CUT FAILED ON THE TWO ROLAND MODULES, and the failure was worth
having: a fixed quarter-arena note cap read 4096 on a 68000 but 2730 on a
host with 8-byte longs, and alliance/wiz1pc carry 3591 note-ons. The 68000
build would have scraped through by luck. The arena is now carved
adaptively (notes up to half, the per-channel copy sized from the busiest
channel after parsing), and a new test proves a too-small arena fails with
ERR_SPACE rather than writing a truncated bank that looks valid.

Verified ON AN EMULATED A1200, not just on the host: the Amiga uainst,
handed a module carrying curse's eight Dqk*.xmi, printed
    music: DQK arrangement, 2 of 3 songs... MUSIC.SLB (4878 bytes)
and the file it wrote is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the host-built bank for the same
inputs. Both cross installers build (uainst_amiga 96480, UAINST.PRG 190472);
the Atari binary is built but not run — its remaining variable is TOS file
I/O, which the art pass already exercises. 551 host tests pass.

Not done here: uaconv's per-design pass (for a module copied by hand rather
than installed), and curse's six extra songs beyond Q1..Q3.

events.title: 3d: cache the backdrop — the sky/floor no longer re-reads 160 KB per change (#20)
events.message:
3d: cache the backdrop — the sky/floor no longer re-reads 160 KB per change (#20)

A1200 report (fast Vampire, so not a CPU problem): "a flash of an unload/load
of textures as it needs to redraw the sky/floor", worse on a stock AGA machine.

load_backdrop opens BACK.CTL, NewPtr's 160 KB, reads 160 KB and frees it —
every call — to extract ONE 88x88 image and a 32-entry palette. That whole-file
read is the flash. It is the same bug the WALL loader already had fixed (the
2026-07-13 "GLIB pool flip", which stopped cw_load_slot pulling a whole ~296 KB
library to copy a few pieces out); load_backdrop was simply never given the
same treatment.

Measured on an AGA walk in amiberry, HEIRS from the SAVGAMB fixture, 10 steps
plus 3 turn-and-steps: 7 loads for 2 DISTINCT ids. Five of seven re-read the
file to rebuild a byte-identical result. Memoising the id takes the same drive
to 2 real loads and 5 cache hits.

★ THE PALETTE RE-INSTALL HAD TO SURVIVE. The wall-reload path deliberately
calls load_backdrop(g_back_set) with an UNCHANGED id, to re-lay the backdrop
band after an event picture wiped the CLUT — so an early return on an id match
would have traded this flash for wrong colours. The cache skips the DISK READ
and keeps the install, replaying it from `bpal`, which was already a static.

Verified by re-running the identical drive and diffing the frames: the only
difference is a text line in the MESSAGE PANE at (440,372)-(469,386), which is
run-to-run variance in the log. The 3D view, the backdrop and the chrome are
pixel-identical, and the entry path exercises the clut-clobbered re-install.

A negative worth recording so it is not re-tested: the first suspect was
g_clut_clobbered forcing load_wall_groups + load_backdrop + a chrome repaint
per step. It does not — instrumented with FRUA_BAR28, it fires ONCE at entry
and never during the walk (confirmed the party actually moved: cell 13,8, view
rendered, frames differ).

New FRUA_BACKPROF reports each load's id and tick cost plus cache hits; it is
pure output, so it stays.

HALF THE PROBLEM REMAINS: a FIRST visit to a zone still reads 160 KB, so a
first-time flash is still possible on slow media. Narrowing that to the
sub-GLIB the way cw_setglib_load does for walls is the next step.

events.title: music: a design's own soundtrack now converts and plays (ADR-0011 for MUSIC.SLB)
events.message:
music: a design's own soundtrack now converts and plays (ADR-0011 for MUSIC.SLB)

A fan module ships its own music and the port threw it away, in three separate
places. Measured against the module corpus (5 of 11 modules carry XMI):

1. THE ENGINE COULD NEVER FIND IT. jt986 built the bare literal "music.slb",
   so the bank could only ever resolve in the install root — the same omission
   ua_open_art fixed for whole-file art reads, and this is the same fix:
   design-first, root-fallback. It matters because a DOS module keeps its .XMI
   INSIDE <design>.DSN (curse does exactly that), so without this the module
   played the BASE GAME's music, which looks like working audio and is the
   wrong soundtrack. A design shipping no bank falls straight through to the
   root and loads the identical bytes, so unmodified designs are unchanged.

2. THE CONVERTER'S FILENAME MATCH REJECTED REAL MODULES. It required exactly
   `??DQ?.XMI` (9 chars), which missed:
     curse  Dqk1.xmi..Dqk9.xmi   8 chars, no driver pair -> 8 songs, converted
                                 to NOTHING
     g39    RODQ1.XMI only       a PARTIAL set; requiring all of Q1..Q3 threw
                                 away the one song the module has
   Now the DQK family (bare and Q-numbered) is recognised and a partial set
   converts what exists, the rest becoming empty songs exactly as the Mac-only
   slots 2..6 already are, so jt985's range check still passes. All five
   modules with music now convert; before, two did not.

events.title: ecs: the backend state dump — the CPU side of #19 is CLEAN, end to end
events.message:
ecs: the backend state dump — the CPU side of #19 is CLEAN, end to end

-DFRUA_ECSDUMP writes PROGDIR:ECSDMPnn.BIN at the end of each present and
tools/ecsdump.py reads it. Everything lands in GAME coordinates, so the
comparison needs no alignment — which is the entire point, after three
alignment methods disagreed (dx 21/28/22, dy 10/23/12) and made every earlier
"N% of pixels differ" figure worthless.

The dump carries BOTH ENDS of the quantiser plus the screen itself: clut and
chunky (the input, i.e. exactly what AGA displays), band_pal and band_remap
(the 32-colour cut), and the front bitplanes with s_front (what display DMA
actually fetches).

Forgotten Realms title, ECSDMP05 — 130 distinct indices, which is exactly what
artview --compose 1,4 reports, so it is provably the same screen:

  chunky vs SSI's art    1 of 64000 pixels differ, by d=6
  cut    vs chunky       5 of 64000 exceed d=120, at x=154..158 y=61,
                         mid-screen highlights, not a left edge
  planes vs cut          0 of 64000
  (earlier) copper words vs band_pal   800/800 agree

AND THE SCREEN STILL SHOWS THE DASHES — same run, same frame. So every value
the CPU computes is right and the corruption appears at DISPLAY time, which no
memory dump can see. That puts #19 in the #167 copper-timing family and
excludes a seventh cause: the cut, end to end.

Two traps handled rather than shipped:

  * The planes hold SLOTS (0..31), not chunky indices (0..255). Comparing
    against the index reported 99.4-99.97% of every frame as broken — a
    spectacular-looking result that was purely my own error. The first version
    of the test encoded the same mistake, so it passed. Both are fixed and
    there is now a named regression test for it.
  * The zeros are not vacuous: the plane checker prints its denominator, a
    round-trip test pins the decoder, and an injected 6-pixel stale run is
    caught and grouped. A "0 mismatches" from a checker that never ran has
    cost this project several rounds already.

Also recorded in TODO 19: do NOT try to measure the artefact rows from a
screenshot. Tried again, failed again — the capture is scaled, the detector
locks onto the border edge at x 7..13, and the row-mod-8 histogram comes back
uniform (12 across all eight residues), which is noise that would read as a
finding if taken at face value.

events.title: ci: Pillow was never in requirements.txt, so the compose test failed on CI only
events.message:
ci: Pillow was never in requirements.txt, so the compose test failed on CI only

The last two pushes emailed a red build. Cause is mine, not the audio work:
tests/test_artview.py's compose check actually RENDERS, so it imports Pillow —
which was present in the local tools/.venv and absent from tools/requirements.txt,
the only thing CI installs. The test therefore passed here and raised
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL' there, every time.

Reproduced CI exactly in a throwaway venv built from requirements.txt alone,
and confirmed the fix is causal rather than incidental: with Pillow the test
RUNS and passes (not skips); uninstall Pillow in that same venv and it fails
again; reinstall and it passes.

The module docstring claimed "PIL is only imported inside artview.render_entry,
so none of this needs it". That was true when written and stopped being true
the moment the compose test was added — the sort of stale comment that sends
the next reader looking in the wrong place, so it now says which test needs
Pillow and why.

Note the other CI skips are NOT this bug: CI reports ~70 skipped against 6 here
because the copyrighted data/ corpus is git-ignored and cannot exist on a
runner. Those tests are correctly skipped there, not silently broken.

events.title: amiga: AHI backend with a Paula fallback, and centre the Paula mix (ADR-0021)
events.message:
amiga: AHI backend with a Paula fallback, and centre the Paula mix (ADR-0021)

Paula hard-pans its channels — 0/3 left, 1/2 right — and the port drove only
AUD0, so the whole engine mix left the machine in the LEFT speaker. Found on
real hardware (A1200 + Apollo V4 IceDrake through a capture card): L-R =
+18.1 dB, reproduced to a tenth of a dB by two independent capture paths, so
the imbalance was the port and not the capture.

  * Paula now plays the ring on AUD0 AND AUD1, started by ONE dmacon write
    with identical LC/LEN/PER — mono centred, which is the faithful rendering
    of a mono source. A separate enable would leave up to a full ring (160 ms)
    of offset and sound like an echo rather than a centre image.
  * plat_sound_init prefers ahi.device and falls back to Paula when it is
    absent or will not open. On an Apollo/Vampire the AHI driver reaches the
    SAGA audio core ("Arne"), which has no published register map, so AHI is
    the only route to it — and it is portable anyway.
  * The general mix path ducks instead of clamping: voices give up 6 dB while
    something rides on top. A deliberate divergence from the Mac, commented so
    it is a one-line revert.
  * devices/ahi.h vendored at third_party/ahi/ (AHI developer archive, Martin
    Blom; the Bebbo toolchain ships no AHI headers).

BOTH PATHS NOW PRODUCE CENTRED AUDIO, which makes the hardware test ambiguous
by construction: "the sound is centred" would confirm nothing about AHI, since
the fixed Paula path does the same. So plat_sound_init says which backend it
took —

    snd: AHI backend up (ahi.device)
    snd: no AHI - Paula fallback (AUD0+AUD1 centred)

Verified in amiberry (no ahi.device on the mount, so this exercises the
fallback, which is the case that could have hung): boots to the menu, logs the
Paula line, 947 020-only instructions in the release binary under
-m m68k:68020 (0 without the flag — the documented objdump trap). 493 tests
pass. The AHI path itself still has never executed anywhere.

events.title: ecs: the copper agrees with the cut — sixth cause excluded for #19
events.message:
ecs: the copper agrees with the cut — sixth cause excluded for #19

ecs_cop_verify re-derives every copper COLOR word from s_band_pal in the 4-bit
encoding and compares it against the word the copper actually reads, at the end
of every present. 800 words (25 bands x 32 slots), 0 mismatched, twice.

The probe reports its CHECKED COUNT next to the mismatch count on purpose, so a
zero cannot be mistaken for 'never ran'. That specific confusion has produced
false passes here repeatedly — a missing objdump, a missing binary, a converter
pointed at a missing file — and it produced one earlier in this same
investigation.

artview gains --compose: a title screen on screen is a BASE plus an OVERLAY,
because l19d4 loads the library twice, so a reference built from the base alone
reports the entire overlay as a difference and reads as corruption. The palette
accumulates across entries, matching the engine's successive installs.

Six causes are now excluded for #19: draw-time planar writers, both palette
caches, stale previous-screen content, the remap, SSI's art, and the copper
words. Recorded honestly: the per-pixel screenshot-to-art comparison was NOT
achieved — three alignment methods disagreed (dx 21/28/22, dy 10/23/12), so no
percentage from it is trustworthy and none is quoted.

Next step removes the screenshot from the loop: dump the backend's own chunky
surface, band palettes and remaps at the end of a title render and compare
offline against artview --compose, both sides in game coordinates.

events.title: tools: artview.py renders the art offline — and it says the art is CLEAN
events.message:
tools: artview.py renders the art offline — and it says the art is CLEAN

Built to settle one question the emulator cannot: when a screen looks wrong on
a 16/32-colour machine, is the mark in SSI's data or did the port put it there?
Everything a screenshot shows has already been through the quantiser.

artview reuses perband's proven decoders rather than reimplementing the codecs,
extending them to keep the pixel POSITIONS the colour-counting versions throw
away: PackBits, transparency-RLE (0 ends the row, >=128 skips 257-b, index 0
transparent), raw 8bpp, mode-9 composites placed by dx/dy, and the jt993
palette-window law. Mono pieces are skipped, not guessed — there is no pen
offline. --info prints the container tree, --item/--all render.

Verdict on #19: TITLE.TLB entry 1 — the 320x200 base carrying the granite
frame and the red gradient the marks sit in — renders smooth and clean at 256
colours. The left-edge marks are NOT in the art. That kills candidate (b) and
leaves the ECS palette path.

Also corrects an error in the #19 notes: 'TITLE.TLB gives 2 items' was me
misreading the API. prequant.parse_glib returns a (count, offsets) TUPLE, not
a list of items; the container has 7 entries, and each title screen is base
entry 1 composited with its own overlay — which is exactly l19d4's two loads.

Nine tests, mutation-checked: 3 of 4 mutations were caught first time, and the
one that survived (flipping the row sign) was a real gap — every fixture was a
single row, so r was always 0. Added a 3-row piece; the mutation now fails.

events.title: ecs: characterise the left-edge corruption and rule out four causes (#19)
events.message:
ecs: characterise the left-edge corruption and rule out four causes (#19)

Not fixed. Recording what it is and what it is not, so the next attempt does
not re-derive any of it.

What it is, measured on the Forgotten Realms title in amiberry at exact pixels:
thin HORIZONTAL runs of beige/white/orange, 3-60 px long, at the left of the
picture, inside smooth dark-red gradient that should hold no such colour. The
same screen on AGA is clean — same engine, same chunky surface — so the fault
is in the ECS conversion, not the drawing.

Ruled out, each by a one-variable A/B:

  - draw-time planar writers: PLANAR=0 renders the frame PIXEL-IDENTICAL
    (5c5c4e5d both ways), so this is upstream of plane writing
  - both palette caches: clutcache=off palcache=off + deleted PALCACHE.ECS,
    identical hashes
  - stale previous-screen content: 3% of candidate pixels match the preceding
    screen, and those are border pixels identical between screens anyway;
    shifted-lookup control 0%
  - a catastrophic remap: the new FRUA_ECSERR probe reports the worst
    used-colour-to-slot distance per band; worst is grey -> slightly lighter
    grey (idx 19 #838387 -> #a8a8a8), never red -> beige

Adds FRUA_ECSERR (worst per-band remap error, with the wanted and assigned
RGB) and notes an exact-pixel AGA config for matched-geometry comparison —
the stock openua.uae blends and drowns the artefact in a naive diff.

Two candidates remain: the copper palette install for non-boundary rows, or
the marks being in SSI's art with AGA's 256 colours hiding what a 32-colour
cut exposes. The latter is offline and cheap and should be tried first; it
needs a real art renderer, since TITLE.TLB does not decode with perband's
piece decoders.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass.

events.title: ecs: present again after the palette lands — the SSI logo now displays (#18)
events.message:
ecs: present again after the palette lands — the SSI logo now displays (#18)

A500 report: 'the SSI / Micromagic logo screen no longer even displays... it's
there on the AGA version.' That split was the clue — same engine code, same
art, one works.

The title's palette is installed AFTER the present that shows it:

    tsq:   jt117 SHOW, mode = 2
    ecsp:  present, dirty=0                 converts under the OLD palette
    ecsp:  set_palette first=16 count=240   the title's palette, after

On a hardware-palette screen that is harmless — the pixels are already placed
and the late CLUT write recolours them, which is why AGA was always fine. On a
quantiser the pixels were converted through the previous palette and no later
write can fix them; at boot that previous palette is the black startup one, so
the screen renders black and the title never appears. It also explains why THIS
screen was missing while later ones merely looked wrong: each title was being
shown in its predecessor's colours.

Quantisers now take one more present after the palette bracket closes, so the
cut runs against the complete CLUT. The backend already declines the premature
present, which is #16's defer doing useful work. HW-palette backends keep the
Mac's single present.

ecs_set_palette also marks the bands dirty for ANY palette write while a
composition bracket is open, not just count >= 32. Size is the wrong test
there: a title whose art declares fewer than 32 colours was filed as colour
cycling and never re-cut.

★ This also corrects a FALSE POSITIVE in #16. As first written, the cut-defer
swallowed jt117 — the one present each title gets, since the composition holds
the rest — so the sentinel counts read 0 because no cut happened, not because
the cut was clean, while the whole title sequence rendered black (60/60 frames)
and the metric said 'fixed'. A metric can go quiet because the work stopped.
The re-verification now requires the titles to actually render as well.

Verified: the SSI/MicroMagic screen renders on ECS and matches the AGA
reference; 4 titles composed -> 4 renders (1:1, was 0); sentinel pixels and
magenta band slots both still 0. All four targets build; 483 tests pass.

Adds FRUA_TITLESEQ (per-title compose/show/art-load tracing and ECS
present/render branch decisions), which is what made this measurable.

events.title: zynaps atari: in-game controls — ESC to the menu, F10 to TOS
events.message:
zynaps atari: in-game controls — ESC to the menu, F10 to TOS

Two deliberate divergences, shim-only, always-on (not cheat-gated), the
differential untouched (make test 4751).
- ESC (0x01) while PHASE_PLAYING -> the main menu, re-using the game's OWN
  back-to-front-end path (frame_loop_once returning FRAME_EXIT_TITLE, the
  all-lives-lost exit). Round trip proven twice in Hatari.
- F10 (0x44) -> TOS, re-using the shim's teardown (restore vectors/PSG/
  rez/palette/base with read-backs, then Pterm). CLEAN in a level; at the
  pure attract screen the main line is parked inside the verified
  attract_wait_for_start, which has no shim checkpoint, so the F10 flag
  latches and fires once a game starts (documented, not a flaky unwind).
- Mechanism: a second unconditional door tap zy_note_control_key beside
  the trainer's; in the ACIA interrupt it only SETS volatile flags, acted
  on the main line in play_one_game after frame_loop_once returns (never
  unwind from the interrupt). Census: no cmpi.b #$01/#$44 anywhere in the
  program — collision-free with SPACE/1/2.

Review caught a real latch leak: g_phase lingers at PLAYING through
boot_front_end_prologue between games, so an ESC auto-repeat edge would
bounce the next game after one frame — fixed by clearing g_quit_to_menu on
play_one_game entry, with a deterministic regression (poke the latch at
attract, start game 2, assert esc_to_menu does not rise) that reddens with
the clear removed.

smoke.py controls: the ESC round trip and the F10 exit proven; every
judged mode asserts esc_to_menu==0 and f10_to_tos==0; mutations 3/3 red.
Matrix green; pacing 2.54 unchanged; ZY_NOCHEATS green. Docs: atari and
recreate READMEs' "In-game controls", root README's divergence paragraph.

events.title: zynaps trainer: audible feedback — a per-key blip and a louder arm fanfare
events.message:
zynaps trainer: audible feedback — a per-key blip and a louder arm fanfare

The typed sequence works on iron, but the arm sound was inaudible: stream
35 opens `fa 03 e8 01 e9 01 ea 01` — all three tone periods = 1, a
near-ultrasonic whistle (−10.7 dBFS on a meter, thin to the ear). Measured
from out/audio/manifest.tsv.

- Arm fanfare 35 -> 23 (CHEAT_SFX_ARMED 0x23 -> 0x17): stream 23 opens
  `fa 03 e8 11 ...`, an audible mid pitch, −10.8 dBFS, 2.0 s — also `fa 03`
  and also an orphan the shipped game never plays, so the resurrected-cut-
  content spirit holds.
- Per-key blip: CHEAT_SFX_KEY 0x1d (stream 29, 0.90 s) plays on each
  ACCEPTED, non-completing letter (Z, Y — and a fresh Z that restarts),
  so the sequence is heard landing key by key; the completing N gives the
  fanfare, not a blip.
- The split honors the interrupt rule: the ACIA door raises g_blip_pending
  (a byte, like g_seq_complete); zy_cheats_tick drains it in the VBL as an
  `else if` to the arm branch, so a blip and the fanfare never sound in one
  tick and sound_start is never called from the keyboard interrupt.

Smoke: cheats reports "1 fanfare on stream 0x177a4 (= stream 23's head),
7 blips"; an independent blip-count replay and STREAM-ID PINS
(CHEAT_ARM_STREAM=23 / CHEAT_BLIP_STREAM=29) — the self-referential
fanfare read-back would stay green if the id reverted to 35, so the pin is
what catches it. Negatives (Z,Y,Z,N and Z,Y) refuse and leave no fanfare.
key_blips added to the record, 0 asserted in every judged mode (dormancy).
Mutations 4/4 red. make test 4751 unchanged; matrix green; pacing 2.53;
ZY_NOCHEATS green. README "Four sounds" -> "Five sounds".

rows/columns can ghost on the IKBD's undiode-isolated matrix and never all

resets (to 1 if it is Z, else 0, so a fumble then a clean Z-Y-N still
arms); breaks and joystick bytes are ignored as before. The VBL tick arms
on the latch with the window open (jingle sfx 35 + g_armed + the pokes),

events.title: ecs: defer the CUT while the palette is still arriving (#16 titles)
events.message:
ecs: defer the CUT while the palette is still arriving (#16 titles)

The A500 title corruption: the art is cut against a CLUT still holding the
art's magenta defer sentinel, so the quantiser spends 10 of every band's 32
slots on a placeholder — a fifth of the budget, which is why the screen reads
as 'colours all inverted' rather than merely speckled.

The engine already marks the window. l19d4 brackets each title's composition in
qd_palette_blackout(), and a hardware-palette backend answers by pushing black
so the half-built screen is never seen. That call RETURNED BEFORE TOUCHING ITS
COUNTER on any other backend, so a quantiser could not ask the one question the
bracket answers.

Keep the counter for every backend (only the black push is hardware-specific)
and publish it as dsp_palette_incomplete(). The state lives in
platform/planar.c — shared by the Atari and Amiga builds, since neither
backend file is linked by the other — and the shim sets it, so the layer rule
holds: compat calls down into platform, never up.

ECS then defers its cut across the bracket, keeping the last complete frame on
screen; the engine's own install at the end of the bracket sets s_dirty and
that present cuts against a whole CLUT. A quantiser cannot blackout instead —
its planes hold slots, not indices — and its problem is worse than a visible
flash: a cut taken mid-bracket is BAKED IN and no later palette write undoes
it.

Measured on the same fixture and instrumentation as the root-cause run:
chunky pixels on sentinel slots 975 -> 0, band-palette magenta slots 10 -> 0,
at every cut. The defer fires for 4 presents.

Bounded at 24 presents, because #8 is what an unbounded wait costs; the bound
is on presents, not wall-clock, so it does not vary with machine speed. An
overrun loses the title, not the game. video.cfg titledefer=off is the A/B arm.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass. Emulator-measured.

events.title: installer: put something useful in the Amiga install console
events.message:
installer: put something useful in the Amiga install console

A1200 field report (2026-09-03), after verifying the AGA installer works: 'the
extra window that pops up with the installer version in it could be used for
the Unlimited Adventures screen, or maybe some of the readme information /
license and required files list'.

That window is ours — IconX opens it from the WINDOW= tooltype on Install.info
— and when the AmigaOS Installer is present the launcher left it empty behind
the Installer's GUI. Now it prints what a first-time installer actually needs
while that GUI is up: what this is and its version, what you need before
starting (engine disk, your data disks, ~7 MB free, and the measured Kickstart
minimum for the variant), what the installer is about to ask, and that RETURN
takes every default.

It also states the thing that matters legally and is easy to get wrong: the
ENGINE is GPL-2.0 with a source pointer, and the GAME DATA is not included and
not ours to give — the data disks come from the user's own copy of FRUA.

Costs nothing at run time and adds no files to a full floppy.

AmigaDOS specifics, both of which bite silently: '*' is the ESCAPE character in
a quoted string, so the bullets are '-' (verified 0 asterisks in the generated
script); and the window is CON:0/20/640/180, which topaz 8 fills at 80x22, so
the banner is kept to 63 columns and 19 lines. Verified by reading Install back
out of BOTH built ADFs, with the ECS variant correctly getting 'Kickstart 2.0
or later (ECS/OCS; 1.3 will NOT work)'. The engine binary is byte-identical
after the rebuild.

events.title: docs: ECS walk shimmer does not reproduce in the emulator — hardware arbitrates
events.message:
docs: ECS walk shimmer does not reproduce in the emulator — hardware arbitrates

Two deliberate attempts, both 1 distinct frame while stationary (24 frames from
arrival, 30 after walking and turning), with adoptions logged in both. The
capture method resolved multiple frames on other screens the same day, so the
negative is trustworthy.

Records the code-level suspicion that survives it — a cache hit restores band
palettes cut before the ink existed, dropping an adoption that the next present
re-applies — and why that loop is benign here. The decisive test is
inkadopt=off on real hardware; the adopter must not be rewritten on speculation
because it fixes a measured bug.

events.title: zynaps atari: the trainer — hold Z+Y+N at the title; F1/F2/F3 cheats
events.message:
zynaps atari: the trainer — hold Z+Y+N at the title; F1/F2/F3 cheats

A deliberate, documented divergence, implemented ENTIRELY IN THE SHIM as
key-triggered pokes of bytes the game already honors (atari/zynaps_cheats.c
+ .h; no src/ include/ test/ file moved; the differential untouched at
4751 and the frame differential still ZERO bytes).

- ARM: hold Z+Y+N for ~2 s (100 VBLs) on the title/attract screen only —
  the window brackets attract_wait_for_start, releasing a key resets, the
  combo is refused in-game. Letters resolved AT RUNTIME from the game's
  own scancode->ASCII table @0x19a39 (a pure QWERTY map, no layout switch
  in the image), plus the AZERTY position for Z (0x11) so the user's
  French STE arms on the keys LABELED Z+Y+N; documented cost: W+Y+N also
  arms on QWERTY.
- F1 toggles the DORMANT invulnerability flag 0x19912 (the secrets hunt's
  find — three death-site reads, no writer in the shipped image);
  F2 lives -> 9 + the panel bit; F3 the five power-up commit arms at the
  game's own ceilings (power 4, shield 3 + HUD mirror, seeker, speed 1,
  timers, panel bits).
- FOUR ORPHANED SOUND EFFECTS RESURRECTED as feedback (35 = the arm
  fanfare with the fa 03 channel code no reachable stream uses; 19 / 37 /
  38 for F1/F2/F3), started through the verified sound_start.
- Inert by default and PROVEN so: every judged smoke mode asserts
  cheats_armed == 0 and zero fires (with the M1-modes' vacuousness stated,
  not hidden); smoke.py cheats is the positive control — arming + the
  fanfare stream on the PSG trace, six poked bytes read off the machine,
  and invulnerability AS BEHAVIOUR (survives to frame 400 where the
  control life ends at ~176; F1 again and the same ship dies at 464) —
  plus the wrong-key and in-game negatives. ZY_NOCHEATS=1 builds and
  smokes green with the ELF asked whether the watcher is in it.
- Pacing cost measured: ~800 cycles/frame = 0.2% (2.52 -> 2.53/2.54,
  ceiling 2.64). Mutations 4/4 killed (wrong-key reset, in-game refusal,
  a fire-count assertion, the dormancy gate).
- Review: the tap had been #ifdef'd inside a header every verified core
  includes (a core compiling differently between builds, invisible to the
  containment gate) — now unconditional, the purist build links an empty
  body; a tautological timer read-back deleted (the three timers honestly
  unpinned on target); a latent interrupt-context out-of-bounds fixed
  (g_fires sized by the wrong constant).

ecs: root-cause the title corruption — the quantiser bakes in the defer sentinel

Instrumented on a full ECS boot: 975 chunky pixels reference CLUT entries still
holding the magenta (255,0,255) unused/defer sentinel, and the cut then spends
10 of every band's 32 slots on it. qd_palette_blackout hides exactly this on a
hardware-palette backend and is a documented no-op on quantisers, so ECS never
had the fix. A fifth of the palette budget going to a placeholder is why the
screen reads as inverted rather than speckled.

Adds the FRUA_ECSTITLE probes (sentinel CLUT entries, sentinel pixels, magenta
band slots, repalette representatives) that measured it, and records that short
boots do not reach the affected title — the first three renders all read zero.

events.title: zynaps atari: the 1 MB diet — 597,470 B against a measured 908,138 budget
events.message:
zynaps atari: the 1 MB diet — 597,470 B against a measured 908,138 budget

The target image shrinks to ZY_TARGET_IMAGE_BYTES = 0x80000 (the kit's
1 MiB OS_IMAGE_SIZE untouched off target). The census that warrants it:
the game shipped for a 512 KB ST and its hard-coded framebuffers end at
0x7fd00, 768 B under that machine's RAM top; program ends 0x6e96e with no
Malloc in the text; all 472 A_* addresses — 315 header #defines AND 157
.equs in the linked asm twins — are below 0x80000; no literal in the
shipped code falls in [0x80000, 0x100000); the upper half was harness-only.
Computed addresses get two WATCHED BANDS (the review caught the first
attempt's blind spot — a single band at 0x80000 sat 768 B above the
world's top): the tail [0x7fd00, 0x80000) checked zero and a 0xa5 guard
[0x80000, 0x81000), both clean after a 300-frame game run.

Budget MEASURED from GEMDOS's own basepage at --memsize 1 (TOS 1.04):
TPA 940,906 (floppy boot is cheaper, the GEMDOS figure is conservative);

events.title: ecs: give new ink a FREE SLOT instead of the nearest wrong one
events.message:
ecs: give new ink a FREE SLOT instead of the nearest wrong one

Reported while verifying #166: on ECS an event's first text line renders bright
cyan and the following lines render dim grey, near-illegible against the box.

Measured on the HEIRS innkeeper event (amiberry, ECS/68000): line 1 ink
#00bbbb, lines 2 and 3 #888888 against a #555544 box. The split is not
temporal, it is SPATIAL and lands exactly on a copper band boundary — line 1
sits in band 13, lines 2-3 in bands 14-15.

Cause: the per-band cut is computed from the surface as it stood, and drawing
text never marks it dirty, so anything drawn afterwards resolves through
remap_rect's absent-colour bucket — the nearest slot the band happens to own.
Band 13 owns a cyan slot only because the event PICTURE is cyan there. Bands
14-15 sit below the picture, never saw a cyan pixel, and resolve the same
glyphs to grey.

The existing remedy was explicitly a placeholder: ecs_ink_hold skips ONE
present in case a palette install is following, and its own comment says that
failing that the ink "paints on the NEXT present via the bucket fallback
exactly as before". The bucket fallback is the grey glyph.

★ And the band had room the whole time. Instrumenting the text-box bands says
they use 7 to 11 of their 32 slots — 21+ empty — while the glyph is forced onto
a slot 3675 away. So nothing needs re-quantising and nothing needs sacrificing:
hand the colour an EMPTY slot, fix the remap, and patch that slot's copper
word.

Writing a FREE slot's COLOR word is safe in a way a palette install is not
(#165): free means no used index maps to it, so no pixel on screen wears that
slot and changing its RGB cannot recolour the outgoing frame. Under
FRUA_PLANAR the band's draw-time coverage is dropped and its rows re-announced,
because rows a writer already stamped used the old remap for that index.

Per-band, because a colour absent here may be present one band down; and only
when the bucket is genuinely bad (ECS_INK_NEAR), so a glyph whose colour the
band already holds costs one distance test.

Result on the same event: all three lines now measure #00bbbb. The drive
adopts 6, 21, 3, 1, 1 slots at its re-band points.

Runtime knob video.cfg inkadopt=off restores the old behaviour for A/B.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass. ECS-only code — Falcon, TT, ST/STE and
AGA are untouched.

Not yet confirmed on hardware.

events.title: ste: $FF820D is a HARDWARE difference, and the write is harmless — fix the comment
events.message:
ste: $FF820D is a HARDWARE difference, and the write is harmless — fix the comment

The comment above st_flip_super claimed only the hi/mid video-base bytes were
written, and that leaving $820D out 'keeps this correct on a plain ST too (no
$820D there)'. The code three lines below writes $820D. One of the two was
wrong; it was the comment.

Which one to fix needed measuring, on the configuration where it matters: a
plain ST with TOS 2.06 and an accelerator (Hatari --machine st --cpulevel 3
--cpuclock 32).

  - the write reaches the bus: 12 writes to ffff820d during boot, against 13
    each to ffff8201/ffff8203, so it is not dead code;
  - it raises no bus error. A full drive (boot, load, dungeon walk) took six
    bus errors, every one from the TOS ROM probing hardware it might not have
    (ffff8900 STE DMA sound, ffff8a00 blitter), and none from frua.

That is evidence rather than absence-of-evidence, because Hatari does model
this fault class on an ST — those ROM probes are exactly it, faulting and being
caught. The ST decodes the $FF82xx block coarsely and swallows the write. It
is harmless by construction too: pages are 256-byte aligned so the low byte is
0 on every flip, which is both its power-on value and the only value a plain
ST's fixed low byte can hold.

And it is a HARDWARE difference, not a TOS one (Compendium B.20: $FF820C
'Video Base Address Low' is STE-and-later silicon). Fitting TOS 2.06 to an ST
does not add the register; TOS 1.04 in an STE does not remove it.

events.title: docs: the 020 build downgrades to ST graphics — run it on an accelerated ST
events.message:
docs: the 020 build downgrades to ST graphics — run it on an accelerated ST

The runtime backend choice was documented in one direction only (the 68000
build running on a Falcon/TT and picking their higher-colour path). It works
the other way too: dsp_detect reads the _VDO cookie, so the 020 Falcon/TT
binary detects ST hardware and downgrades itself to the same 16-colour ST-low
banded backend. The graphics follow the machine; only the CPU decides which
binary you can run.

That makes the Falcon/TT zip the right binary for an accelerated ST, which was
documented nowhere. Measured in the guest's own clock (FRUA_STEPPROF), one
dungeon step's render: stock ST 8MHz with the 68000 build = 155 ticks; ST with
an 030 at 32MHz running the 020 build = 9-13. Small sample, so the section
quotes the magnitude rather than the ratio.

Also records that no Hatari patch is needed to try it (--machine st --cpulevel
3 --cpuclock 32, with Hatari's own TOS 2.06/EmuTOS and 32MHz-max caveats), and
corrects a stale claim in the ST/STE entry: 'no version check in the code, so
earlier TOS may well work - nobody has tried' was wrong twice over.
plat_stram_alloc DOES gate Mxalloc on Sversion() and fall back to Malloc, and
TOS 1.04 has now been tried - a stock non-e ST boots and plays.

Stock-ST colour, measured rather than assumed: the STE 4-bit palette encoding
carries its extra bit in bit 3, so a plain ST reads a correct 3-bit
approximation for free - an ST frame uses only the even gun indices, the STE
frame uses the odd ones too. Costs colour count (15 distinct vs 23 in a walk
frame), not band seams: the mod-8 band-boundary test scores ST 5/20 and STE
4/20 against a chance baseline of ~2.5. It cannot get worse either, because
the collapse is deterministic - the 3-bit path can only merge colours, never
split them, and merging cannot create a seam.

events.title: input: one stamp per key — the accelerator beep is a DOUBLE DELIVERY (#11)
events.message:
input: one stamp per key — the accelerator beep is a DOUBLE DELIVERY (#11)

Reported from the Mega STe: [P]lay / [L]oad / [B]egin each WORK but beep every
time, "don't recall it doing that before".

The chime is jt1080, fired by L2d3e Phase 5's `else` arm when no DLItem claims
the key. That arm is faithful — the Mac beeps at a key nothing wants. What is
not faithful is that the port hands Phase 5 the SAME keystroke twice: the first
read claims the accelerator and opens a modal, the second finds no item with
that letter in the modal that just opened, and chimes. The beep was the engine
telling the truth about a key the port delivered twice.

Traced end to end on a Mega STe, one physical press:

  plat_kb_poll  = 9836      one poll
  kb_to_event   = 9836      one event
  l6dd0 STAMP   = 9836      stamp #1 -> jt1133 reads 'l' -> CLAIMED, opens Load
  jt1125 STAMP  = 108       stamp #2, no new poll and no new event
                            -> jt1133 reads 'l' -> UNCLAIMED -> jt1080

That also settles the open question in plat_kb_poll's own #132 comment, which
set out the discriminator and left it unanswered: two polls for one press would
be IKBD repeat or the test injector, one poll and two engine reads is ours. It
is one poll and two reads. The repo has been blaming the harness injector.

Cause is the TaskList #84 stash. l725c pops an event, pushes a copy to
g_evfifo so jt1125's consumers still see what the pump ate, AND routes it to
l6dd0 — which for a key stamps the pending slot (-818/-820). jt1125 later pops
the stashed copy and its port bridge stamps the same key again.

On the Mac the two paths cannot collide: jt1125 reads a separate IRQ-filled
buffer while L725c reads the Toolbox queue, so exactly one stamp lands per key
and jt1125 does not stamp at all. The bridge is a port addition for the single
shared queue, where whichever path reaches the event first consumes it. It was
right to add; it just has to know when the other path already ran.

Fix: jt1125 stamps only for an event it fetched ITSELF, not one popped from the
stash. That restores the Mac's one-stamp-per-key invariant. The event is still
RETURNED either way, so l2d3e Phase 1's movement routing is untouched — that
path reads the returned event, not the pending slot, and a walk drive confirms
it (party 10,8 -> 12,8, innkeeper event fires, text renders).

Measured A/B, same fixture, keys P L B, Mega STe under Hatari:

  HEAD   1 beep — 'p' stamped by l6dd0 then again by jt1125, second read
         unclaimed. Which key doubles is a race and moves run to run ('l' in
         an earlier run), which is consistent with a machine whose timing
         favours it beeping every time.
  fixed  0 beeps, one stamp and one read per key, all three claimed.

Falcon: 0 beeps after, and it never showed the letter double before — only the
shared Return case — which is why this read as Mega-STe-specific.

An unclaimed Return in the Hall still chimes. That is the faithful arm, not
this bug: nothing there has a Return shortcut.

Adds FRUA_BEEPTRACE (every beep source plus each Phase-5 key with its claim
result) and harmonises the FRUA_KEYDIAG caps to 400 across boot.c, events.c and
input.c — they were 60, and this bug is only visible by correlating stamps
ACROSS those layers, which a per-layer cap mismatch silently breaks.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass.

Not yet confirmed on the reporting hardware.
