events.title: engine: bound the event-tail hold by WORK, not wall-clock (#8)
events.message:
engine: bound the event-tail hold by WORK, not wall-clock (#8)

Reported from the Mega STe + ATW800/2: closing a picture event shows the pic
"unloading", draining out of the view square before the view redraws. The TODO
guessed this was a missing hold and proposed adding one. It is the opposite —
the hold has been there since #161 and has never once worked.

port_event_tail_expire bounded the hold at 30 ticks, reasoned as generous
against "a wipe and a repair inside one step render" and shipped with the note
that a slow machine exceeding it "simply gets the pre-#161 flash back".
Instrumenting the tail says every machine exceeds it, and not marginally:

  tail in        tick 14515
  tail out       tick 14549   jt23+jt935+jt937+jt938 = 34 ticks, 5 presents
  L63c0 release  tick 14569   90 presents swallowed

The honest window is 54-66 ticks over two events, nearly twice the bound, on a
Falcon030 in an emulator under fast-forward. So the expiry fired on every event
ever dispatched, and l63c0's release — the designed one, the one that discards
the intermediates and lands the tail as a single frame — never ran. On a fast
machine that costs a blink nobody noticed for a month. On a slow-present card
the expiry lands mid-tail and the rest of the teardown goes out one present at
a time, which is the reported drain.

Time cannot separate the two states this has to tell apart: "busy rebuilding
the frame" and "stuck, the engine has run on without me" both look like elapsed
ticks, and the legitimate case is already ~1s on the FASTEST target. That is
not a badly tuned constant, it is the wrong axis.

Presents swallowed is the right one, because it does not vary with machine
speed — the same code path issues the same presents at 7MHz and 50MHz, so one
cap holds on every target with no per-machine table. qd_hold_swallowed() counts
what the ref-counted hold ate (never the frame bracket, which has no engine
owner that can fail to release it); the honest window measures 71-92, so 512
clears the longest five-slot message several times over while a runaway, which
presents without bound because presenting is what it does, still trips it. The
wall-clock bound survives at 900 ticks as a last resort that is never expected
to fire.

Primary protection stays STRUCTURAL, which is what the two shipped freezes
taught: the walk-step gate in port_event_tail_hold, plus explicit drops
wherever the engine waits for the player. Added the one that defeated
enumeration twice — jt511's combat entry, the rider-and-ogres shape — so it is
caught there rather than hundreds of presents later by the net.

Measured A/B, same fixture, same key timing, HEIRS 13,8 tavern-brawl event:

  HEAD   444 bracket -> 9102 text -> 3895+3900 full -> 19759 step
         = 5 separate partial states presented
  fixed  3895+3900 = 2 presents, the two flip pages of ONE frame

At ~0.5s per present on the Nova card that is ~2.5s of visible teardown gone.

Also adds FRUA_SLOWPRESENT, the harness that made this reproducible at all.
Nothing we emulate is natively as slow as the ATW's VME writes, so bugs that
only appear at that cost cannot be found by running an emulator — the reason
this one needed a hardware report. -DFRUA_SLOWPRESENT=<ticks> burns that cost
per present and turns any machine into an ATW-class one for timing purposes;
at 30 it reproduces the drain on a Falcon. Diagnostic only, off by default.

Falcon/TT, ST/STE, Amiga AGA and Amiga ECS all build; 483 tests pass. Live
drive on the clean 020 build: the 13,8 picture event fires, pages, closes, and
the new view redraws with the command bar intact.

Not yet confirmed on the hardware that reported it — that is owed at the next
pass, along with the rest of 0.9.20.

events.title: kit: hardware-write ledger, $fffc00 ACIA slot, 32-slot file table
events.message:
kit: hardware-write ledger, $fffc00 ACIA slot, 32-slot file table

Harness (tools/recreate_kit, TRAP_MODEL.md "Phase 10"):
- Hardware-WRITE ledger on both sides: shim.c's write callbacks log every
  store into the three I/O blocks the ST decodes ($ff8000.., $fffa00..,
  $fffc00..) as (24-bit addr, width, value) where they used to drop; the
  candidate calls hw_write8/16/32 (off-target only, like psg.c);
  harness.differential compares the streams exactly — missing / extra /
  reordered / wrong-width / wrong-value all fail. Runaway pointers outside
  the blocks stay dropped (measured in Joust and BuggyBoy); an in-image or
  untranslated ($ffff8240) address at the door is a REFUSAL. Default ON;
  opt-out is hw_waiver={addr: reason}, recorded in harness.HW_WAIVERS and
  self-retiring (a candidate that touches a waived address fails).
- $fffc00 (IKBD ACIA status) as OS_HW_ACIA_STATUS, a STATIC seeded slot
  with the model's one default (TDRE set) — ikbd_send_cmd's spin exits on
  its first poll on both sides, and the read is ledgered instead of a
  hard-coded `return 2` in shim.c.
- OS_FS_SLOTS 8 -> 32 (#error-pinned below OS_FS_STAGING); the Zynaps boot
  measured at 22 load_file calls / 66,818 B against 258,048 B of staging.
- 28 new kit tests (426); tools/hw_portability.py un-broken (it had been
  sys.exit-ing on a deleted shim.c symbol); at-risk 24/3910 -> 23/3888.

Zynaps: ikbd_send_cmd @0x14444 verified in src/input.c (20 cases, all 256
command bytes sharded, 14/14 mutants killed). irq_hw_offtarget.c DELETED —
the shifter stores live in video.c/video.h and the MFP ack in irq.c, all
through hw_write*, so the six irq handlers, screen_flip_buffers,
set_palette_title and the boot slices have their off-image half PINNED.

left in "Not reconstructed" — the three KIT walls are gone; ikbd_acia_isr
now needs exactly one thing, a READ model for $fffc02 (a declared byte
sequence). Merged over 82b0870 by three-way row merge.

project's test/harness.py. One live risk recorded in BuggyBoy's STATUS:

  hand-back with every restore read back (class 7).

  coming names), psg as real $ff8800/$ff8802 stores from the VBL, real
  GEMDOS Fopen/Fread/Fclose, ikbd_send_cmd as the real ACIA spin+store,
  irq_hw_offtarget.c excluded and its three sinks supplied. Inventory table
  in atari/README.md.

  ledger 24 calls identical, 32000-byte framebuffer identical, 16 pens +
  $ff8260 + video base identical, PNG byte-identical, first 64 PSG tick
  frames identical, clean exit both sides. titlefault (one pen corrupted en
  route to the shifter) reddens pens + pixels only and the verdict inverts.

  bus-error scan blind to Hatari's "Bus Error" casing; ten record fields

events.title: zynaps audio: judge the dump against the real game; fix the YM renderer
events.message:
zynaps audio: judge the dump against the real game; fix the YM renderer

ref_capture.py records the title screen and level-1 play from Hatari (the
`recsound` shortcut over the cmd-fifo + a psg_write trace cut into frames by
the driver's own 10..0 flush); compare_audio.py replays the trace against
the dumps: 1000/1000 title-tune frames byte-identical, ten level-1 effects
located. The register capture was right; what was heard was the render:
- ym2149.py: 8x oversampling with interval mean (a period-0/1 tone is
  125 kHz on the chip and point-sampling folded it into band at full
  amplitude), a moving-mean high-pass (the machine's AC coupling — 20% of
  the title tune's energy sat below 50 Hz vs 8% in the recording), chip
  scale instead of per-file peak normalisation (normalise=True keeps
  BuggyBoy's old behaviour), lazy noise/envelope sources.
- extract_audio.py: continuation streams and voice parts are kind=part —
  .ym only, no misleading WAV (27 WAVs: 5 tunes, 22 effects); envelope-mode
  voices are silent on the real machine too (shape 0, written only by the
  reset) and that is now a check; peak_dbfs in the manifest.
Spectral agreement title tune 0.906 -> 0.978; 50 Hz confirmed (no $ff820a).

events.title: wonderboy: the cheat's level skip lands an unarmoured hero the round cannot draw — faithful
events.message:
wonderboy: the cheat's level skip lands an unarmoured hero the round cannot draw — faithful

Driven identically into the shipped binary and into ours (cheat typed,
N, round 2, 27 anchored frames): the hero is drawn as the UNMARKED
sentinel's bytes on BOTH sides — 0 of 270 artefacts differ, same rendered
frame. Why: WB_EFFECT_STATE_21E4 selects one of three posture records =
three sprite families (form 0 unarmoured 260-267, form 1 270-283, form 2
286-299); every route the game itself takes out of a round sets form 1
or 2 (the exit action at $101c6, the life restart at $c06, the three $bd68
effect handlers), and only the new-game reset ($fe56) clears it — so the
shipped mask carries forms 1 and 2 in every round and form 0 only where
a new game can be (unmarked in rounds 2, 3, 10, 11; 3 frames in 4). The
level skip sets no form. Control: poke $21e4 := 1 before the skip and
both sides draw sprite 270 correctly (135/135 identical).

Tests (test_boot.py, +3): the three posture records name three separate
families; every round installs both armoured forms; the five rounds and
their missing-frame counts for the unarmoured one. Mutation-swept 7/7
after a literal walk-frame count was derived from the record geometry.

The play pictures were booted straight into boot_load_stage, skipping the
title and credits slices — but the game's HUD art (LIFE / SCORE / HIGH /
GOLD / RND: and the slot frames) IS the credits picture's panel region,
copied down onto the front buffer by boot_credits_screen with the lives
drawn over it by game_restart_reset; the stage load only repaints the play
window. Every play frame now comes from an image that ran clear_palette,
clear_both_screens, boot_title_screen, boot_credits_screen and
boot_load_stage in the boot's order, as run_the_boot_chain does on target.

Pins: both screen buffers after the chain are byte-identical to
atari/build/ORIGRAM.BIN (the original's RAM dumped at $f8b4) — 0 of 32,000
bytes differ in either; a stage reload changes neither buffer, which is
why the panel survives a round end on the machine. game_restart_reset
also resets WB_LEVEL_SEQ_INDEX, so the stage-1 image is seeded with
nothing but the staged files; the revival box no longer occurs (the
player no longer dies there) — stage8-message.png -> stage8-lava.png, and
the message-box picture moved to stage 2's entry ("Let's go.", verified by

events.title: wonderboy: send IKBD $12 at boot — fire on iron needs the mouse off
events.message:
wonderboy: send IKBD $12 at boot — fire on iron needs the mouse off

Second iron result (probe disk, 4 MB STE, TOS 1.62, stick in port 1):
title loads, 35 IKBD bytes reach the handler, reset ack $f1 heard, and
the PRESS half of the fire wait times out ($d018) — no $FF packet with
bit 7 ever arrives. On a real ST the mouse's right button IS joystick
port 1's fire line: with the mouse enabled the 6301 reports joy-1 fire
as a mouse packet and strips bit 7 from the joystick packet (Hatari
models it: IKBD_DuplicateMouseFireButtons). The original's init_ikbd
sends exactly one IKBD command, $12 disable-mouse ($f8f0, sole caller
$e48c); this port sent none. Every smoke pass crossed the fire gates by
debugger poke, so the input path had never run anywhere.

Harness:
- wonderboy_main.c: ikbd_send(IKBD_DISABLE_MOUSE) once in install(),
  where $e48c sits; re-sent after each end-of-run reset's reply so the
  shim's own resets cannot re-enable the mouse mid-wait; stats field
  ikbd_mouse_disable_sent; STATS_MAGIC 'WBA6' (a pre-$12 record is
  refused by name).
- smoke.py: record row on every record-writing mode; trace row on every
  io_write-traced pass (ownplay 2 AND 4, floppy 1/2/3/5): before the
  first program-side pen write the IKBD traffic is exactly [$12], after
  it every $12 follows a reset; play passes require none after. One
  program_io_writes walk (ROM floor + repeat-collapse refusal; EmuTOS
  writes $00 to $fffffc02 three times running from $e0d078) shared by
  pen_window and the $12 row. RED-proved: send deleted, send claimed
  but not made, a reset injected after the send, the send moved into
  chain_prologue.

execution.md taxonomy 12 (a gate crossed by a poke is a gate whose

events.title: datadisks: pre-reduce the art by default (PERBAND=auto)
events.message:
datadisks: pre-reduce the art by default (PERBAND=auto)

The user's call, from hardware: the ECS build looks worse than the ST's
despite better hardware, because ALL of the ECS's bigger colour budget is
spent by a runtime quantiser on a 7MHz 68000. Converting offline is what
fixes that, so it should be what happens by default rather than something
you have to know to ask for.

PERBAND now defaults to `auto`, which picks the budget from the target:
24 colours per band for `amiga` (ECS has 32 per copper band), 12 for
`atari`/`atari720`/`gotek` (ST/STE has 16). `PERBAND=off` restores SSI's
palettes untouched, `PERBAND=<n>` sets your own.

The trade is documented where it is made, because one disk set serves a
whole family (atari feeds the ST *and* the Falcon/TT; amiga feeds ECS
*and* AGA): converting is right for the bitplane member and slightly
flattens the 256-colour one, so `off` is the answer when the media is for
a Falcon/TT/A1200/graphics card only. Measured palette rms error 9.3 at
budget 24 and 14.5 at 12, against 26.3 for a global 32-colour cut and
34.6 for global 16 — even the ST budget lands far closer to SSI's
original than what the runtime quantiser produces on the machine it is
for.

Verified: `amiga` converts at 24 (4518 over-budget bands -> 0, rms 7.6),
`atari` at 12 (rms 13.2), `PERBAND=off` runs no conversion, and the
resulting images differ from the unconverted ones.

events.title: tools: perband reads DOS .TLB too, and mkdatadisks can apply it (PERBAND=)
events.message:
tools: perband reads DOS .TLB too, and mkdatadisks can apply it (PERBAND=)

Wires the per-band converter into the media the user actually installs
from, without adding a step or a prompt to any installer (the ADR-0019
lesson: installers stay pure-copy).

Two parts:

1. perband.py now converts SSI's DOS .TLB (HLIB) art, not just the Mac
   .ctl (GLIB) twin. That matters because the data disks ship .TLB by
   default and the engine derives the .ctl on first touch — convert only
   the .ctl and the reduced palettes never reach the machine. An HLIB
   palette entry carries the SAME RGB payload at the same +8 offset as its
   GLIB twin (only container endianness and header word order differ, and
   _convert_entry passes colour tables verbatim), so the tool converts to
   GLIB in memory, runs the analysis with the decoders already proven
   there, and writes the merged triples back into the ORIGINAL bytes by
   position. Verified on PICA.TLB: same length, magic preserved, all 8011
   changed bytes inside palette RGB blocks, and the result still converts
   to a valid GLIB.

2. mkdatadisks.sh takes PERBAND=<colours> and converts a COPY of the
   source tree before packing. Suggested budgets: 24 for Amiga ECS (32
   per copper band), 12 for ST/STE (16), leaving headroom for the chrome,
   roster and text box that share every band.

OPT-IN, deliberately. One set of data disks serves a whole family: the
atari disks feed the ST *and* the Falcon/TT, the amiga disks feed ECS
*and* AGA. Reducing the art helps the machine that must quantise and
slightly flattens the one that need not, so it is a choice made when
building media for a specific low-colour machine rather than something
done to everyone's art by default.

pictures (1 skipped, an art_convert layout it already could not read,

bands -> 0, rms 7.6 — and the built ADFs differ from the stock ones
(7053/29835/16215 bytes on disks 1-3), so the conversion demonstrably

events.title: tools: perband.py — offline art reduction to the PER-BAND budget (ADR-0020 v2)
events.message:
tools: perband.py — offline art reduction to the PER-BAND budget (ADR-0020 v2)

The v1 global palette was the wrong target and the ECS proved it: reducing
a picture to one 32-colour palette throws away the copper's 25 per-band
palettes and looks flatter than what the runtime quantizer already
produces. The hardware's actual constraint is per BAND, so the target is:

    no 8-scanline strip may need more than "budget" distinct colours

A picture meeting that can still carry far more than 32 colours overall —
different strips spend their 32 on different colours — and every band then
quantizes EXACTLY: nothing merged at runtime, so no per-band seams and no
nearest-luma stray pixels.

Met by MERGING PALETTE ENTRIES ALONE, no pixel rewriting: a strip's cost is
its number of distinct RGB values, not indices, so giving two indices the
same RGB costs one colour wherever they co-occur. Pixels, offsets and
codecs are untouched (the by-construction-valid rewrite v1 proved). Each
merge picks the closest pair inside an over-budget strip, so fidelity is
spent only where the constraint binds. A picture lands at screen y=24, a
multiple of the 8-row band height, so its own strips align with the bands.

Decodes every colour codec the art uses: mode 2 + 0x40 (PackBits 8bpp),
mode 7 (transparency RLE), mode 9 (composite), and l2d4e's raw-8bpp
fall-through (modes 0 and 5 — mode 5 being the dungeon wall tiles). 1bpp
mono pieces draw in a single pen colour, so they constrain nothing and
must not disqualify their picture.

Whole HEIRS corpus at budget 24: 364 pictures, 0 skipped, worst band
197 -> 24 colours, 2323 over-budget bands -> 0, palette rms error 7.6 —
against 26.3 for v1's global 32 and 34.6 for global 16.

MEASURED ON ECS, artefact rows in the tavern picture:
  stock art, pre-#167    9 rows / severity 3.39
  stock art, post-#167   3 rows / 0.85
  per-band art           0 rows / 0.00   <- clean, modelling intact

7 new tests pin the budget guarantee and that ONLY palette RGB bytes
change; 481 pass.

events.title: ecs: load each band's palette in the PRECEDING hblank (#167)
events.message:
ecs: load each band's palette in the PRECEDING hblank (#167)

The A500 'the bigpics all had leftover pixels' report is a copper timing
bug, not leftover pixels. cop_build waited for the band's OWN first
scanline at hpos 0 and then issued 32 COLOR moves. A copper MOVE costs 2
copper cycles = 4 colour clocks, so 32 need 128 CCK, and the display
window opens at DIWSTRT hpos 0x81 = 129 CCK: one colour clock of margin,
before the four memory-refresh slots at the top of every scanline and any
blitter contention. The tail of the load lands inside the visible line
(or slips a line), so that scanline shows the PREVIOUS band's colours for
the registers not yet rewritten — a thin wrong-coloured line at every
band boundary, dashed because only slots that differ between the two
palettes look wrong.

Now waits on (line - 1, hpos 0x64 = CCK 200, past DIWSTOP's 193) so the
load owns the tail of the previous line plus the whole horizontal blank —
~156 CCK for the 128 it needs — and every register is in place before the
band's first pixel.

How it was pinned, since three plausible causes were wrong first:
  - draw-time planar layer: RULED OUT, PLANAR=0 is pixel-identical.
  - row-diff announcements: RULED OUT, a whole drive under
    FRUA_DIRTYCHECK logs 0 unannounced rows.
  - both palette caches: RULED OUT, palcache=off clutcache=off unchanged
    (and the log confirms 0 cache hits).
  - The Falcon renders the same picture from the same save perfectly:
    no copper, no band palettes.
  - Every artefact row sits at an exact multiple of ECS_RPB (game rows
    32/48/56/72/80/96, mod 8 == 0) and the SAME rows appear on two
    different pictures — positional, not content.

Measured on the HEIRS tavern-brawl picture, picture region only: 9
artefact rows / 3.37 severity -> 3 rows / 0.85, a 75% reduction. The
residual is most likely the genuine per-band palette seam rather than
timing; quantsim on the same frame says banding is otherwise worth
keeping (mean sq err 125.8 banded vs 249.6 global), so the answer there
is palette continuity or ADR-0020's offline pre-quant, not fewer bands.

AGA and ST/STE build; 474 tests pass.

events.title: wonderboy: the actor tier on a record view (x3.7 → x2.5), --gc-sections
events.message:
wonderboy: the actor tier on a record view (x3.7 → x2.5), --gc-sections

Reconstruction — the actor tier
- include/actor_view.h + src/actor_view.c: an ActorRecord VIEW of the
  actor's own record, proved ONCE per actor at the door instead of per
  field: inside the image it is a pointer (d16(An) fields, no mask, no
  guard); a record the image does not wholly hold runs against a 32-byte
  scratch pre-filled with the live prefix, writes masked by a per-byte
  `live` map (a dropped store must stay zero — six swoop cases say so),
  and given back whole at the close. Longword fields are whole-operand,
  as the shim's bus is. Every published routine keeps its (image, actor)
  signature as a door over a `_body`; 111 doors, all through one macro
  family; host-only REC_WITHIN_RECORD asserts on the accessors.
- src/behavior.c, map.c, player.c, actor.c: 591 + 131 + 59 field
  accesses moved onto the view; every actor.c helper that reached the
  caller's own record by address (actor_set_side_flag — the tier's last
  raw unguarded pointer — damage_template_hitpoints, defeat_and_score,
  start_motion_at_speed, …) has a record-taking body, so nothing writes
  the record behind an open door. The 61-row linear handler search is a
  switch (a compare tree under -fno-jump-tables). actor_fall_and_settle
  3,843 → 1,691 cycles a call, actor_behavior_pass 60.6 K → 42.3 K a
  frame walking vs the original's 17.1 K (x3.7 → x2.5); the frame is
  vblank-quantised, so walking reads 443 frames / 22.15 fps as before.
- Measured and rejected: a fast-arm mask branch (+8 KB for 0.3 K).

Build — --gc-sections adopted
- atari/build.sh: -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections, --gc-sections;
  every symbol gate asks the OBJECTS (pre-collection) — the ELF-based
  clone gate had broken the six modes that draw no sprite; a mode-aware
  ELF check keeps the seam symbols that must be live. PRG text −15 KB,
  boot floppy 26,624 → 39,936 B free.
- atari/mkprg.py: fixups filtered to loaded sections, each read back
  from the flat binary and cross-checked against the ELF, the emitted
  GEMDOS table decoded and matched; every guard a real refusal (no
  assert); negative addends and a one-past-the-end pointer accepted.
- atari/tos.ld: `.bss SUBALIGN(2)` — byte-packed .bss put a longword at
  an odd address once collection reshuffled it (Address Error on
  target; Joust's copy carries the same latent fault — cross-noted in
  its STATUS); KEEP for the .s file's own .text.

Verification
- make test 6,457 green (new pin: slot 7's damage arm at a record
  straddling the image top — RED before the class was closed, GREEN
  after); make guarded clean (10,050 runs); full on-target ladder OK
  (m1 novbl m2 m5 m6 m3 boot ownplay floppy); mutations per change in
  STATUS.md.

Docs
- STATUS.md "Performance" (three actor phases, the view's semantics,
  holes registered honestly, gc-sections), atari/README.md, bus.h and
  backend seam census, docs/on-target-execution.md (the .bss/gc gotcha).

events.title: text: the typewriter presents its OWN ROWS, not the whole screen (#166)
events.message:
text: the typewriter presents its OWN ROWS, not the whole screen (#166)

The slow-text pacer (l435a) shows each glyph with a FULL present. On a
machine where that is expensive — a 7MHz ECS, or the ATW800/2 whose VME
full present measures ~0.5s — it costs far more than the glyph interval
the pacer was willing to give away, so the machine immediately falls
behind. The fell-behind arm returns before reaching the present at all,
so presents STOP and the remaining glyphs are drawn invisibly until
something else presents.

The player does not see a typewriter: they see a fragment, a pause, then
the rest at once — 'it will say The weary wande, pause for one or one
and a half seconds, then finish' (Mega STe + ATW hardware report). The
same thing reproduces headlessly on ECS: two consecutive frames read
THE WEARY WANDERER then THE WEARY WANDERER., the whole difference being
the final character.

Narrow the present to the rows the glyph actually announced, so the
per-glyph cost is one text line instead of 200 rows and the pacer stays
ahead. Falls back to a full present when the announcement says scan-all
or no span can be derived (identical to the old behaviour). Adds
qd_surface_width() so the row span can be presented full-width without
hardcoding a machine's geometry.

Verified on ECS at the same square that showed the split: the text now
arrives progressively — 15 consecutive distinct frames at 1s sampling
(THE COMMON ROOM IS FR ... FREE TO YOU RIFF-RAFF, BUT HAVE A CARE TO)
where before there were two. Falcon boots to menu unchanged; ST/STE and
020 builds link; 474 tests pass.

events.title: ecs: titles compose whole — defer the copper palette to the flip, drop the mid-body present (#165)
events.message:
ecs: titles compose whole — defer the copper palette to the flip, drop the mid-body present (#165)

Two independent causes behind the A500 field report ('half buffer, then
load more, and corruption', 'wrong colors for a brief moment'), both
reproduced in amiberry and fixed:

1. WRONG COLOURS. ecs_reband() installed the new per-band copper palette
   immediately, but when the caller is ecs_render() the planes that
   palette describes do not exist yet: the whole-screen remap + c2p take
   ~12 SECONDS on a 7MHz 68000 (measured via FRUA_ECSTRACE: render start
   rl 446597 -> end 637848). The copper spent all of it showing the
   OUTGOING screen under the INCOMING palette — old pixels, wrong
   colours, sliced horizontally because the bands ARE the copper's
   palette regions. Now staged and committed WITH the plane switch. The
   content-same (remap_same) arm still installs immediately and must:
   there the planes are already right and only the RGB moved (deferring
   that would re-create #140).

2. HALF-DRAWN SCREENS. l19d4's mid-body present deliberately shows the
   base image WITHOUT its overlay piece. Free on the Mac (the body ran
   between frames); here it is a real screen-building pass, so the
   half-composed title is what a slow machine shows for most of the
   title's life. HW-palette backends already skipped it; the same
   reasoning applies to any backend, and dropping it matches both the
   DOS release (titles arrive whole) and the Mac's net frame.

Also adds the tear-free threshold for the incremental full present
(video.cfg tearfree=<rows>, 0 = off): scene-sized row sets go through
the page flip instead of converting into the page the copper is showing.

Measured: 80 samples over 160s of the ECS title sequence now yield 3
distinct frames, each a complete correctly-coloured title (was a
succession of banded and half-drawn intermediates). Falcon boots titles
to menu unchanged; ST/STE and 020 builds link; 474 tests pass.

  cont-only action file — `:trace` prints no VBL line, and any debugger

Reconstruction (the walking frame)
- src/scroll.c fill tier: clear_cells/draw_tiles walk host pointers,
  low half first then swap as the original stores, dbf counts held by a
  COUNT_BARRIER — fill_column 87.7 K → 67.9 K a call (x1.42 → x1.10).
- src/blit.c: the row counter and exit word decided before the walk

events.title: v0.5.1: career depth (training, diary, records, youth) + AI shooting fidelity
events.message:
v0.5.1: career depth (training, diary, records, youth) + AI shooting fidelity

CAREER — the manager finally has levers, and the club has a memory.

* WEEKLY TRAINING (new). Pick a drill, an intensity and up to six players; the
  session is graded and slowly loads their skills. Modelled on FIFA 18's
  weekly graded session and CM 01/02's intensity dial, mapped onto SWOS's seven
  0..7 skills. Deterministic (CareerRng only) and completely skippable.
  Design + sources: docs/decisions/04-training-and-development.md
* YOUTH INTAKE DAY (plan #6). The academy's new players once a summer, each
  with a scouted RANGE rather than a number.
* CLUB DIARY (plan #7). One line per event across the whole career: signings,
  milestones, thrashings, runs, intakes, the board's verdict, the season's
  finish. Read-only by design — no unread counter, nothing to clear.
* APPEARANCES + GOALS and a CLUB RECORDS board (plan #8). New APP/GLS columns
  in the squad screen and an all-time appearance list that a sold player keeps
  his place in.

Three long-standing defects these screens exposed:

* every regular in every career was pinned at 100 fatigue — i.e. playing at
  FatigueModel.SkillPenalty's -2 tier for whole careers. Recovery between
  matches was FLAT and could never catch a big enough per-match gain; a flat
  rate cannot have an equilibrium below the cap. It now also sheds 35 % of the
  carried fatigue over a week's rest, and a pre-season divides it by five.
* the youth academy fell permanently silent after ~3 seasons: a club at the
  squad cap was given no intake at all.
* FormModel.FormSkillDelta had no caller outside a test. Form was computed,
  stored, displayed — and ignored by the match. It and the new sharpness now
  apply in CareerMatchTeam.ToPlayerRecord, capped at one SWOS level either way.

GAMEPLAY — closer to the original, and the CPU shoots straight.

* The AI no longer curves the ball away from goal. A port-only chase heuristic
  with no counterpart in the reference fired 25 410 of 30 000 ticks and
  overwrote the team-wide currentAllowedDirection from an arbitrary off-ball

events.title: wonderboy: bg_scroll_blit at parity — sixteen straight-line bodies again
events.message:
wonderboy: bg_scroll_blit at parity — sixteen straight-line bodies again

bg_scroll_blit 148.8 K → 111.6 K cycles a call against the original's
105.3 K (x1.4 → x1.06; the variant body itself is 102.4 K exclusive vs
101.5 K). Frame 339.5 K → 328.4 K, 23.60 → 24.40 fps.

Reconstruction
- src/scroll.c: the column's seam split is a compile-time constant
  again (LONGWORDS_BEFORE_THE_SEAM), and DEFINE_COPY_VARIANT generates
  the sixteen routines names.txt names, bg_scroll_copy_x0..x15, each
  owning both halves of its blit as the original's does — one call per
  blit, entered by index through BG_SCROLL_COPY_BY_COLUMN. Column 0 is
  the shipped bytes instruction for instruction: thirty
  move.l (a0)+,(a1)+, addq.l #8,a0, lea 40(a1),a1, dbf; the seam
  columns keep the original's lea -128(a0),a0.
- include/scroll.h: copy_constant_run — a Duff-style fallthrough that
  folds to a straight run for any constant length ≤ 30 — serves the
  text box (22) and the stage tile row (2) as well; the runtime
  block/tail copier is retired.
- tools/recreate_kit/include/machine.h: CURSOR_BARRIER — the empty asm
  that keeps a walked cursor in an address register ("+a" on m68k):
  without it GCC folds postincrements into d16(An) moves (28 cycles)
  and lets the allocator park the cursor in a data register.
- atari/build.sh: scroll.c's -O3 reason re-measured (the bodies are
  level-independent; the queue/serve tier is +4.4 K a frame at -O2).

Verification
- make test 6,453 green; make guarded clean (10,043 runs); mutations:

events.title: walk: render the step BEFORE its square's event fires (#163)
events.message:
walk: render the step BEFORE its square's event fires (#163)

Field report (Mega STe ATW800/2, 0.9.17-diag2): stepping onto a text
square printed the text at the bottom of the screen BEFORE the 3D view
drew the move — 'The Weary Wanderer.' landing while the view still
faced the caravan square. Structural, not timing: #90's deferred-render
optimization skips l1908's own jt312 (the Mac renders there), and
l63c0's replacement re-render runs only after the whole dispatch —
but jt297's GAP-1 block dispatches the square's event (l709e) INSIDE
the dispatch, so the event's text drew into a frame the step had never
reached. Invisible on a fast present; glaring on the ATW800/2 where a
full present is ~0.5 s of VME writes. The Mac order is
move-render-then-event (jt955's arm renders, THEN L41b2 dispatches).

Fix: hoist the cell-special read and flush the deferred render (jt312,
which presents) exactly when the step will do more than move — an
event will dispatch, or the sticky text box is about to clear.
Ordinary steps keep the #90 single-render path; only event steps pay
the second render, which is the frame the Mac drew anyway.

Verified in Hatari with an authored STICKY.DSN (sticky message,
confirm_mask=0, one step north of entry): enter -> view shows the move
and the text prints; standing -> text persists; leave -> box clears.
471 passed; 68000 + AGA + ECS build. Authoring trap re-confirmed while
setting it up: _hook's (col,row) vs the position box's ordering — hook
both readings when in doubt, one of them is silently a wall.

events.title: titles: black the hardware CLUT while a title composes — each screen pops in whole
events.message:
titles: black the hardware CLUT while a title composes — each screen pops in whole

Field report (Mega STe ATW800/2, 0.9.17-diag1): every title screen showed
its seams — the previous screen recoloured by the incoming master
palette, the base image crawling in before its set palette landed (the
magenta 'defer' slots on screen = the pink frames), then the overlay
piece arriving as a second visible crawl. The cause is structural on a
hardware-palette screen with a slow present: a CLUT write recolours the
frame INSTANTLY while a full present is ~0.5 s of VME byte writes, so
NO ordering of "install palette" and "write pixels" is seam-free —
53e7a8b9's blit-then-commit only moved the flash.

New qd_palette_blackout(on) (hw-palette backends only, no-op on
quantisers): on=1 pushes an all-black CLUT and latches further
qd_set_palette forwards (the logical palette still accumulates); off
pushes the accumulated palette. l19d4 wraps each title's two-pass
composition in it — the rows land invisibly on a black screen and the
release pops the finished title in whole, with a short fade-to-black
between screens: the DOS/Mac presentation. The hw path also skips the
mid-body present (it would spend a second slow present on an invisible
intermediate); quantisers keep the Mac's two-present cadence unchanged.

Verified: Falcon title captures match the pre-change landmark hashes
frame for frame (quantiser path untouched, cycling alive); TT shows
each title whole and correctly coloured with black fades between, SSI
stars cycling on the hold; emulated ATW800/2 (xVDI) and AGA both boot
through the roll to a correct menu (blackout balanced, palette
restored). 471 passed; AGA + ECS link.

nova: Seurat register diagnostic (novadiag=on) + FPGA identity gate

Two answers to the v0.9.17 field failure:

- video.cfg `novadiag=on` dumps the card's info block (version string),
  VTG mode registers, blitter register window and MegaSTE CPLD version
  to DBG.LOG, then runs a fully-logged self-test in OFFSCREEN VRAM:
  op-register write/readback (a shifted or write-only window shows up
  right there), a 1-row cmd-0x0003 copy and a 2-row cmd-0x0005 fill,
  each with poll counts, status snapshots and byte-verified
  destinations. One diagnostic boot on the real Mega STe produces
  everything needed to correct the emulation-derived blit model.
  docs/seurat-diag.md carries the emulation baseline to diff against.

- The direct-LUT/blitter arming now requires the Seurat's " cpm" ID
  longword at LUT+0x200+24 (the same compare xVDI's own detection runs,
  verified on the real ATW800/2) — the xVDI COOKIE alone was the wrong
  gate, since xVDI also drives ET4000-family cards (VMG-4000) where
  these addresses are plain framebuffer RAM: the LUT write/read probe
  would "pass" against RAM and we would paint pixels believing they
  were palette entries. No ID -> vs_color path; novalut=on still
  overrides.

FRUA to the menu): identity gate passes, all self-tests byte-perfect,

events.title: engine: the title logos cycle again — jt1066 phase A copied the wrong way
events.message:
engine: the title logos cycle again — jt1066 phase A copied the wrong way

The SSI stars and MicroMagic shimmer died in v0.9.7, when the jt919 title
roll replaced the port intro (the port intro ran its own cycle loop, so it
never depended on the engine tables). The chain was healthy until the
commit: jt993 read the title set's 3 cycle records (TITLE.CTL set 2 metric
[.,3,0,32,0,224,3,.]), jt1069 installed them into -3258 — and the very
next jt1066 wiped all three before jt1067 ever saw one come due.

Phase A of jt1066 is the third reversed-jt406 lift in this one subsystem
(after jt1067's rotate and jt1069's 0x756e install). The Mac pushes at
0x75e2-0x75ea are len 8, backup(-3354+i*8), live(-3258+i*8) — and by the
convention the 0x756e fix pinned (the push nearest the jsr is the SRC),
that is BlockMove(live, backup): the commit SAVES each flagged range.
The lift restored instead — from a backup jt1068 seeds to 12 empty
sentinels and nothing else writes — so every commit erased every fresh
range. The walk's fireplace only survived because dungeon_cycle_ensure
re-installs its ranges before every tick; the title roll has no such
guard, which is exactly the asymmetry that hid this for ten releases.

Bisected on release binaries (dense 0.6s captures, md5 runs): animated at
v0.9.6, dead from v0.9.7 — the jt919 commit's window, matching the user's
"some time after adding the music". With the copy righted, FRUA_CYCTRACE
(new, in-tree) shows the 3 ranges live and committing spans 176-191 +
208-239, and the SSI screen's frames all differ again; the UA wizard's
lightning alternates too. Menu and credits hashes are byte-identical to
the pre-fix build. 471 passed; 68000/STE titles render clean to the menu;

events.title: nova: blitter-offloaded presents on the ATW800/2 — 43% less VME traffic
events.message:
nova: blitter-offloaded presents on the ATW800/2 — 43% less VME traffic

The Seurat 2D engine (regs at LUT+0x900; model measured against xVDI
20260730 on the hatari-et4000 emulation) copies card memory only, so
the CPU still crosses the bus once per doubled pixel — but the 2x row
duplication moves to the card: the full present's CPU writes each
doubled row once and one cmd-0x0003 blit per changed-row run copies
the even rows to the odd rows. The init clear (512,000 CPU byte
writes) becomes one cmd-0x0005 fill blit from a zero row parked past
the visible screen — xVDI's own desktop-fill idiom.

Measured on the emulated ATW800/2 (VME access counters at the same
boot-to-menu anchor): 2,778,599 -> 1,594,553 bus writes, -43%, menu
pixel-identical. Armed only after the LUT bind (same xVDI-cookie
hardware gate — a classic card bus-errors at these addresses);
video.cfg novablit=off opts out; a bounded status poll drops back to
CPU presents for the session if the engine ever fails to go idle.
The register model awaits confirmation on the real FPGA — novablit=off
is the field escape if the first hardware run misbehaves.

events.title: nova: auto-switch the card to 640x400x256 for the game, restore on exit
events.message:
nova: auto-switch the card to 640x400x256 for the game, restore on exit

On a Nova/ATW800/2 the game now plays full-screen in the card's native
640x400x256 regardless of the desktop mode (big desktops left the game
in a corner; a TrueColor desktop meant no card at all), and QUIT hands
the desktop back exactly the mode it booted in.

The sanctioned interface: the driver's XCB block via the xVDI/NOVA
cookie — p_chres(RESOLUTION*, 0) at XCB+8, the same call XVDIMENU
makes. Three facts measured on the hatari-et4000 emulated card:
- p_chres is a REGISTER-ABI call (RESOLUTION* in A0, fll_ofst in D0,
  from XVDIMENU's own code) — a C stack call sets a garbage mode;
- vq_extnd still answers with the PRE-switch caps afterwards (the
  VDI's device info is not rebuilt at runtime), so the backend takes
  width/height/planes from the .BIB entry it just set;
- RESOLUTION entries are 86 bytes; match on mode byte +35 (2 = 256c)
  and the HDI/VDI display words +60/+68. The .BIB is read from the
  boot drive's AUTO folder; restore entry = the XCB's current index,
  verified against the live size, with a scan fallback.

Verified on the emulated ATW800/2: 1024x768x256 desktop -> game at
640x400x256 (menu clean, LUT bound) -> q/y quit -> desktop back at
1024x768. Classic NOVA-VDI (640x480): benign no-op, unchanged boot.
video.cfg novares=off opts out.

events.message:
Reconstruct the 1987 SSG renderer from the Amiga binary; add .dat support

Recover the lost SSG (Scene Simulation Generator) renderer as C source in
ssg-src-authentic/, reverse-engineered from the original 1987 Amiga 68000
executable with Ghidra and validated byte-for-byte against the binary's
output under vamos. The reconstruction reproduces the binary's actual
behaviour rather than merely its images: bare rt-style names, single-
precision (FFP) math, an fscanf .dat reader built on the executable's own
recovered scanf grammar, a fixed up-front sphere allocation, and the
scanline-coherent screen-space-culling renderer (per-sphere projected
bounding boxes, per-scanline active lists, per-pixel column cull). Builds
as the ssg_authentic target with a ctest that checks it against the
captured original-binary renders.

Also add the runtime .dat parser for the modernized rt pipeline
(src/datparse.c) and PNG output (src/png.c); reverse-engineering notes;
blog posts (parts 3 and 4); Ghidra export scripts and validation tooling;
and the original-binary capture files used as the validation oracle.

wonderboy: blit register window — no libgcc modulo (4.75 → 9.45 fps)

Reconstruction
- src/blit.c: mask_reg/plane_reg wrapped the 68000 register window with a
  `% WB_BLIT_SCRATCH_REGS`; -m68000 has no 32-bit divide, so each was a
  ~900-cycle __umodsi3 (→ __udivsi3 + __mulsi3) call — 856 per frame, 47%

  blit_row 42,000 → 8,807 cycles per call; the original runs 320 K/frame
  at a locked 25 fps.

events.title: ecs: CLUT-keyed RAM palette cache — the walk's per-step re-quant churn (A500)
events.message:
ecs: CLUT-keyed RAM palette cache — the walk's per-step re-quant churn (A500)

Field report: on the A500 the town walk drains and reloads its colours on
every step ('the CLUT keeps unloading/loading'). Measured on the inn
street route: SEVEN full re-bands in sixteen moves, each dragging a full
re-render — the walk's wall-set CLUTs alternate between a handful of
palettes, and the only cache (the disk one) keys on clut+FRAME hash,
which can never hit mid-walk.

This is the ST's st_pcache ported: six RAM entries keyed on the CLUT
alone (hash + full 768-byte verify, MRU). A hit skips the cut entirely
and carries the two guards the ST proved out: indices the cached cut
never saw are re-pointed at their nearest per-band slot (no falling
through the absent-colour bucketing), and when the restored remaps equal
the live ones the planes on screen stay valid — palettes-only, no
force-full, no epoch reset. Fresh cuts and exact disk hits both store.
video.cfg clutcache=off opts out. ~59 KB of BSS.

Same route on the cache build: 3 fresh cuts (first-ever CLUTs only),
3 RAM hits, and the user's exact video shots — the brown door, the
innkeeper event — render correct in emulation.

events.title: engine+ste+ecs: the v0.9.7 title regression — palettes commit before the blits, and a replaced CLUT re-quantises eagerly
events.message:
engine+ste+ecs: the v0.9.7 title regression — palettes commit before the blits, and a replaced CLUT re-quantises eagerly

Field report + archaeology: the titles 'displayed perfectly a few versions
ago'. Verified — v0.9.6's are clean; v0.9.7's are not. 87251793 (v0.9.7)
replaced the port's hand-written intro (which pre-installed each screen's
palette) with the engine's own jt919/l19d4 sequence, whose Mac order is
blit-then-commit. On the Mac that whole body runs inside a frame; the
planar backends stamp the visible planes AS the blit runs (seconds at
8 MHz), so each title rendered quantised under the PREVIOUS screen's
palette — the yellow wizard and candy-striped credits. The DOS original
(DOSBox, 0.35 s sampling) shows every title fully-formed and correct, so
this was never faithful in effect.

Three-part fix, verified frame-by-frame in Hatari (STE, real-time):
- l19d4 commits each picture's palette BEFORE its blits (the Mac's net
  frame; the original tail commits skip via the CLUT-unchanged guard),
  and holds presents across the compose (qd_present_hold).
- st/ecs_clut_major_change(): a wholesale CLUT replacement (>=64 entries
  moved clearly) vetoes the registers-only repalette — the split
  heuristic cannot see 'everything moved' — and re-quantises EAGERLY at
  install time, so draw-time stamps after the commit use the new cut.
  Same total cost: the present's CLUT-unchanged guard then skips the
  re-band this replaces; the walk's CLUT alternation stays on the
  palette cache.
- Chunky backends (Falcon/TT/Nova) get the ordering fix for free: the
  commit-first order removes their draw-vs-install colour flash too.

Wizard + Forgotten Realms + credits now compose and settle in their own
colours; settled frames match v0.9.6's.

events.title: nova: row-diffed present + long writes — the slow card text; name the >8bpp fallback
events.message:
nova: row-diffed present + long writes — the slow card text; name the >8bpp fallback

Field report (Mega STe + ATW800/2): text crawled in Nova mode while
normal ST mode was fine. A full qd_present rewrote all 512,000 card
bytes over the VME bus with per-byte writes, and every glyph update
triggers one. Two-part fix: a shadow of the last-delivered frame makes
the full present write only rows whose bytes changed (compares run in
local RAM, an unchanged screen costs zero bus traffic), and the doubling
loop now emits one aligned LONG per two source pixels instead of four
byte stores — a quarter of the transactions for rows that do write.
novadiff=off in video.cfg restores the old behaviour for A/B.

Also: a card found at 16bpp+ was silently handed back to the ST backend,
reading as a probe failure in the field. Our present writes raw 8-bit
indices, so >8bpp genuinely cannot work — but now DBG.LOG says the card
was FOUND and asks for the desktop to be set to 256 colours.

events.title: engine: the plate cache keys on the label TEXT, not just its pointer — the treasure bar drew POOL over EXIT
events.message:
engine: the plate cache keys on the label TEXT, not just its pointer — the treasure bar drew POOL over EXIT

A1200/ECS real-hardware report: on the treasure screen, SHARE the platinum
then TAKE the ring and the command bar shows POOL where EXIT belongs;
clicking that "POOL" presses (and acts as) EXIT. Reproduced identically on
the Falcon — shared-code, not ECS.

The A/B convicted the command-button plate cache (#138-#141): with
FRUA_NOPLATECACHE the re-laid bar is correct (VIEW POOL EXIT); with the
cache it replays VIEW TAKE POOL. The cache key was (label POINTER, count,
top, left, state) — but a bar re-layout rebuilds its label strings in the
SAME pool slots, so the slot that held "TAKE" now holds "POOL" at the same
address and position, and the stale plate replays. The pressed repaint
misses (state bit differs), which is why the clicked button flashed its
true label — the tell that convicted stale pixels over stale logic.

Fix: a djb2 hash of the label C string (capped at 32 bytes) joins the key;
find and capture both carry it. A reused slot with new text now misses and
repaints; identical text still hits, so the 82->23-tick bar win is intact.
Verified: the exact repro (beginplay -> entry chain -> s,t,t) renders
VIEW POOL EXIT with the cache ON, matching the no-cache control frame.

events.title: ecs: disarm the sprites at display takeover — the pointer-over-title and the left-edge garbage (A1200 real hardware)
events.message:
ecs: disarm the sprites at display takeover — the pointer-over-title and the left-edge garbage (A1200 real hardware)

The takeover DMACON write only SET raster+copper — sprite DMA stayed
however Workbench left it (on), and the BPLCON2=0 line commented "no
sprites" sets sprite PRIORITY, not sprite enable. On real silicon the
Intuition pointer therefore kept displaying over the title screens (the
original shows no pointer until the menu), and dangling sprite fetches drew
a garbage column at the left edge. Cycle-exact amiberry showed neither,
which is why five weeks of headless runs never caught it.

Fix: clear DMAF_SPRITE (a plain clear, not SETCLR) and disarm all eight
channels (SPRxCTL=0, data words cleared — an armed sprite keeps displaying
its last data even with DMA off) before enabling raster+copper; shutdown
re-sets sprite DMA before LoadView(oldview) so the Workbench pointer
returns after quit. The AGA backend already had the null-sprite discipline
(kept from the retired sprite cursor, #64) and is untouched.

Needs the real A1200/A500 to confirm — the emulator renders identically
either way (verified: boot + title unchanged headless).

events.title: installer: the Install icon exits cleanly — CD off the floppy before running
events.message:
installer: the Install icon exits cleanly — CD off the floppy before running

A1200 (WB 3.2, Installer 47.19): a fully SUCCESSFUL install ended with
"Please insert volume OpenUA-ECS-1 in any drive" and the install window
stuck open. The launcher script runs FROM the engine disk, so its shell's
current directory is that floppy's VOLUME; when the Installer hands control
back, AmigaDOS re-validates the CD for the next script line — and the disk
in the drive by then is the last data disk. The WAIT tooltype then kept the
IconX window up on top of it.

Fixes: the launcher does `CD RAM:` first and uses absolute paths throughout;
the WAIT tooltype is gone (the Installer route closes its window itself) and
the instdisk fallback branch pauses explicitly instead ("Press RETURN to
close"); the redundant (protect uaconv +e) tail line is dropped (copyfiles
preserves the bits). instdisk now derives the drive from PROGDIR: (where the
binary was loaded from) rather than the current directory, so the CD change
cannot confuse it — verified headless: CD RAM:, instdisk run from a subdir,
full data+engine install lands. Also: uaconv.c's header caught up with
ADR-0019 (it is an optional tool now, not the install path).

The end-of-install requester itself cannot fire in the harness (filesystem2
volumes are never "removed"), so the exit-clean confirmation needs the next
real A1200 install.

skills: the porting kit, distilled — port-ssi-mac-68k, planar-display-kit, hardware-media-kit

Three skills capturing what this project discovered the hard way, so the
next SSI title (the ST only ever got Curse of the Azure Bonds; the Amiga

- port-ssi-mac-68k: what is reusable as-is (toolchain, Mac Toolbox shim,

  content edges only, never arbitrary boundaries = the #40 seam), the
  CLUT-guard/repalette/split-guard cache family, the disk palette cache

events.title: ecs: viewport palette groups — the walk re-band drops ~9.5 s -> ~1.1 s (#139 port)
events.message:
ecs: viewport palette groups — the walk re-band drops ~9.5 s -> ~1.1 s (#139 port)

The ECS re-band ran the median cut per band: 25 cuts a frame, and the phase
profile put cut+buckets at 86% of a ~149,000 raster-line (~9.5 s) re-band on
the 7 MHz 68000. The ST solved this in #139 by splitting at the only lines
where the content really changes — the first-person viewport edges — and
cutting once per group. Ported: with a rendered viewport in the frame, the
re-band cuts 3 groups (chrome above / viewport / chrome below), 32 colours
each. 96 slots against a walk frame whole ~63 colours, so fidelity holds.
Measured on the walk: 16,400-18,900 rl per grouped re-band = ~1.1 s, ~8x.

Screens WITHOUT a viewport (title, menus, event pictures) keep the full 25
per-band cuts: one-time work the disk cache replays forever, per-band
fidelity on big pictures is worth keeping, and their existing cache entries
stay bit-valid (that path is untouched — boot re-bands measured identical
to the pre-change baseline).

Two mechanisms the port needed:

1. dsp_viewport_note: the engine announce of the rendered viewport rect.
   dsp_viewport_commit is gated on the backend supplying a scratch, and the
   ECS supplies none (it renders straight into the engine surface) — the
   first cut registered the commit hook and grouping never engaged. The
   note fires unconditionally at the end of every 3D render; no listener,
   no effect (the ST registers none and is unaffected).

2. A CONTENT fingerprint, not present-order bookkeeping: the announce
   samples 16 spread pixels of the rendered viewport; the re-band re-samples
   and groups only when they still match. A full-screen picture or menu
   overwrites them (falls back to 25 bands — no #40 seam from splitting a
   picture on a stale boundary); HUD/bar updates do not. The first scheme
   cleared a flag per present and most walk re-bands missed it — order
   between render, CLUT install and presents is not stable; content is.
   Verified live: the caravan portrait (drawn over the viewport area)
   correctly re-bands ungrouped; 3 of 3 true walk re-bands grouped.

video.cfg vpgroups=off restores the old path wholesale (one binary, the
runtime-A/B discipline). Falcon/ST/AGA builds link and make test passes;
the AGA/RTG/Falcon chunky backends are untouched (no quantizer there).
events.author: slaapliedje

events.title: wonderboy/kit: batch 44 phase B — the disk wall is a seam; the title loads
events.message:
wonderboy/kit: batch 44 phase B — the disk wall is a seam; the title loads

THE WALL CROSSED: the sector driver's 1,644 bytes are a SEAM, not a
model. disk_load_file ($5e7c) is the lowest routine with file-shaped
inputs (a 12-char DOS name in, bytes at a destination, 0/negative
out — the resource table's rows ARE the names); everything below is
sector-shaped. The band's crossings enumerated as a SET of four —
the seam's one call, an INTERRUPT crossing (the VBL's floppy-motor
timeout, invisible to any call walk), the Copylock's failure arm
inside its counted boundary, and an operand fragment — with the
closed-subgraph claim now POSITIVELY classified (every scan hit
names its enclosing instruction, decoded from declared anchors over
the 144 unwalked in-band bytes) and the in-edge census widened to
the statically-resolvable forms (jsr/jmp d16(pc), DBcc — planted
and RED-checked; the seven-sighting operand-hiding class covered).

THE HYBRID, decided on evidence (WD1772 model rejected: nothing
above the seam reads driver state): port above / counted boundary
below / GEMDOS substitution at the seam — AND THE ORACLE PERFORMS
THE SAME SUBSTITUTION (hand-assembled GEMDOS poked over the driver,
both sides through the kit's staged-file model), so the ordinary
byte diff holds the two statements equal. Kit TRAP_MODEL Phase 9
(disk.h/disk.c); the backend is the seventh required symbol.

ON TARGET: the .PRG loads TITLESCR.RAD across the seam, depacks it,
sets the palette — 0 of 32,000 framebuffer bytes and 16/16 pens vs
the shipped binary, both ROMs, with its picture control.

FOUND ON THE MACHINE: DOS names are SPACE-PADDED (CREDITS .RAD —
an internal-space case a strip assertion cannot see; caught only on
hardware); Super(0)/Super(ssp) is NOT a balanced pair (TOS returns
on the frozen USP — crashed AFTER a clean teardown with every
read-back green; fixed here, and Joust ships the identical wrapper:
registered at its own surface, comment-only). Four pins true for
the wrong reason retired; the retraction scan became a CASE whose
first run caught a fourth quotation no reviewer had flagged.

Suites: wonderboy 6,363 / kit 392 / joust 4,369 / buggyboy 292 /
hw 56 — all clean-build serial; 18 modes x 2 ROMs green. Sweep 29
killed / 0 survived. Queued: the credits/prompt/stage-load rungs to
the own-entry boot; the retraction scanner's tools/ promotion; the
error arm's oracle-side answer.

events.title: ecs: disk-backed palette cache — the 16-entry cap was THE "converts every screen" bug
events.message:
ecs: disk-backed palette cache — the 16-entry cap was THE "converts every screen" bug

The palette cache held EPC_MAX=16 blobs in RAM and, once full, STOPPED
caching (the add was gated on e_pc_n < EPC_MAX with no eviction). A dungeon
shows far more than 16 distinct scenes, so every frame past the 16th
re-quantised on EVERY view, forever — the A500 "it converts every single
screen" misery. The PROGDIR fix only helped the first 16.

Now the KEYS live in RAM (8 bytes each, EPC_CAP=2048) and the 8.8 KB blobs
live on disk in PALCACHE.ECS: a cache hit reads its blob back, a miss
appends a new one. Effectively unbounded, and it FREES ~141 KB of RAM
(the old 16*8800 blob table is gone) — welcome on a 2 MB ECS machine.

Robustness: the entry count is derived from the file SIZE and new entries
are appended with plain "ab", so there is no in-place header rewrite — an
"r+b" update the Amiga ncrt0 stdio would not do reliably (the first cut
used r+b and silently never grew past the initial entries). File layout is
unchanged (hdr + n*(key+blob)), so v1 caches still load; e_pc_last skips the
disk read when the wanted blob is already live.

Verified headless (ECS, User-Startup CD SYS:): cold boot creates the file
and appends; warm boot loads the keys and HITS them with zero quant; a
deterministic miss (truncate the file to one entry) quantises once and
appends back — the file grows, which the capped version could never do.
Each scene now quantises ONCE, EVER, then reads from disk forever.

events.title: installer: ship DOS .tlb + convert at install with uaconv; include Save A
events.message:
installer: ship DOS .tlb + convert at install with uaconv; include Save A

The Amiga now ships the authentic DOS .tlb art and converts it once at
install (the engine cannot convert at runtime, ADR-0015), rather than
shipping our derived .ctl. The flow:

- mkdatadisks defaults every target to .tlb again; the Amiga set carries the
  DOS art and uaconv converts it in place at install.
- instdisk, after the engine step, runs the installed <dest>/uaconv <dest>
  (SystemTags) — the DOS art is converted with no extra user action, and
  uaconv asks whether to delete the .tlb originals.
- the Workbench Install (AmigaOS Installer) route ships uaconv too and, after
  copying the data, protects it +e and runs it, with an askbool for whether to
  delete the originals (uaconv -d, since the Installer run has no stdin).
- uaconv and uaconv.info ride on the AGA disk and ECS disk 1, and are in
  ENGINE.LST so the instdisk route installs them.

Saves: mkdatadisks shipped the .DSN-root save CRUFT (headless-test leftovers)
because it skipped all of SAVE/. It now drops every savgam*/vault*/cch and
re-adds ONLY SAVE/SAVGAMA.CSV + SAVE/VAULTA.DAT — the authentic Save A, the
sole save on the original HEIRS disks. Placing it needed the Amiga image
writer to recurse (it was one-level); it now walks the staged tree at any
depth. Verified: Save A lands in HEIRS.DSN/SAVE/ bit-exact on both Amiga and
Atari, and instdisk->uaconv converts a .tlb install bit-exact on the 68000.

events.title: installer: uaconv — the Amiga one-time DOS-art converter (.tlb -> .ctl)
events.message:
installer: uaconv — the Amiga one-time DOS-art converter (.tlb -> .ctl)

The Amiga engine cannot convert DOS art at runtime (ADR-0015), so the art
must be converted at install. This is that converter: it scans the OpenUA
folder and its .DSN design sub-folders for DOS HLIB .tlb art, writes the Mac
GLIB .ctl twin the engine loads, then offers to delete the now-redundant
.tlb originals to reclaim the space.

Portable C over stdio + the artconv core (the same one uainst uses for fan
modules); the only platform split is the directory scan (dos.library
Examine/ExNext on the Amiga, POSIX readdir on the host, so the convert path
is host-testable). Colour convert only — no mono synthesis (that is the ST
mono build. install-time job). Borrows uainst_run_big_stack (asl_amiga.c) for
the stack artconv needs.

Verified: host and Amiga (68000) both convert the 23 base libraries + a
.DSN design library BIT-EXACT to make gamedata-dos; the keep/delete prompt
works and defaults to keep on EOF; a second run finds nothing (idempotent).

events.title: ecs: palette cache to PROGDIR: — it was writing to the CWD, so it never persisted
events.message:
ecs: palette cache to PROGDIR: — it was writing to the CWD, so it never persisted

The ECS palette cache (PALCACHE.ECS) is content-keyed and written on every
quantiser miss, so a repeat view of a picture should be instant. On the A500
it re-converted every boot: the cache used a BARE relative path
("PALCACHE.ECS"), and frua boots with the CWD set elsewhere (the mount
User-Startup does `CD SYS:` before running it; a Workbench-icon launch sets
CWD to the drawer, a Shell launch to wherever you were) — so the file was
written to SYS:, never found again, and every boot was a cold cache. DBG.LOG
never had this problem because it already uses PROGDIR:. Same fix here.

Verified headless (ECS mount, User-Startup CD SYS:): cold boot writes
PROGDIR:PALCACHE.ECS (2 entries, 17624 b) and quantises twice; warm boot logs
"palette cache entries loaded = 2", quantises ZERO times, file unchanged.

events.title: installer: Amiga data disks ship .ctl art (the engine cannot convert), quieter disk polling, and a drawer icon
events.message:
installer: Amiga data disks ship .ctl art (the engine cannot convert), quieter disk polling, and a drawer icon

Three fixes from the A500 real-hardware run (2026-08-22), after the
Install icon itself started working:

1. THE GAME DID NOT RUN. "Please insert disk [" with a sword cursor,
   right after a one-second "CONVERTING ART" bar. That is the engine
   cold-disk retry (jt987/l157c) on a missing resource: ALWAYS.CTL,
   "LBLoad: Bad Lib". The DATA disks ship DOS .tlb art (ART=tlb), and
   the ATARI engine converts .tlb->.ctl on first touch (boot.c
   ua_open_art fallback) — but the AMIGA engine does NOT: ADR-0015
   compiled that conversion out, and instdisk copies files verbatim, so
   a .tlb-only Amiga install has no path to the .ctl the engine loads.
   mkdatadisks now defaults amiga to ART=ctl (ship the converted libs,
   23 files, 6 disks); Atari keeps tlb. Reproduced by hiding the .ctl
   twins in the ECS mount (ALWAYS.CTL "Bad Lib"); .ctl-only boots to the
   SSI title with every library loaded.

2. THE POLLING WAS TOO AGGRESSIVE. Each poll of an empty DF0: raised
   AmigaDOS system requester "Please insert a disk in DF0", once a
   second — the installer looked like it was nagging. pr_WindowPtr = -1
   turns the DOS requesters off for the process (a missing disk is then
   a plain open failure, which the poll already treats as "not yet"),
   and the poll interval went 1s -> 2s.

3. NO DRAWER ICON. The Installer-script route makes one via
   (makedir (infos)); the plain instdisk route (WB 3.1, no Installer)
   did not, so the OpenUA drawer had no Workbench icon. instdisk now
   writes <dest>.info from an embedded 346-byte drawer icon
   (installer/drawer_icon.h). Verified under AmigaDOS: DH0:ICONTEST.info
   written byte-identical.

Also fixed a host-only bug the harness surfaced: wait_for_disk spun
forever on a closed stdin (now gives up). make test 471 passed.

events.title: wonderboy: batch 43 phase F — M3 closed; THE ON-TARGET LADDER IS WALKED
events.message:
wonderboy: batch 43 phase F — M3 closed; THE ON-TARGET LADDER IS WALKED

M3 CLOSES THE LADDER: all three of game_key_actions' endings driven
DELIBERATELY on a 68000 — the round-end reload (code 1), the cheat
level skip (code 2), the quit through the fadeout (code 3) — each by
a debugger poke at a program instant, with each run's own undriven
pass as the causal control, and a FOURTH run poking the scancode
alone (the cheat word left clear) proving the $604 predicate
load-bearing: its poke set is DERIVED from the arm's own minus the
word, so the control cannot drift from what it controls.

THE HAND-BACK, asserted from outside the program: both vectors
restored to TOS's own (values read per ROM), the machine's frame
clock +19 over the nineteen vblanks between two readings chained off
the program's own Pterm — because TOS RESETS a crashed machine
(restoring vectors, re-running the program, overwriting the records:
an absolute-vblank tail was defeated twice before the Pterm anchor
and rename-aside rescue landed, now covering every pass). The
m3fault control (vector stores suppressed): every hand-back row red
while Hatari exits 0 with a clean log — an incomplete hand-back is a
SILENT DEAD TOS.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND ON CODE NOTHING HAD EXECUTED: (1) every key-driven
exit hung forever — the exit scancode impersonated the IKBD
acknowledge in pin_sched_wait8's reset; isolated (the scancode alone
kills a run), fixed, and the interactive sibling (a key release in
the reset window) closed with it; (2) run.sh's --sound on never
parsed — found BY THE USER at the first real launch, the one line no
headless check ran; now --sound 44100 + a parsecheck mode whose
control re-inserts the rejected value and requires the refusal.

THE JOYSTICK BOUNDARY, measured to its terminal state: Hatari's
control-socket injects keys at the real IKBD (scancodes reached
WB_KEY_LAST_SCANCODE through the ACIA interrupt) but cannot press
the stick (--joy1 maps host events) — partial by construction,
run.sh and a person at the cursor keys are what run those arms.

Gate (6 findings applied): the retired absolute-count design swept
from three surfaces; the pass-1 record read given its own Pterm
rescue; the N-alone control added; mode_runsh's guard and
negative-index substitution rewritten; the +19 interval label
derived not asserted.

Suites: wonderboy 6,140 / kit 392 / hw 56; 33/33 on-target mode
runs across both ROMs. THE LADDER: M1 boot+backends, M2 52 frames
byte-exact, M3 endings+hand-back, M5 hardware vector+picture, M6
ordered write timeline — every rung green with controls both
directions. Beyond it: the boot chain (outside the spine), and the
carried queue.

events.title: installer: the Workbench Install icon falls back to instdisk — WB 3.1 never shipped Installer
events.message:
installer: the Workbench Install icon falls back to instdisk — WB 3.1 never shipped Installer

The A500 retest after the .KEY fix: "Installer was not found". Workbench
3.1 did not include Installer at all — it was a separate developer
package (Installer-43_3 on Aminet) that vendors bundled under a signed
paper licence from AMIGA Technologies (clause B.10), so we cannot ship
it either; only the complete unmodified archive is freely
redistributable, and 3.1 has no LhA to open it.

So the icon uses what we wrote. `instdisk` now rides on the AGA disk and
ECS disk 1; the IconX launcher runs it when neither SYS:System/Installer
nor SYS:Utilities/Installer exists, in the icon's CON: window (WAIT
tooltype keeps the window up). instdisk itself: RETURN takes a default
destination (DH0:OpenUA / C:\OPENUA) so the icon-clicker needs no path
syntax; starting from the ENGINE disk says so instead of "no DISK.LST";
and wait_for_disk no longer spins forever on a closed stdin (the host
harness found it re-prompting until killed).

Headless on 3.2 with System/Installer hidden: the launcher takes the
ELSE arm, instdisk starts, reads the drive and prompts — the full
console flow needs a real CON:, i.e. the A500.

events.title: installer: instdisk reads the DRIVE, installs the engine, and gets a GEM front-end; Workbench Install icon
events.message:
installer: instdisk reads the DRIVE, installs the engine, and gets a GEM front-end; Workbench Install icon

Three installer changes, all driven end to end in the emulators.

1. THE A1200 LOOP (first real-hardware run, 2026-08-22). instdisk read
   DISK.LST relative to its current directory — on AmigaDOS a lock on
   the VOLUME "OpenUA-Data-1" — so after the disk-2 swap the OS asked
   for volume OpenUA-Data-1 back, read disk 1's manifest, said "I need
   disk 2", forever. The source is now the DEVICE of the current
   directory (DosList: the volume lock's handler task -> the device
   entry -> "DF0:"), which always means whatever is in the drive. And
   since the OS notices a disk change itself, the Amiga swap prompt
   polls for the expected disk instead of waiting on RETURN.

2. THE ENGINE STEP. After the data set, instdisk asks for the engine
   disk(s) and installs from ENGINE.LST (same header line, then
   "<src> <dest> [a]" — `a` appends, which joins the two ECS halves into
   one frua). mkhwdist writes ENGINE.LST on every raw-binary engine disk
   (Falcon/TT, ST Gotek, AGA, ECS 1+2; the 720K zip disk has none and
   instdisk says so). Host-tested: two data disks, two engine disks,
   the join byte-exact.

3. INSTDISK.PRG — the GEM build (installer/gem_atari.c): file selector
   for the destination, alerts for the disk swaps, a window with a
   progress bar, console silenced. Raw AES/VDI trap bindings in the
   fsel_atari.c style. Driven headlessly under Hatari: a four-disk
   install plus the engine, 118 files, every data file byte-identical
   to the staged gamedata and FRUA.PRG identical to the release.
   Traps: fsel_exinput VALIDATES its seed path (a not-yet-existing
   folder throws "cannot find" and falls back to the floppy, which an
   OK then picks as the destination) — create it first; the VT52
   console paints printf over the desktop — silence it in GUI mode.
   Both INSTDISK.PRG and .TTP ride on Atari data disk 1.

4. THE WORKBENCH INSTALL ICON. An IconX launcher (`Install`) finds the
   OS Installer in SYS:System or SYS:Utilities (standard since 2.0,
   never in the path) and runs Install.script: askdir for the drawer,
   engine copy (ECS: both halves, then Join/Protect/Delete), then
   askdisk for each OpenUA-Data-N volume. Driven headlessly in amiberry
   with the disks mounted as named volumes, NOVICE mode: AGA and ECS
   both land 120 files with frua byte-identical to the release.
   Installer-language traps found the hard way: `dest` is a reserved
   word, `(all)` and `(pattern)` are mutually exclusive, and a
   `(pattern "a|b")` on a directory source silently matches nothing —
   copy files one at a time.

HARDWARE.md describes the three install routes; the data-disk README
explains the engine step. mkdatadisks skips a design's SAVE/ tree.

events.title: wonderboy: batch 43 phase E — M6, run.sh, and M3's first exit on target
events.message:
wonderboy: batch 43 phase E — M6, run.sh, and M3's first exit on target

DELIVERED FOR THE USER: atari/run.sh — the interactive Hatari
launcher. bash atari/run.sh builds the play PRG (frame cap and
watchdog lifted), stages the drive through smoke.py's own machinery
(ROM/memsize/monitor/auto-boot all exported from one place — no
copies), and launches windowed with sound, cursor keys + Right-Ctrl
as joystick 1, Ctrl-Q to quit. What you see, measured: the first
playable stage mid-game (the original's own post-boot RAM; no
title — the boot chain is unported), running INDEFINITELY at 4-5
frames a second on the emulated 8 MHz 68000 (1,000+ frames measured
on both ROMs). Hardened by the gate: spaced ROM paths, the record's
exit semantics.

M6 LANDS — the ordered write timeline: every write to the machine
over 52 frames, in order, reduced to a per-side shape derived from
each side's own buffer addresses (three pinned constants broke at
once on EmuTOS — the tell they were one fact written thrice) and
compared: heartbeat address-for-address, zero palette loads, zero
redundant loads, and the shipped binary's 1,155 PSG writes an EXACT
ORDERED PREFIX of ours — gated on measured PSG noise with a
committed instability floor. Instrument gotchas recorded: Hatari's
two hex spellings of one register, collapsed repeat lines (refused),
the classifier's base-address dependency. THE ORDER-ONLY SINK MUTANT
DIES: invisible to every M5 surface (measured — m5flash entirely
green with it applied), red in m6flash's order row. m6rearm proves
its own invisibility by running the whole M2 differential inside
itself (52 loads / 51 countable redundant — the instrument decided).

M3's FIRST EXIT EXECUTED ON TARGET: the ROUND_END ending driven by
a debugger poke on the play build — loop_ending is now the record's
evidence field, RB_VBL_TICKING asserts the liveness it is named for
(the old frames==requested proxy false-redded every player exit).
Completing M3 (all three endings deliberate + Pterm hand-back
asserted) is owed, and run.sh is the mechanism.

Findings: this port ADDED a screen-base transient the original
lacks (§3 retracted); a FOURTH boot deviation (the boot publishes
BACK where our shim publishes FRONT — cmt 0xf906); an EIGHTH
sweep-lie mode of the phase's own making (a staging test rewrote
the shared disk/ mid-boot). Gates: the author's eight (incl. a
live blocker) + the independent five (the play record's false red,
run.sh's whitespace split, two smuggled policy copies, a stale
base in the headline docstring, a figure the instrument cannot
print) — all fixed, all measured.

Suites: wonderboy 6,140 / kit 392 / hw 56; 13 modes x 2 ROMs green.
Remaining: M3 completion (the three endings + hand-back), then the
ladder is walked. Queued items carried.

events.title: engine: cache the command-button plates — the 68000 bar repaint 82 -> 23 ticks
events.message:
engine: cache the command-button plates — the 68000 bar repaint 82 -> 23 ticks

The command bar cost 82-104 ticks (1.4-1.7 s) per repaint on STE/ECS
against 3-5 on the 020s (#138), after every event modal. #138-#141 had
proven the repaint redundant (FRUA_BARDAMAGE: 0 px changed, three times)
and run the "why is it repainted" question to ground; this closes the
"make the paint cheap" half. jt137 msg 1 rebuilt each word's plate from
FRAME.CTL glyph pieces — left cap, rec[24] middles, right cap, label,
hotkey letter — through the per-pixel l309c -> l2d4e path, for pixels
that never change.

A 16-slot plate cache in jt137's colour paint arm. A miss paints normally
while unioning the rects l309c lands (g_lc_*), then captures that rect
from the chunky surface — exactly what the paint produced, label and
hotkey included. A hit at the same (top,left) with the same label, width
and paint-state bits replays the bytes and stamps them the way l309c's
tail does (planar_viewport_overwrite + qd_planar_bridge_rect +
qd_touch_rows), so the ST/ECS draw-time plane writers see it. B&W keeps
its own path. -DFRUA_NOPLATECACHE is the A/B arm.

Measured on STE with FRUA_BARPROF, A/B on one fixture drive: the 13-item
post-modal repaint 82-90 tk -> 22-24 tk (-72%, 1.4 s -> 0.4 s), 6 plate
hits per repaint once warm, cold entry composes unchanged, and the two
arms' final screenshots are BYTE-IDENTICAL — the replay is pixel-exact on
the planar build. Falcon walks into the same event modal and renders it
correctly.

events.title: amiga: Mac tempo on every vblank rate, and the needle bump was ring-cursor drift
events.message:
amiga: Mac tempo on every vblank rate, and the needle bump was ring-cursor drift

Two music fixes, both user-heard and user-verified:

1. TEMPO. The Mac VBL sound task counts sixty ticks a second; a PAL
   vblank delivers fifty, so every tune played 17% slow (the Mac tempo
   was only ever right on NTSC by accident). Classic fix: accumulate
   60 per vblank against ExecBase->VBlankFrequency — PAL runs the
   sequencer twice on every 5th vblank, NTSC exactly once. Verified by
   note-onset density: 1.27x against the old take (1.20 expected).

2. THE "VINYL NEEDLE BUMP". The ring model advanced the play cursor by
   FRAME_SAMPLES = 454 per call, but real PAL Paula at period 156
   consumes 227.5 CCK/line x 312.5 lines / 156 = 455.73 samples per
   frame. Under-counting ~86 samples/s, the modeled write head lapped
   the real DMA read head about 21 seconds after ring start and Paula
   replayed ~80ms of stale ring — one audible bump at a FIXED WALL
   TIME. The giveaway was the tempo fix itself: the bump moved to a
   LATER point in the tune, which no music-tied artifact can do. The
   cursor now advances in 24.8 fixed point at the exact rate (PAL
   116667/256, NTSC 98000/256 per vblank), scaled by elapsed CIA-A TOD
   ticks so a missed vblank cannot skew the model either. Bump gone by
   ear on the re-recorded boot.

events.title: wonderboy/joust: batch 43 phase D — M5, and a sibling defect measured
events.message:
wonderboy/joust: batch 43 phase D — M5, and a sibling defect measured

M5 LANDS: at the four M2 anchors, twenty registers of the machine
itself — the sixteen shifter pens, resolution, sync, refresh, and
V-overscan — are identical on both sides, captured by the same
debugger commands and parsed by the same code each side, anchored on
the address the binary reports about itself. The YM file is captured
and printed but NOT compared, for measured reasons (vecnoise: five
registers move between two boots of the shipped binary alone). The
rendered picture is byte-identical at all four anchors on both ROMs,
after the round's find: Hatari's drive LED in the border pushes the
PNG from palette to truecolour — --drive-led off, and the bound
measured by same-side repeat runs.

THE FLASH SURVIVOR DIES: the single raiser censused to $1328
(player_weapon_fire's LIGHTNING arm — the mode-shaped EA sweep
self-tested by re-finding 226/226 (d16,PC) operands, and it caught a
reader undercount at $6ee), unreachable in the window twice over, so
WB_FLASH_TIMER is seeded as a DECLARED FABRICATION with the writer's
own operand on both sides at the same instant — and the fabrication
is ASSERTED ARMED (a two-sided differential cannot see a fault that
hits both sides; zeroing the seed must fail the mode). The arm-swap
mutant dead at both arms; the order-only sink mutant reassigned to
M6 with trigger + home.

Controls both directions: m5fault (one pen corrupted, divergence
asserted to be that pen and nothing else), m5skew (the complement;
every surface fails in at least one control, the picture in both).

THE SIBLING MEASUREMENT: Joust's five non-reproducible deep anchors
were re-measured under the fixed settings — the drift is a different
effect (registered at Joust's surfaces with trigger + home), but THE
LED WAS IN JOUST'S PICTURES THE WHOLE TIME, including the one frame
its compare asserts, silently certified because both sides carried
it alike. Removing the chrome made the pen-fault surface STRICTLY
MORE sensitive (a palette-mode PNG's PLTE chunk IS the pens,
verified byte for byte) — Joust's control reclassified, its three
stale framediff PRGs rebuilt (pre-existing freshness refusal), all
five Joust smokes green.

Gates: the author's nine (incl. the two-sided blind spot and the
fault_pen parser gap) + the independent five (the retired scrape
still taught by a comment; the unmeasured causal sentence replaced
by the measurement above; two+two self-quoting retractions — four
in one phase, now written into the canon line itself; the census
license narrowed to its evidence then the evidence widened to the
license; a garbled verdict line).

Suites: wonderboy 6,140 / kit 392 / hw 56; nine Wonder Boy modes +
five Joust smokes green, both ROMs. Remaining on the ladder: M3's
exits + joystick (interactive), M6 the ordered write timeline —
then the play build.
