events.title: wonderboy/atari: batch 36 — six clean monsters, and the grep-to-zero rule
events.message:
wonderboy/atari: batch 36 — six clean monsters, and the grep-to-zero rule

Slots 14-19 ($35d8..$4118, 1,940 B, all CLEAN — the family's first block
with no boundary): the escort-dropping patroller whose retry sits below
the failed-allocation branch; the turn-and-hop walker (list chosen
BEFORE the turn, where slot 14's is after — pinned per slot); the
lobbing hopper whose bclr is test and write at once; the drifter on two
GLOBAL cursors whose 1-in-8 draw seeds five records numbered 5 to 1
(the y table is HALF the x one, so the burst fires twice per horizontal
figure); the charger that saves its whole flag byte across the charge;
and the two-phase glider that PUBLISHES THE RECORD IT JUST ALLOCATED as
a sprite — an original defect, reproduced both-armed (offset $14 of the
new record, or the vector page's word on a full pool) and generalised
into docs/m68k-disassembly.md. 43 of 62 rows live; verified 249 /
30,456 B (68.8%); suite 4670 -> 4812. The plate was the cheap authority
six for six. Two inbound edges from unported rows (slot 24's bra.w into
the seed burst, slot 25 borrowing slot 18's rts) are pinned and
cross-referenced in the OWNERS' plates so batch 37 reuses instead of
re-porting.

THE GATE'S FIND: the batch's own plate-fix pass failed silently — the
ledger certified four corrections of which one landed, one landed
transposed, two never landed (a scripted replace asserting only "text
changed" met a pattern that matched nothing). The rule that fixes the
class, now in docs/methodology.md and applied here with proof: A PLATE
CORRECTION IS LANDED WHEN THE OLD PHRASE GREPS TO ZERO — assert each
replacement individually, and never let a retraction quote the
retracted phrase. The tree-wide grep immediately caught a rename miss
no new-name grep could find. Also fixed under it: slot 19 documented
as irreversibly attacking on four surfaces while the bytes (and its
own test) return it to the glide; the spawner family rule that
contradicted the durable doc written from the same defect; and the
sibling-table over-read ambiguity — reconciled from the image to five
of thirteen rows, then CLOSED with three-way discriminating cursors
(raw vs masked-same vs masked-sibling), 8/8 composite mutants caught.

Queued: slots 20-27 close the family (extents in their plates), then

wonderboy/atari: the pkill-eats-its-own-shell variant, recorded

Batch 35's post-mortem produced a third self-inflicted diagnostic
variant beside the killed-sweep .so and the mutating reviewer: a
`pkill -f "<pattern>"` whose pattern appears in its own shell's command
line kills that shell mid-diagnosis, and the next check runs against a
state nobody established — a healthy, already-committed tree was read
as total loss twice before the cause was found. The rule joins mode
4's guard block in the README: pkill patterns must exclude the
invoking shell (pgrep | grep -v $$, or match the interpreter path),
never a string the command itself carries.

events.title: wonderboy/atari: batch 35 — the monster family opens, and the mask is not a bound
events.message:
wonderboy/atari: batch 35 — the monster family opens, and the mask is not a bound

Slots 9-13 ($2e12/$303a/$3218/$33bc/$34d2) + actor_random_facing_hop
($2f46): 1,310 bytes, 37 of 62 rows live; verified 243 / 28,516 B
(64.4%); suite 4558 -> 4670. Slot 9's nominal 552 bytes were 152 — the
gap is six shared leaves, five already ported: a dispatch table gives
entry points, not extents, and the per-slot plates' decoded extents
were byte-exact all along (the cheap authority; difference-of-entries
is data). Behaviourally: 9 walks then randomly hops (stepping on the
OLD facing, publishing the NEW); 10 is a flier closing on the player's
y once per 32-frame hover cycle, never probing the map; 11 spends one
rng word on a facing AND a hop, publishing nothing that frame; 12
chases with its animation picked by the SUPPORTED bit; 13 hops every
supported frame and its throe is the family's one unconditional
defeat.

THE GATE'S FIND OF THE BATCH: every frame read in the family indexes
its table with the RAW cursor byte — the andi lands only on the value
stored back — and three surfaces asserted the inverse ("the cursor is
masked, so nothing can reach past"). The C was faithful; the claim
invited the cleanup that would break it. Four seeded over-index cases
now pin what the raw read actually fetches (slot 13 publishes slot
14's OPCODES as a frame word at cursor $20; the hover adds slot 11's
entry instruction to its y), nine mask-order mutants all caught, and
the "unreachable" duplicate blocks are re-derived as what they are:
reachable-but-identical padding. docs/methodology.md's census recipe
is rewritten to stop teaching the trap — a direct-reader census bounds
direct readers; a block beside an indexed table needs the index's
provable range pinned separately (batch 28's wall, one mode over).

Process, now in the durable docs: a killed sweep leaves the mutant .so
beside restored sources — relink before the green check; and A
REVIEWER THAT MUTATES IS A WRITER — give it a copy or a named backup,
re-verify by NAME (a diff looks identical whether an edit is missing
or was never made; this batch lost a dedup to exactly that, silently).

A bare byte count says nothing about the shape of the sprite it holds.
Write each pixel_t array's size as width * mask * height * entries, the

bytes are laid out.

in row-pairs, which is the blitter's loop count rather than the number of
rows present, and gave glyphs 24-27 and 103-114 a width of 6 or 7 bytes.

blit_width6 and blit_width7 draw 2 and 1 bytes respectively, as the

events.message:
wonderboy/atari: batch 33 closes — the BCD extend chain carries

The four packed-BCD accumulators take the extend bit as an argument and
return their carry-out; nothing in the original clears X on entry, so
the caller's X is an input the old interface could not carry. Both
recorded chains proven live before fixing: the case written first went
RED against the unfixed C, off by one in exactly the predicted byte
(slot 28's counter at $9996 carrying into the score; the payout draw
carrying into the counter at award $0096). The kit cannot set an entry
CCR, so the chains are pinned at caller level — the carry produced
inside the run, folded by the oracle, matched by the port.

The independent gate then caught the fix's own blind spot: $6c26 was
mis-filed as an entry-CCR case, but the `lsl.w #2,d2` that leaves
spawn-type bit 14 in X runs INSIDE actor_defeat_and_score — the oracle
produces the carry itself, and the hard-coded clear diverged (proven
red at $4000/$ffff seeds; the old seed-refusal had excluded exactly the
exposing type on a premise the template table cannot support — it has
no shipped bytes). The bit now threads, the refusal is gone, and the
sbcd "equivalent" survivors turned out to be coverage holes: borrow-in
and borrow-out are pinned model-side (leaf.run_candidate_only), sweep

Every call site carries its reading: three proved clear from the bytes,

constant — quantified by reading the caller chain: the assumption fails

events.title: Factor out constants duplicated across the facade and its hosts
events.message:
Factor out constants duplicated across the facade and its hosts

Three values were defined independently in several places, each pair or
group of which has to agree:

- MAXSTAMPS (4), the depth of the stamp()/sleep() nesting, was defined
  four times: in the ZX facade, in the SDL host, as MAX_STAMPS in the
  RISC OS host and as FAKE_MAXSTAMPS in the unit tests. The facade's
  stack and each host's stack are pushed and popped in lockstep and both
  assert rather than grow, so a divergence would show up as a crash in
  one build only. It now lives in Spectrum.h with that contract
  documented.

- The 48K and 128K CPU clock rates were CHQ_CLOCK_48K/CHQ_CLOCK_128K in
  the RISC OS host, bare 3546900.0/3.5e6 literals in two SDL host
  ternaries, and CPU_HZ in a test. They are Spectrum facts, not host
  choices, so they become CPU_CLOCK_48K/CPU_CLOCK_128K in Spectrum.h.

- GAMEWIDTH/GAMEHEIGHT (256/192) in the SDL host duplicated
  SCREEN_WIDTH/SCREEN_HEIGHT from the Spectrum.h it already includes.
  The RISC OS host already used the header's names; the SDL host now

events.title: Fix sampled sound playing ~12x slow in the web build
events.message:
Fix sampled sound playing ~12x slow in the web build

The game thread's catch-up cap was expressed as a multiple of the sleep
the caller had just asked for:

    if (next_deadline < nowSecs - duration * maxLagFrames)
      next_deadline = nowSecs - duration * maxLagFrames;

That reads sensibly for the 20ms frame sleeps it was written against --
four frames, 80ms of catch-up -- but 'duration' is whatever the caller
passed. play_speech_128k asks for SPEECH_NIBBLE_TSTATES between nibbles,
447 T-states or 126us, which collapses the budget to 504us. Any stall
longer than that moved the deadline forward and discarded the debt, so
the game clock lost time it could never claw back.

Under emscripten the host clock's own granularity exceeds 504us, so
every tick bled time: measured with per-second counters, the game thread
emitted ~660 speech nibbles a second against the 7936 the nibble rate
implies, and the samples played back at about a twelfth of their pitch.

Cap the lag as an absolute span instead (CHQ_MAX_LAG_SECS, 0.08 --
the same 80ms the frame path always had, now independent of request
size), and skip waits too short for the host to time rather than
attempting them, leaving the debt on the deadline for the next call.

Also revert the sample-frames hint from 0b7cd90. Its premise was that
the ScriptProcessorNode was underrunning; the counters disproved that
(zero drops, zero dry samples, callbacks pulling the full device rate),
and it cost ~85ms of latency for nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Fix web build audio: main-thread starvation and needless resampling
events.message:
Fix web build audio: main-thread starvation and needless resampling

The Emscripten build played sound samples as a low chugging buzz, worse in
Chrome than Firefox. Four compounding causes, all downstream of one wrong
assumption: that SDL3's Emscripten audio backend runs the callback on its
own thread.

It does not. SDL_emscriptenaudio.c sets ProvidesOwnCallbackThread and drives
playback from a ScriptProcessorNode, so chq_audio_callback runs on the main
browser thread, interleaved with emscripten_set_main_loop's game and render
frame. Every long frame underruns the node.

- The SDL_HINT_AUDIO_DEVICE_SAMPLE_FRAMES "256" hint was asking for a
  smaller buffer to help a producer/consumer race that does not exist. The
  backend doubles the hint, so it gave a 512-frame node -- 10.7ms at 48kHz,
  on the thread that also renders. Ask for 2048 (4096 frames) instead;
  latency is the only cost.

- chq_apply_due_audio_events locked queue_mutex once per sample, i.e. 44kHz
  of lock traffic on the main browser thread, which cannot Atomics.wait and
  so spin-waits when the game Worker contends -- and it contends heavily
  during speech, at three AY writes per nibble. Hoist the lock to one
  acquisition per callback chunk.

- The backend forces the device to audioContext.sampleRate (48kHz on most
  Windows machines), so every callback resampled 44100 to 48000 on that same
  main thread. Query the opened device's rate, set the stream's source rate
  to match, and emulate the AY at that rate. The replay cursor counts sample
  periods in it too, otherwise it would advance at 44100 while the callback
  produced 48000 samples a second and slide events progressively late.

- AY_REPLAY_CUSHION_NS had been raised to 120ms to paper over the above. The
  cushion is also how long the chip holds its last state after the queue
  runs dry, so that turned each starve into a long low chug rather than a
  short click -- the buzz itself. Back down to 50ms.

Native behaviour is unchanged where the device already opens at 44100.

and the helper cluster $517a..$5207. 26 of 62 dispatch rows live.

events.title: input: stretch the TOS key-repeat delay, and add FRUA_KEYDIAG (#132)
events.message:
input: stretch the TOS key-repeat delay, and add FRUA_KEYDIAG (#132)

MEASURED baseline, which is the finding: TOS hands us Kbrate = 0x0F02 — a key
starts repeating after 15 ticks (0.3s) and then repeats every 2 ticks (25/sec).
That is desktop tuning. On an 8MHz machine where one FRUA repaint can take most
of a second, an ordinary keystroke can outlast 0.3s and emit a second character —
rare, unpredictable, and impossible to see under the test harness, where injected
keys press and release in ~0.1s. That last point is why this has historically
been blamed on the injector.

plat_input_init now asks for a 90-tick (~1.8s) delay and leaves the rate alone,
so a deliberate hold still repeats but a normal press cannot. The old value is
restored at shutdown (Kbrate returns delay in the high byte, rate in the low).
Atari-only: the Amiga has its own input layer.

FRUA_KEYDIAG (opt-in) traces a key through every layer it crosses —
plat_kb_poll (the lowest point a key enters the port), kb_to_event, the jt1125
and l6dd0 stamps, and the jt1133 read — so COUNTS separate "the key arrived
twice from below" from "we processed one key twice".

What it has already shown, in the char-gen name field:
- 15 consecutive keys: 15 polls / 15 events / 15 stamps / 15 reads. Clean.
- ONE anomalous run: 3 polls but 4 READS — an extra read with no key behind it,
  i.e. the engine delivered a stale -818 twice. Real, and NOT injector doubling
  (the poll count was correct).
Ruled out for that extra read: the l6dd0 path (it always sets -818 AND -820
together — line 25656 — and never fired here at all) and event-queue
duplication (queue_push is only used for mouse edges and PostEvent, never
keyDown).

So #132 is NOT closed: the Kbrate change addresses a real hardware-only
doubling mechanism, but the engine-side extra read is reproduced-once and
unexplained. Note when reading the trace that dbglog DEFERS lines written from
interrupt context, so the sequence can be reordered — trust the counts, not the
order.

469 passed, 6 skipped; 68000 / amiga-ECS both build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: engine: delete by erasing the cell, not by drawing a space (jt1078)
events.message:
engine: delete by erasing the cell, not by drawing a space (jt1078)

#131. Maintainer's read of the symptom was the key: "maybe it's only doing a
move left and not move-left-and-delete". That is precisely what the code could
do, because the erase was a PRINTED SPACE and the tail cleanup was the repaint's
single trailing space ("%s ") — both of which only erase if a space glyph paints
its BACKGROUND opaquely. Where it does not, the letter stays on screen, the next
keystroke lands on top of it, and the field reads as corrupted.

Deletion no longer rests on that assumption: the vacated cell (plus the old
cursor cell after it) is cleared with jt1161, a filled rect in the field's bg —
the same primitive this loop's own cursor block uses, so it cannot depend on
glyph rendering at all.

Both display modes in the report are the SAME Mega STe (Control at boot skips
AUTO for ST-Low; letting AUTO load the xVDI drivers gives the card), so a
backend-specific cause was never likely — a rendering assumption shared by both
fits far better.

Verified in Hatari (FRUA_CHARGEN drops straight into char-gen), and the rect is
checked not to over-erase: HELLO -> BS -> BS = "HEL" (prompt and remaining
letters intact), + P = "HELP" (typing after a delete is clean), then backspaced
to empty with one extra press at empty — field blank, "CHARACTER NAME:" prompt
undamaged.

Together with 3a36487a (the Atari DELETE key was a no-op) this should close #131
on hardware. 469 passed, 6 skipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: engine: the Atari DELETE key erases in text fields (jt1078)
events.message:
engine: the Atari DELETE key erases in text fields (jt1078)

#131, partial. The line editor's erase arm handled 8 and 262 only, so the Atari
DELETE key (0x7F) fell through to the printable-insert arm, where `key > 126`
just beeps. Measured in Hatari on the char-gen name prompt (FRUA_CHARGEN):
pressing Delete left the frame BYTE-IDENTICAL. After the fix "XY" + Delete -> "X".

Why the gap existed: on the Mac the key labelled "Del" IS backspace and arrives
as 8, so one case covered that keyboard. An Atari has two distinct keys —
Backspace 8, Delete 0x7F — and only the first was wired.

Noted in a comment while here: 262 is NOT a delete code in this port. jt1125
maps scancode 0x4b (LEFT ARROW) to 262, so Left is destructive in a text field.
Left, so as this editor has no cursor movement for it to do instead, but it is a
port artifact rather than the Mac's meaning.

NOT the whole of #131. The reported "backspace overwrites the letter and
corrupts the text" does NOT reproduce here: on ST-Low, Backspace deletes
correctly ("AABC" -> "AAB") and typing after it appends cleanly ("AABD"). The
erase depends on the repaint's trailing space painting an opaque background, and
that works on this backend; the machine/keypress for the corrupting case still
needs pinning down.

Also observed while testing, as evidence for #132: typing A, B, C produced
"AABC" — the first keystroke doubled, in the emulator, on the FIRST field entry.

469 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: platform: put the desktop's palette back on exit (ST/STE, ST-High, Nova)
events.message:
platform: put the desktop's palette back on exit (ST/STE, ST-High, Nova)

Reported on hardware: quitting from the ST-Low build AND the xVDI 640x400x256
build drops to a desktop with black icons and black window contents. The Falcon
backend has restored its palette for a while; the others never did.

Each backend saved the resolution and the screen bases and restored those, but
not the COLOURS — while owning the colour hardware outright for the whole run:
- display_ste.c: the per-band raster split rewrites all 16 registers at 0xFF8240
  several times a frame, so the desktop's palette is long gone by exit.
- display_sthigh.c: same omission (mono only lights 0 and 15, but this backend
  also runs on a colour monitor booted into ST High).
- display_nova.c: worse since we started writing the card's hardware LUT
  directly and re-stamping it every present — closing the VDI workstation does
  not undo that, so TOS inherits the game's 256 colours.

Fix, same shape everywhere: snapshot at init (Setcolor/COL_INQUIRE on the ST
side, a straight 256-entry read of the LUT on the card, taken BEFORE the first
write) and restore at shutdown. Palette goes back AFTER the mode change /
workstation close, matching the Falcon's default exit order — Setscreen can
reinitialise the VDI and its colour table, so the restore must have the last
word.

A/B'd in Hatari (--machine ste) rather than assumed, because "the desktop looked
fine afterwards" is not evidence on its own — a trap this repo already paid for.
With the restore disabled the reported bug reproduces exactly (near-black
desktop, black icons, unreadable window contents); with it in place the desktop
returns normal. The Nova arm is the same mechanism but is NOT emulator-testable,
so it stays unverified until the card says otherwise.

events.title: engine: restore the main-menu Quit confirm; strip the freeze instrumentation
events.message:
engine: restore the main-menu Quit confirm; strip the freeze instrumentation

#130 — QUIT FROM GAME dropped straight to the desktop, so a mis-click or a stray
'Q' lost the session with no warning. The Mac does confirm; the port had dropped
the arm. Faithful lift of CODE 22 + 0x5292:

  jsr JT[76]                   ; jt76()
  movel %a5@(-14292),%sp@-     ; the prompt string POINTER
  jsr JT[159]                  ; jt159(prompt, 0)
  tstb %d0 / beqs L52aa        ; NO  -> back to the menu loop
  moveq #0,%d0                 ; YES -> return 0 = quit

-14292 is read by exactly one instruction in the whole game and written by none,
i.e. a DATA-seeded pointer. It arrives seeded: measured live, it holds the Mac's
own wording "Quit Game? ", so no invented text is needed and the maintainer's
"Quit to TOS?" only exists as a fallback for an empty slot (PORT_QUIT_PROMPT,
Workbench on the Amiga) — the DOS release's "Quit to DOS?" would be a lie on a
machine that has neither.

Verified headlessly on the STE, both arms: the dialog paints "QUIT GAME? YES NO",
NO restores the full main menu and keeps running, YES still tears down
(ExitToShell). 68000 / 020 / amiga-ECS all build; 469 passed, 6 skipped.

Also strips the diagnostics that did their job:
- FRUA_FREEZELOG entirely (ua_main, l07dc, l120c, l23b4, nova appl_init/exit).
- The FRUA_NOVA_PALTRACE block in load_menu_ui.
- The "slot15 CLOBBERED" log: the VDI overwriting that slot is the EXPECTED
  steady state now, so it was noise every boot, not a signal. The unconditional
  re-stamp remains — that is the fix.
- nova_white_pen / the novawhite key, a knob born of a theory the LUT read-back
  disproved. Slot 15 is now never sent to vs_color at all (pen 1 addresses slot

proved the mechanism: slot 15 was found holding, in order, near-whites
(0xFFF9/0xFFEF/0xFFF7), a grey (0xCE99), the VDI magenta default (0xFABF) and
finally 0x0000 BLACK — i.e. the VDI really does re-emit its colour table over
ours, and the per-present re-assert is what keeps the UI white on screen.

Writes up the whole path: the pen-1/slot-255 root cause, the LUT address derived
from Logbase() (never probed — the 4MB offset bombs a 2MB card), the RGB565
format decoded from a read-back rather than assumed from the manual's 15bpp pixel
layout, why one write is not enough, and the video.cfg keys.

Records the two maintainer observations that cracked it, each of which killed a
theory of mine: "the PRESSED button has the right colours" (localized it to one
slot) and "the sprite page turns them CYAN, not white" (there was never an
unlock — that page just draws the pressed style).

events.title: nova: assert the hardware LUT last, and once per present
events.message:
nova: assert the hardware LUT last, and once per present

Field result on the card: with the direct LUT write the hotkey letters now come
up WHITE (so index 15 does reach the card) but go black a moment later. Two
corrections to the earlier reading, both from the maintainer:
  - the char-gen page turns the letters CYAN, not white, so it never "unlocked"
    anything — that page just draws them in the pressed style (clut 11);
  - the letters change back on their own, i.e. something re-emits over us.

Not `dim`: a dimmed item draws BODY=0 too (the whole label would go black), and
the label body stays grey. So the letter really is index 15 and slot 15 is being
lost after we set it.

Two changes:
1. Assert the LUT AFTER the batch's vs_color calls, not inline. Writing LUT[15]
   at i=15 and then calling vs_color for 16..32 let the VDI re-emit its table
   (where slot 15 is black) microseconds later — self-inflicted, in the same
   loop. nova_lut_assert() also re-stamps EVERY slot ever set, so a re-emit
   triggered by an unrelated range cannot leave an older slot wrong.
2. Assert once per full present, so any VDI re-emit between palette installs is
   corrected within a frame rather than persisting.

Also added a bounded (8-line) check kept in the SHIPPING build: if slot 15 is
found holding anything but the white we last wrote, log it. That distinguishes
the two mechanisms that look identical on screen — a CLUT clobber (log fires,
and these changes fix it) versus an engine-side repaint with a different index
(log silent, palette innocent, look at the draw path instead).

Nova-only; ST/STE boot re-verified. Filed the missing main-menu Quit confirm
("Quit to DOS YES|NO?", maintainer suggests "Quit to TOS?" on Atari) as a task.

events.title: Identify demo engine routines that differ from retail only by address literal
events.message:
Identify demo engine routines that differ from retail only by address literal

47 of the remaining "not yet identified" $8000+ engine gaps turned out
to be the same routine as retail, byte-identical except for one
embedded 16-bit address operand (a data table living at a different
offset in this build's memory layout) - which is why the earlier
straight byte-diff missed them.

Found via masked comparison: disassemble the gap, wildcard the 16-bit
operand bytes of any instruction whose disassembly contains an
address, then search retail memory for a match on the unmasked bytes.
Any hit is safe by construction - the search can only succeed if every
non-operand byte already matches, so a match can't be a coincidence on
short/generic sequences.

events.title: nova: own the hardware LUT (RGB565) — fixes the black hotkey letters
events.message:
nova: own the hardware LUT (RGB565) — fixes the black hotkey letters

MEASURED on the card (read-back of the ATW800/2 FPGA LUT, per the Programmer's
Manual the maintainer pointed at):

  Logbase()       = 0xFEA00000   card video base (ADDR jumper at 0x(FE)A00000)
  LUT             = base+0x1FF000 = 0xFEBFF000   reads fine
  base+0x3FF000   = 0xFEDFF000                  BUS ERROR on a 2MB card

  slot   7 = 0xAD55 -> (172,170,172)   the alternating-bit 565 grey
  slot 254 = 0xFFE0 -> (255,255,0)     yellow
  slot  15 = 0xF81F -> (255,0,255)     magenta  <- never got the UI white
  slot 255 = 0xFFFF -> (255,255,255)   WHITE    <- where the UI white went

Root cause: nova_hw_inverse is the 16-COLOUR VDI pen->register table, in which
register 15 is reached by pen 1. On a 256-colour device pen 1 is black = index
ncolors-1 = 255, so every UI-white write (14 per session, always 0xFFFFFF) landed
on slot 255 — leaving the accelerator letter on UNPRESSED buttons wrong (the
reporter's "black hotkey") AND clobbering a live art colour. Slot 11 -> pen 14
works, which is why PRESSED buttons showed their cyan correctly; that asymmetry
in the field report is what localized it. Engine side was blameless: values and
ordering verified correct on the ST backend (the UI palette installs LAST, after
both clut-129 installs, with the right cyan/white).

Fix: bind the card's hardware LUT and write it directly — index == slot, so all
256 entries are reachable and the pen table's unreachable slots are gone. Entry
format RGB565 big-endian, decoded from the read-back against known colours (not
assumed from the manual's 15bpp PIXEL layout). vs_color is still called for
idx != 15 so VDI's own CLUT shadow stays in step for any VDI/AES redraw; slot 15
no longer writes pen 1 at all, ending the slot-255 corruption.

Safety: the offset is DERIVED from Logbase() and verified by write/read-back/
restore, never probed speculatively — the diagnostic build's blind 4MB candidate
read bombed a 2MB card (2 bombs, crash to desktop; my error). video.cfg keys:
novalut=off (back to vs_color only), novalut=4mb (4MB cards). Falls back silently
if the read-back fails. Nova-only; ST/STE boot re-verified unchanged.

This is a plain shipping build — no diagnostic flags needed.

events.title: diag+nova: measure where the UI white lands — read the ATW800/2 hardware LUT
events.message:
diag+nova: measure where the UI white lands — read the ATW800/2 hardware LUT

The card log settled the black-hotkey symptom to ONE slot. Slot 15 (the UI white
= the accelerator letter on an UNPRESSED button) is written 14x per session,
always 0xFFFFFF, always through vs_color PEN 1 — and never shows. Slot 11 (pen
14) works, which is why PRESSED buttons show their cyan accelerator. Values and
ordering are correct (verified engine-side on the ST backend), so only this pen
fails.

Why: nova_hw_inverse is the standard 16-COLOUR VDI pen->register table, where
register 15 is reached by pen 1. But pen 1 is VDI's BLACK, and on a 256-COLOUR
device black is index ncolors-1 = 255. So the white most likely lands on slot 255
and slot 15 keeps whatever the art palette left there. PALTEST derived the table
from pens 2/3/6 (-> slots 1/2/3) and never exercised pen 1.

Rather than guess a replacement pen (a wrong one silently corrupts another UI
colour — pen 15 drives slot 13), measure. Per the ATW800/2 Programmer's Manual
(maintainer's pointer) the FPGA LUT is memory-mapped READ/WRITE at
screen_adr + 0xFF000 (+1MB for a 2MB card, +3MB for 4MB; the manual's absolute
Mega ST/STE/TT addresses are the 2MB case), 0x200 bytes = 256 16-bit entries.

Added: a Supexec LUT read-back dumping slots 0/1/7/11/13/15/254/255 for both the
2MB and 4MB candidate bases, fired right after the 1st and one later slot-15
write. That answers both open questions at once — WHERE the white landed (15 vs
255) and the ENTRY FORMAT (slot 11 is a known-RGB sample, so the raw word decodes
the encoding; the manual documents only the 15bpp PIXEL layout and assuming the
LUT matches would be a guess).

Also: novawhite=<pen> in video.cfg overrides the slot-15 pen, so alternatives can
be A/B'd on hardware without a rebuild. Read-only probe; no write path changed.

events.title: diag: trace the UI text CLUT slots (Nova black-hotkey report)
events.message:
diag: trace the UI text CLUT slots (Nova black-hotkey report)

Field report: on the Nova the menu hotkey letters are BLACK until the char-gen
sprite page loads, then correct for the rest of the session. The letters paint
with FIXED clut indices (11 cyan / 15 white — the l6c2a label draw), not a
nearest-match, so black means slots 11/15 held black when the menu painted.

Measured locally (STE, so the engine side is machine-independent) and it
ELIMINATES the ordering theory:
  main: clut 129 installed, entries = 256      <- the 256-entry art palette
  main: clut 129 installed, entries = 256         (documented to clobber 1/7/11/12/15)
  paltrace: UI palette install entries = 33    <- UI palette lands AFTER them
    menu_pal[11] cyan  rgb = 0x67FFFF          <- correct value
    menu_pal[15] white rgb = 0xFFFFFF
  menu: modal up
i.e. the engine writes the right cyan/white to 11/15, last, before the menu is
up. So the remaining suspect is the Nova pen mapping (nova_hw_inverse) — the one
thing in display_nova.c that can only be validated on the card.

Trace changes: log every UI-palette install (engine side, with the 11/15 RGB),
and in nova_set_palette log each write to slot 11/15 WITH the vs_color pen it is
routed to. Budget raised 80 -> 400 lines and narrowed from "all idx<16" to just
11/15, because the old bound was exhausted during boot and never reached the
char-gen install that "unlocks" the colour. One card run then distinguishes:
same rgb+pen written again at char-gen (=> mapping/timing) vs different values
(=> engine gating).

events.title: fix: Exit-From-Play freeze — jt574 must restore -27932 on every create exit
events.message:
fix: Exit-From-Play freeze — jt574 must restore -27932 on every create exit

Hardware DBG.LOG (Nova card, P->C->D->E->E) pinned it: the l07dc cleanup
`while (g_a5_27932 != 0) jt19(0,1)` spun forever (counter climbed past 188),
with 27928(party)=0 and 27932=cg_rec (the static char-gen buffer, 0x1c37c0).

Root cause in jt574 (Create Character): l3666's Done sets -27932 to the temporary
cg_rec so the stat sheet / name / review operate on it, but the restore
`-27932 = -27928` lived ONLY on the full-commit pool-add path (inside
`if (cg_pool_count < 16)`). Every cancel — sheet Exit (the user's first E),
body-icon review cancel, "Save NAME?" declined — and a full 16-char pool
returned with -27932 still dangling at cg_rec. jt19 is faithful (the Mac's
L2d8a also just rts when -27928==0), so it never clears a selection that isn't
in the party list -> the drain loop never terminates -> hard freeze. The Mac's
jt574 tail restores -27932 on every exit; the port didn't.

Fix:
- jt574: route all create-cancel returns through a cg_done label that restores
  -27932 = -27928, and move the commit-path restore out of the pool-count guard
  so it runs on every exit.
- l07dc cleanup: add a no-progress guard (if jt19 leaves -27932 unchanged, drop
  it and break) so any future dangling selection degrades to a dropped pointer
  instead of a machine-hard-freeze.

Display-independent (not Nova-specific); the FRUA_NOVA correlation was
incidental — the merge only changed which builds reach this Hall path in
testing. Instrumentation (FRUA_FREEZELOG) retained, inert in shipping, pending
a hardware confirm of the fix.

events.title: wonderboy/atari: batch 29 — the behaviour tier's foundation
events.message:
wonderboy/atari: batch 29 — the behaviour tier's foundation

Reconstruction: 20 routines / 1,266 B into new src/behavior.c — the
per-frame walk (actor_behavior_pass $8d0), the four-instruction
dispatcher ($928), the 62-entry table, the spawn animation ($698a —
the plate said vanish; the bytes say SPAWN, bit 2's two operand sites
prove it), the 13 shared leaves, and the three high-fan-in FUN_*s named
from the bytes: actor_followed_overlap_mask (42 callers),
actor_hop_ascend_step (36, not the scout's 29), actor_hit_by_player_shot
(25). Verified 196 / 22,290 B — 50.4% of the honest denominator, the
first port batch priced against it.

The dispatcher FETCHES the table longword through the bus guard (not a
compile-time copy) and its boundary is keyed by ADDRESS: ported targets
run and report DISPATCH_RAN; unported ones return their address and the
differential runs the oracle to a stop_pc there with a cov_visited
witness on the jmp — one row flips per future batch. The wrapped-offset
lesson applied at design time: 248 of 65,536 types dispatch (a raw
guard would have refused 186), enumerated in 8 shardable chunks + three
alias-band differentials.

Tests: 4019 green (+425, all in the new test_behavior.py). Sweep 43
mutants / 42 caught / 1 equivalent — and it caught a transferable
gotcha: A KILLED SWEEP LEAVES ITS MUTANT BEHIND (the suite ran 3977
green on a wrong wrap mask until the restore was noticed).

Review (5 reviewers, findings applied + mutation-verified): writes now
go through the bus guard (bus.h gained bus_write_byte/word — read-only
guarding was worse than none), the runaway got its own code
(DISPATCH_UNBOUNDED, unreachable by construction and stated as a case),

events.title: diag: FRUA_FREEZELOG drills into l23b4 — the Exit-From-Play modal spin loop
events.message:
diag: FRUA_FREEZELOG drills into l23b4 — the Exit-From-Play modal spin loop

The Nova log pinned the hang at l120c "pre jt159" — i.e. inside jt159 -> jt182 ->
l23b4, the yes/no ("QUIT ANYWAY?") modal loop. l23b4 is a for(;;) that exits only
when l2d3e() returns a selection >= 0, so a freeze here is either a spin
(l2d3e never selects) or a call inside the loop that never returns.

Instruments it to tell those apart:
- ENTRY: DLItem count (g_a5_9250 — were the YES/NO buttons installed?), dialog
  mode (13018), and the present-gate booleans (jt1163/jt1200/27990 — does the
  loop ever push the dialog to the card?).
- a sparse spin heartbeat (first 4 iters + every 30000th) with l2d3e's return:
  a climbing "spin #" = spinning on l2d3e (no selection); stuck at 0/1 = hung
  inside jt1067/port_cycle_present/l2d3e (a Nova-backend call that never
  returns). EXIT logs the winning item.

events.title: docs: Exit-from-Play freeze reproduced headlessly — suspect is -DFRUA_NOVA, not the gate
events.message:
docs: Exit-from-Play freeze reproduced headlessly — suspect is -DFRUA_NOVA, not the gate

Reproduced P->C->D->E->E in Hatari STE (= card-less ST-Low): the machine hangs
after EXIT-FROM-PLAY when the path went through CREATE->char-detail (l618c).
Verified a genuine freeze (game-drawn cursor frozen, 3 identical frames,
clicks+keys ignored, Hatari process still alive = CPU spinning).

Findings:
- jt178 shape-5 cells (c3332ed5) EXONERATED: the path never clicks MODIFY, so
  they are never installed; also predates the merge.
- The l2d3e gate-revert (b89efa29) is DISPROVEN: that very build still freezes.
  It is not the fix (the restoration is harmless/faithful, but the "freeze
  suspect" framing was wrong).
- Quit-to-desktop teardown does NOT freeze in either build; the hang is specific
  to "Exit from Play -> main menu" after the char-creation path.
- Leading suspect is -DFRUA_NOVA (7e4d74b7), the merge's ONLY functional change:
  it runs a boot-time dsp_backend_nova() probe that calls appl_init (AES) on a
  GEMDOS PRG, which the pre-merge ST-Low never did. Explains both Nova-mode and
  ST-Low regressing at the same point.

Definitive next step: DBG.LOG from a real freeze (file-based dbg_file markers on
the boot probe + play->menu teardown) to pinpoint the hang location.

events.title: engine: restore the l2d3e iy>=8000 hit-test gate (redundant removal; freeze suspect)
events.message:
engine: restore the l2d3e iy>=8000 hit-test gate (redundant removal; freeze suspect)

7898113a removed l2d3e's `iy >= 8000` hit-test gate to make the modify-char
stat rows clickable. But the REAL fix landed separately (c3332ed5): those rows
are installed as shape-5 cells at 8000-space y (8036..8056), so they pass the
gate anyway. The removal was therefore redundant — and it changed click
hit-testing on EVERY screen, which is the leading suspect for the reported
post-create "Exit from Play" freeze (create a character -> through the MODIFY
screen -> back to the Hall -> Exit from Play hangs).

Restoring the gate returns the known-good pre-2026-08-10 behaviour on every
screen while keeping the modify stat-click intact — verified live: clicking DEX
then INT still maps to act 3 / act 1 and the DEX selection persists (cur stat 3
on the second click). The two are independent.

HONEST STATUS: this is a suspected fix, not a confirmed one. The freeze repros
only on hardware; the headless harness cannot commit Exit-from-Play at ANY
commit (it shows the same stuck-highlight state on 12ad1063, before all recent
work), so I could not bisect or confirm the cause here. Restoring the gate is
justified on its own merits (it was redundant and non-faithful), and it is the
change most likely to have caused a regression on the click path; hardware
verification is needed. The faithful no-gate form is worth revisiting once the
offending absolute-coord item/method can actually be reproduced.

469 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: Port CRT shader to Emscripten via raw GLES2, fix F4 double-toggle and OSD alpha
events.message:
Port CRT shader to Emscripten via raw GLES2, fix F4 double-toggle and OSD alpha

SDL3 has no stable WebGPU backend, so the web build renders the CRT
post-effect through a raw GL context (WebGL1/GLES2) instead of SDL_GPU,
mirroring the Metal/Vulkan backends behind the same opaque API.

Emscripten backs every SDL_Window with the same canvas, so the
recreate-window workaround used to dodge the Linux stuck-swapchain bug
left the GLES path with no live GL context on the second F4 press
(display going blank); it now just re-creates the GL context on the
existing window instead.

Also fixes the OSD green-interior colour constant, which packed alpha
as 0x00: harmless on the SDL_GPU swapchain paths, but on Emscripten the
canvas alpha channel composites with the page background, rendering the
OSD text black instead of green.

- chq_dispatch_events read event.window.windowID for every event type,

  and read the correct field per kind instead.

  input into 0. Add chq_parse_int (strtol-based) to reject non-numeric
  values explicitly.
- Error paths in main() returned without tearing down already-created
  instances or calling SDL_Quit. Add chq_shutdown_all and use it on
  every exit path.

events.title: Fix window cascade offset: arithmetic on SDL_WINDOWPOS_UNDEFINED corrupts it
events.message:
Fix window cascade offset: arithmetic on SDL_WINDOWPOS_UNDEFINED corrupts it

SDL_WINDOWPOS_UNDEFINED is a magic encoded value (0x1FFF0000 | display
index), not a coordinate -- adding index*40 to it corrupted the encoding
instead of offsetting the position, so every two-up window landed centred
regardless of index. Read back the real position SDL assigned after
creation and offset from that instead.

events.title: Share the loading-screen wait across two-up instances instead of serialising it
events.message:
Share the loading-screen wait across two-up instances instead of serialising it

Each instance held the splash for LOADING_SCREEN_DURATION_MS before the next
one was even created, so -n instances paid N times the startup delay for no
reason -- the wait doesn't depend on anything instance-specific. Split
chq_instance_create (window/audio/splash bitmap) from a new
chq_instance_launch_game (game thread start), and hold the splash once in
main() across every instance's window before any of them launch.

An instance that quits during the shared wait never launches a game thread,
so chq_instance_destroy now skips the game teardown calls for it instead of
dereferencing a NULL game/game_thread.

events.title: Add multi-instance (-n), -quiet, -scale options to SDL3 app for two-up testing
events.message:
Add multi-instance (-n), -quiet, -scale options to SDL3 app for two-up testing

Runs N concurrent game instances from one process to smoke-test for static
data trampling between them (audit found none: engine/library layers have
no mutable statics). Each instance owns its own chq_sdl_state_t, window and
game thread.

Fixes along the way:
- SDL_PollEvent drains one process-wide queue; polling it per-instance let
  one instance steal another's input. Events are now pumped once per frame
  and dispatched to the owning window by windowID.
- An instance's window stayed open after its close button was clicked,
  because teardown only ran once every instance had quit. Each instance now
  tears down as soon as its own quit flag fires, tracked via a new
  CHQ_FLAG_CLOSED bit rather than a side array.

events.title: build: `make atari-binaries` -> FRUA.PRG (68000) + FRUA_020.PRG (020)
events.message:
build: `make atari-binaries` -> FRUA.PRG (68000) + FRUA_020.PRG (020)

Two shipping Atari binaries, both with the Nova backend built in:
  FRUA.PRG      68000 codegen — runs on EVERY Atari (ST/STE/Mega STe/TT/Falcon),
                the safe universal build.
  FRUA_020.PRG  -m68020-60 codegen — Falcon030/TT030 only, faster (32-bit
                muls/divs + bitfield ops). The original Mac was pure 68000 THINK
                C, so this is codegen we ADDED; a 68000 machine cannot run it.

The CPU68K value is in the BUILDSTAMP, so each sub-make fully rebuilds on the
switch — two clean compiles, never a mix (the illegal-instruction death that
bit us on 2026-07-15). The target integrity-checks the 68000 binary in place:
it fails the build if any real-code 020 op survives (the ~10 phantom
bfextu/bfins are const lookup tables GCC parks in .text, excluded per CLAUDE.md).

Verified: FRUA.PRG md5 = the consolidated 68000 build (Nova + the modify stat-
click fix); FRUA_020.PRG carries genuine 020 codegen (2223 muls.l/bfextu/bfins
in boot.o). Both gitignored as build artifacts.

The maintainer accepted two binaries over a fat/CPU-detecting single binary (a
runtime codegen switch would mean two copies of the hot loops plus trampolines —
not worth it vs two named PRGs).

Ports jt178's gated shape-5 install block (CODE 7 0x288a..0x2976), which our
lift had stubbed as "the shape-5 jt452 button bar for mouse clicks is a TODO" —
the reason the Modify screen's stat rows were mouse-dead while the keyboard
command bar worked. The maintainer confirmed the feature IS in Mac 1.0
(BasiliskII) and it is byte-identical in 1.2, so this is a faithful wiring fix,
not a version cherry-pick.

When g_a5_-12911 is set (it is, on this screen), jt178 now streams eight shape-5
cells through jt452: six over the ability rows (8000-space y = 8036/8040/8044/
8048/8052/8056 = STR..CHA, 4 apart), one at 8004 (name), one at (8012,8080)
(HP), each x=8000 rec22=4 rec24=80 with rec[28] bit 4 set (commit-on-click);
jt180() adds bit 1 to the name cell. Shape 5 -> method jt378, the same list-cell
hit-test the treasure / character-select screens use — which was the
maintainer's lead.

shape-5), a click on the DEX row hits its cell (iy 8048), l25b6 maps it to act=3
(DEX = stat index 3), move-pending is set, l4d64(3) selects it, and a follow-up
click on INT reports cur stat 3 first — proving the DEX selection persisted. Two
assumptions from the trace were wrong and are noted: -6927 is NOT always 0 (the
commit path sets it), and the cells DO hit-test once present.

events.title: engine: hit-test every DLItem, not just 8000-space ones (modify-char mouse)
events.message:
engine: hit-test every DLItem, not just 8000-space ones (modify-char mouse)

l2d3e's click loop gated the per-item hit-test on `iy >= 8000`, so every
ABSOLUTE-coordinate item (rec16 < 8000) was dropped before its method ran. The
8000-space screens — the icon grid, the Hall — worked; any screen laid out in
absolute pixels was mouse-DEAD. That is the shape of the reported bug: the
modify-character sub-screens are mouse-unresponsive while keyboard accelerators
work.

The gate is not faithful. CODE 3 L2d3e's loop (0x2d84..0x2dac) pushes
(item, cmd=2, cy, cx) and `jsr (a0)` UNCONDITIONALLY — there is no
coordinate-space guard in the Mac. The method scopes the test itself: jt137
msg 2 handles both spaces (jt1135 passes values <=6000 through unchanged), and
a non-clickable item computes a rect the click simply isn't inside, so removing
the gate cannot manufacture a spurious hit. The `hm != NULL` check stays — that
is a PORT-SAFETY guard (the Mac would fault on a null method), not a behaviour.

How this was found: FRUA_CLICKDIAG now logs jt137's paint-y beside its msg-2
rect, in one coordinate space. That KILLED the previous theory — the DONE
plate paints at y=188, inside its hit rect [186,198); paint and hitbox AGREE.
The "painter draws lower than the item" idea was screenshot-to-engine mapping
noise (offsets 48..59 across runs, cy clamped at 199), not a real offset. With
that gone, the real defect was the gate one line up.

PROVEN: the gate is non-faithful (asm), and removing it does not break the
working screens — DONE still commits, sprites still colour, the Hall buttons
still hit. NOT YET DEMONSTRATED end-to-end: an actual dead button coming alive
on a modify sub-screen, because those need a populated roster and every headless
route to one is blocked by imprecise mouse injection (the same injection noise
that faked the paint offset). The fix is correct by faithfulness and matches the
mechanism exactly; the live confirmation is a hardware/real-mouse check.

Also builds clean as CPU68K=68000 (integrity: 0 real-code 020 ops).

events.title: tools: the icongrid probe disproves my own dating of #137
events.message:
tools: the icongrid probe disproves my own dating of #137

Ran the endpoint calibration the bisect needs, and it overturned the conclusion
I committed in 12917a32. Recording that rather than quietly moving on.

I had said the hand-rolled CLUT install in l09dc was correct when written and
broke later, when the GLIB pool flip (43d813f5, 2026-07-13) made jt468 return
the already-extracted sub-GLIB. That was inferred from commit messages and
never measured. The probe judged 43d813f5^ — the commit immediately BEFORE the
flip — and the grid is ALREADY BLACK there (verdict=bad, meanL=7, satpx=0, and
the frame is unmistakably the grid screen: DONE/EXIT bar, READY/ACTION panel,
TEST/MALE/HUMAN/FIGHTER). So the flip is a sufficient explanation for why the
navigation cannot work NOW, but it is not the point of regression.

Pushed back further: at e05e625b, whose message claims the icon-grid colours
were fixed, the route cannot reach char-gen at all — it stops on the Hall
screen, and the probe correctly reports SKIP instead of inventing a verdict.
So there is no GOOD endpoint: every commit this probe can judge says bad. The
likeliest reading is that the live route NEVER produced a coloured grid, and
e05e625b was verified through the FRUA_BODY harness (which calls jt573 directly
and passes) rather than the live jt574 path — the harness/live divergence that
already cost four wrong theories earlier in this work. Probably not a
regression at all.

The measured mechanism is unaffected: l37aa(set1, 0) returns 0 at HEAD, no
palette is installed, jt124 fixes it, and the Falcon/STe frames prove the fix.
Only the causation claim was wrong. Corrected in the l09dc comment and
docs/jt-call-audit.md, both of which now say the dating is unknown.

Two more infrastructure traps found and fixed while getting here, either of
which would have silently ruined a bisect:

- STRAY SOURCES. The Makefile globs $(wildcard src/engine/*.c), and checkout
  does not remove a file untracked at the old commit but tracked on main — so
  src/engine/a4_map.c was compiled at a commit predating a4_map.h. Reads
  exactly like an unbuildable commit. Now `git clean -fdq src platform compat`,
  scoped and without -x, because -x at the root would delete data/.
- THE HARNESS CHANGED INSIDE THE RANGE. 4017f651 (2026-07-26) taught it to find
  the Falcon TOS instead of requiring FALCON_TOS, so an older checked-out
  harness invoked Hatari with options it rejected and Hatari printed its usage
  text — which reads as "the engine will not boot". The harness is now pinned to
  a shadow tree outside the repo, for the same reason the probe is.

events.title: tools: icongrid probe — a verdict that can say "I could not tell"
events.message:
tools: icongrid probe — a verdict that can say "I could not tell"

The old metric counted DISTINCT COLOURS in the grid region and could not
distinguish "the sprites are black" from "the route never got to the grid".
Worse, it scored the main menu at 14 against a correct grid's 12 — so it was
capable of calling a healthy commit bad, and did.

Replaced with two plain statistics over the cell panel, measured on real frames
of every screen the route can land on:

  screen                meanL   satpx
  coloured grid (good)  121.2   29.1%
  black grid (bad)        3.8    0.0%
  main menu              88.3    2.7%
  PICK race/class        90.7    6.1%

satpx >= 15 -> good (exit 0); meanL <= 20 -> bad (exit 1); anything else is NOT
A VERDICT and exits 125 so bisect skips. Statistics rather than a reference
image on purpose: a crop of the game's rendered UI is copyrighted art and must
not enter the repo. `--classify <png>...` re-checks the thresholds offline.

Pacing is now polling instead of fixed sleeps. Keep screenshotting until the
frame classifies as a grid or patience runs out; `shots` already waits for a
settled frame, so each poll doubles as a stability check. The fixed sleeps were
tuned on a 16MHz run and silently desynced on anything slower — an older commit
booting at 8MHz sat on the PICK screen and got judged there, which is precisely
how a healthy commit produced a "bad" verdict.

Switched from the 68000 ST to FALCON: the bug reproduces identically on
Falcon/VIDEL, ST-Low and NovaGPU (three backends sharing no display code, which
is what proved it engine-level), and Falcon boots in ~10s against the ST's
~200s. Falcon also has 14MB, which is what killed the 4MB-ceiling theory.

events.title: platform: video.cfg nova=force, so an emulator can reach the Nova backend
events.message:
platform: video.cfg nova=force, so an emulator can reach the Nova backend

display_nova.c is the only backend with no emulator. dsp_detect gates the probe
on _VDO <= 1 (a real card leaves the cookie reading ST/STE), which also makes
the backend unreachable anywhere else: Hatari reports Falcon AND its VDI
emulation tops out at 4 planes, so the 8-plane screen the probe requires cannot
exist there. Every Nova change therefore costs a round trip through the real
ATW800/2 — including the workstation-leak fix in bbbd5167, still unverified.

video.cfg may now contain `nova=force`, which runs the probe regardless of
_VDO. Read by a small independent helper rather than through videl_cfg_mode(),
because that runs inside videl_init — after a backend has already been chosen.

A config key rather than a -D so ONE binary serves the card and the emulator.
This session already lost time to a field log produced by a build older than
the fix it was meant to be testing; fewer variants is fewer chances to compare
the wrong two things.

Scope, stated plainly: this makes ARAnyM able to exercise the probe, the AES/VDI
workstation open, the depth query and the palette writes — enough to regression-
test the detect leak by counting "nova: card width" in DBG.LOG. It CANNOT
validate nova_hw_inverse, the pen -> hardware-slot table measured on the
ATW800/2. ARAnyM is the same class of target, not the same hardware.

docs/aranym-harness.md records the feasibility work, which is PARTIAL and says
so: ARAnyM boots TOS 4.04 headless at 8bpp, but plain TOS has no HostFS (the
host-folder mapping is a NatFeat), and ARAnyM rejects Hatari's EmuTOS image
outright. EmuTOS-for-ARAnyM boots, yet its default desktop still shows no host
drive, so nothing has actually been RUN under ARAnyM yet and no Nova path has
been verified. Remaining steps are listed there.

Also recorded: `import -window` on a STALE window id hangs and then wedges the
whole X server, so xwininfo and xwd hang afterwards too and Xvfb has to be
restarted. ARAnyM's window id changes between runs, which made this look like
"ARAnyM cannot be screenshotted". Re-query the id before every capture.

events.title: platform: cache dsp_detect — every palette write was leaking a VDI workstation
events.message:
platform: cache dsp_detect — every palette write was leaking a VDI workstation

The NovaGPU menu hotkey letters paint correctly once and go black on the next
redraw. DBGNOVAT.LOG says why, and it is not the palette.

qd_set_palette() calls dsp_detect() on EVERY palette write. On the Nova path
that reaches dsp_backend_nova(), which calls nova_open_ws() — appl_init +
v_opnvwk — and on success deliberately returns with the workstation still OPEN
for init()/shutdown(). Nothing closed the previous one and nova_open_ws
overwrites s_handle unconditionally, so each palette write leaked one VDI
virtual workstation AND one AES application slot.

The field log shows the shape exactly: "nova: card width = 640" (a detect-only
line) appears 12 times during boot, the twelfth landing on the same line as
"menu: modal up". So the menu's first paint happens right as VDI runs out of
handles. After that v_opnvwk fails, s_handle goes to 0, vs_color writes to
nothing, and dsp_detect starts handing back the ST/STe backend instead of Nova
— the next redraw resolves its colours against a CLUT nobody is updating any
more. Correct once, black afterwards, and Nova-only because no other backend
allocates anything in its probe.

Fix: cache the result. dsp_detect answers a hardware question that cannot
change while we run, so answering it once is also just correct — and it drops a
per-palette-write probe from every Atari backend, not only Nova. Plus a
belt-and-braces guard in dsp_backend_nova: an already-open workstation is the
normal steady state on this path, so reuse it rather than stacking another.

Verified: Falcon char-gen frame md5-IDENTICAL, Mega STe 4MB boots to the menu
with the hotkey letters intact. 469 passed, 6 skipped.

NOT verified on the card — Nova cannot be exercised under Hatari (dsp_detect
returns VIDEL on _VDO==3 before the probe, and the probe needs an 8-plane VDI
screen while Hatari's --vdi-planes tops out at 4). The check on hardware is
DBG.LOG: "nova: card width" should now appear exactly ONCE, not twelve times.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: tools: verify every JT-call lead by hand — one real bug, five tool defects
events.message:
tools: verify every JT-call lead by hand — one real bug, five tool defects

Worked through all the outstanding leads against the disassembly. The result is
worth stating plainly: the tool was wrong far more often than the engine was.

Every one of the 16 surviving shape-matched leads is now read and cleared —
idiom substitution (max/min, memset, vsprintf, _NewPtr/_FreeMem), an omitted
error-alert path, or a deviation the code already documented (l5c1e pumps l725c
via jt1134; l01be uses design_save_path because GEMDOS has no HFS ':'; l1276
paints its own name; l0004's desk-accessory arms are the HAL-moot class). l78fa
turned out to be an inline expansion: jt118 IS jt108(1) + jt1001(...), which it
calls. Full table in docs/jt-call-audit.md.

So the whole exercise yielded exactly ONE genuine drop — l309c's pending-text
flush, fixed in 5e8218a7 — out of roughly thirty raised. A hit from this tool
is weak evidence; the doc now says so.

Three more defects found in the tool while verifying, on top of the two already
fixed:

- Callbacks installed by ADDRESS were invisible. `l63c0(..., (long)&jt237,
  (long)&jt236)` never matches a `name(` pattern, so every callback
  installation in the engine was reported as a drop: jt241, jt240, jt169,
  l1bfe, jt511, l2558, jt239, jt127, l100c. Now matches bare identifiers — with
  comments and string literals stripped first, because PROBE("jtNNN") and the
  doc comments would otherwise satisfy every check and the tool would find
  nothing at all. Stripping also exposed drops those comment mentions had been
  hiding, so this cut both ways.
- Extracted helpers, in three flavours, all of which hid the call: a
  `<name>_suffix` sibling (l0980_slots holds l0980's JT[661]/JT[670]), a
  suffixed lift of the entry itself (jt1154_pg IS JT[1154], so jt52 and jt965
  were reported for a call they make), and a helper named after an asm label
  INSIDE the parent's span (l45f0_menu holds jt955's four jt155 calls and its
  jt182 "Blocked:" prompt). All three are credited now, the last one bounded to
  labels within the function's own address range so it cannot launder an
  unrelated function's calls.

Net across the sweep: 174 -> 75 drops, 32 -> 16 shape matches, and the
calibration held through every change (pre-fix l09dc reports JT[124], HEAD is
clean). Two new tests pin the pointer and comment/string behaviour.

469 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: engine: l309c flushes pending text before blitting, as the Mac does
events.message:
engine: l309c flushes pending text before blitting, as the Mac does

The one finding from the JT-call sweep that survived verification. CODE 5
@0x30d6 calls JT[1124] with no arguments, right after the l2856 lookup's
null check and before the bearing adjustment; our l309c did not.

JT[1124] is CODE 4+0x4d88 = l4d88, which we had already lifted faithfully and
in full: it takes the deferred character count (-936), derives the bounding
rect ((mode ? 8 : 12) * count wide), fills it, InvalRects it, then clears the
count and resets the buffer pointer to &-1041. The Mac empties the pending
glyph buffer before drawing art over that area. Skipping it leaves buffered
text to be painted over, with the stale invalidation resolved later.

Call-site census says this was an isolated miss rather than a pattern: the Mac
has 16 (13 pc-relative within CODE 4, 3 through the jump table), our C had 14.

Falcon regression frame is md5-identical, so nothing visible changed on the
char-gen screen — the buffer is empty there at that point. To be clear about
what this is: a faithfulness fix with NO user-visible symptom attributed to it.
It is not a claimed fix for any of the outstanding text bugs.

Two traps recorded in docs/jt-call-audit.md while settling this. L2856 sits
immediately beside the dropped call and reads like the same routine, but
CODE 4+0x4d88 and CODE 5+0x2856 are different code — l2856 is NOT an alias for
JT[1124]. And CODE 5's L25f4, another JT[1124] caller, is not this repo's
l25f4, which is CODE 13+0x25f4 (the same-offset-different-segment trap);
CODE 5's is simply unlifted, so the audit never covered it.

Also documented, as understood rather than outstanding: l309c's other drop,
JT[1200] at 0x3172, where the Mac shifts bpp_w left by 3 only when
jt1200() == 0. Our l2d4e is re-parameterised and applies the *8 internally and
unconditionally, which agrees exactly in the jt1200() == 0 case our 8-bit
targets are in. It would diverge only on a colour screen that is not 8-bit
deep, which the port does not produce.

467 passed, 6 skipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: tools: jt_call_audit — fix two false-positive sources, document the top three drops
events.message:
tools: jt_call_audit — fix two false-positive sources, document the top three drops

Following the sweep to its conclusion. Both of the tool's own defects were
found by reading the asm instead of trusting its output, and both inflated the
findings:

- Multi-line forward declarations parsed as definitions. The decl-vs-def test
  only looked for a trailing ';' on the FIRST line, so a two-line declaration
  fell through and brace-matching ran on into the next function. This made the
  tool report l33ac as dropping JT[1200] and JT[394] — a confident, wrong, and
  very plausible-looking finding, since l33ac is the GLIB loader and those two
  calls are exactly what a loader would use. Its real body (49k lines further
  down, un-annotated) makes both calls. Now decided by whichever of ';' or '{'
  comes first.
- Wrapper/implementation splits reported the whole body as dropped. The port
  often lifts one Mac function as a thin wrapper plus the real body (jt110 is
  an 8-line forwarder to l33ac; both are CODE 6+0x33ac), so the full asm was
  being compared against the wrapper: 13 phantom drops. One level of delegation
  is now followed, for a small body with a single callee. jt110: 13 -> 1.

120 drops -> 112; 32 shape matches -> 29. Calibration unchanged in both
directions (pre-fix l09dc reports JT[124], HEAD is clean).

What the three most-dropped targets actually are, now written down so nobody
re-investigates them: JT[1200] is the display-mode query, JT[399] is memset,
JT[394] is sprintf. Their frequency is idiom substitution, not near-misses —
jt21 and jt910, for instance, zero their buffers with plain C loops.

The useful find: JT[1200] picks the file EXTENSION. In l33ac the display mode
chooses "%s.ctl" vs "%s.tlb" (and "%s%d%03d.ctl" vs ".tlb" for the numbered
form) — mode 3 asks for .TLB. Our l33ac does this faithfully. The distinction
is live in the DOS-converted set: all 23 .CTL/.TLB pairs are the same SIZE but
different BYTES, so they are genuinely different art. The matching sizes read
like a collapsed conversion at first glance and are not one.

And the 1.0-vs-1.2 question: none of this is version skew. The audit compares
against the 1.0 disassembly, which is the lift target, so every drop is
1.0-internal by construction — and the jump table is permuted between the forks
(1208 vs 1207 entries), so JT numbers are not comparable across them anyway. Of
the three, only JT[399] appears in the 1.2 worklist (hunk 8, fill 0 -> 1 in
l36e0_c10), already ported. Both 1.2 passes are complete, so the DOS data
switch remains the thing that changed under this code.

467 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: tools: jt_call_audit — find lifted bodies that drop a JT call the Mac makes
events.message:
tools: jt_call_audit — find lifted bodies that drop a JT call the Mac makes

#137 took seven weeks because nothing could see it. The char-gen icon grid had
65 hand-written lines where CODE 17 has one `jsr JT[124]`; it compiled, ran,
and carried a comment explaining why the JT call was skipped. The workaround
was correct when written and silently wrong nine commits later, when the
loader it assumed (jt468) changed underneath it.

This is the structural check for that class. For each of the 1422 functions in
boot.c annotated `(CODE NN + 0xXXXX)`, extract the matching asm body, collect
the JT[n] targets it calls, and report the ones the C never calls. An lXXXX
alias for the same address counts as the call (docs/lxxxx-jt-aliases.md).

Calibrated against the bug itself, in both directions: run it on
12917a32^:src/engine/boot.c and it reports `l09dc NOT in C: JT[124]`; run it on
HEAD and l09dc is clean. tests/ pins the behaviour on synthetic fixtures, since
the real disassembly is git-ignored and CI has nothing to point it at.

The first run was useless and that is worth recording: 174 hits, 100+ of them
CODE 1's low jump-table entries. Those are THINK C runtime, not engine calls —
JT[1]/JT[2]/JT[3] are the sparse/sparse-long/range switch dispatchers, and
JT[4]..JT[8] are 32-bit mul/udiv/umod/sdiv/smod. A faithful lift writes
`switch` and `*` and `/`, so none of them can ever appear. Verified by
disassembling CODE 1 0x130..0x20c and against boot.c's own jt4..jt8, which are
literally `return a * b;`. Excluding them: 120 real drops, 32 matching the
#137 shape (big C body, one or two drops, no admitted TODO).

One finding verified by hand so far: l309c (CODE 5+0x309c) omits a zero-arg
JT[1124] at 0x30d6. The near-miss there is instructive — the asm calls L2856
at 0x30c4 and our C does too, so it looks like the same routine appears twice,
but CODE 4+0x4d88 and CODE 5+0x2856 are different code. l2856 is NOT an alias
for JT[1124].

The other 31 are leads, not findings, and docs/jt-call-audit.md says so — this
is an instrument that needed its own exclusion list fixed before its output
meant anything, and it still cannot tell a declared deferral from a hidden one.

467 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: engine: the char-gen icon grid commits its palette with jt124, as the Mac does
events.message:
engine: the char-gen icon grid commits its palette with jt124, as the Mac does

The 7x7 body-icon grid rendered every sprite black on ALL FIVE backends
(verified Falcon/VIDEL and ST-Low here, reported on NovaGPU) because this
site did not do what CODE 17 does.

The Mac is three instructions:

  0a4c: pea 0x47b0            ; "DUNGCOM1"
  0a52: jsr %a5@(914)         ; JT[110]  bind
  0a5e: jsr %a5@(1026)        ; JT[124]  commit the palette
  0a68: jsr %a5@(954)         ; JT[115]  free the slot

We had 65 hand-written lines in place of the jt124: navigate outer item 1 ->
its item 0, parse the colour-table header, clamp it away from 0..31, and
install via port_clut_install. That was written in June (e05e625b) for a real
reason -- back then jt468("DUNGCOM1") returned the OUTER DUNGCOM.CTL, so
jt124 -> l3eea -> jt993 read a nested GLIB's stub header as a colour table
and splattered 0..255, wrecking the stone frame.

The GLIB pool flip (2026-07-13, cw_setglib_load) removed that premise:
"jt468(group) IS the extracted sub-GLIB, so the old l37aa(base, set) index
step disappears". The wall-set code was updated for it. This site was not,
so its extra l37aa(...,1) then walked one level too deep, landed on a TILE
instead of the set, and l37aa(tile,0) returned 0 -- no palette installed at
all. The sprite pixels (indices 87/72/79) were left resolving against clut
129, where all three are RGB(0,0,0). Hence black, on every backend, which is
what proved it was not a display bug.

The faithful call reaches the right table unaided: jt1017 reports index-type
0 (hdr[11] of the set GLIB), so jt993 fetches sub-item 0, whose header
already declares start=32/count=224. The 0..31 UI range is protected by the
DATA, not by a clamp we invented -- which is why the stone frame survives
without the hand-rolled guard.

Verified on Falcon (14MB, VIDEL) and Mega STe (4MB, ST-Low): 49 coloured
sprites on silver cell grounds, frame chrome intact. 461 passed, 6 skipped.

Two theories this kills: the 4MB memory ceiling (the Falcon shows it at
14MB) and any Nova palette involvement (three unrelated backends, one fault).

events.title: Trace MONA's W (write to tape) command end to end
events.message:
Trace MONA's W (write to tape) command end to end

Four inputs, not the two the manual describes: filename, First:, Last:
and Start:. The last supplies the entry address written into the file
header. The file is opened before the addresses are asked, which is why
all four abort branches converge on CLOSE_AND_EXIT instead of returning.

Running it and capturing the firmware call shows what is actually
passed: CAS OUT DIRECT receives HL = First, DE = Last - First, BC = the
Start address, A = 2 for a binary file.

That length is one short. For First=&5000 Last=&500F it passes 15, so
the byte at Last is never saved, and First = Last writes nothing at all.
The sibling commands do add the one - CMD_COPY does INC BC, CMD_FILL
does INC HL - and both were verified inclusive by running them. So W is
inconsistent with I and P, and with the manual, which calls the range
inclusive for all three.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: sarnau

events.title: Trace MONA's P (fill) command end to end
events.message:
Trace MONA's P (fill) command end to end

Twenty-five bytes, with two details worth recording.

The abort test is out of order on purpose. CP &FC at &0F9E sets Z, then
LD A,L, EX DE,HL and POP BC all leave the flags untouched, so the RET Z
three instructions later still acts on that compare - the check is made
before the registers are rearranged for the loop, and acted on after.

The loop is three instructions because CPI is used purely for its side
effects: it increments HL, decrements BC and sets P/V from BC, while the
comparison it performs is thrown away. RET PO leaves when the count hits
zero. Two bytes where INC HL, DEC BC and a test would need four.

Verified by running it rather than by reading: &5000..&500F fills
exactly, both endpoints included and the following byte untouched, and a
single-byte range writes one byte - confirming the INC HL that turns
Last-First into the count.

A range with Last < First never reaches this code; INPUT_FIRST_LAST
abandons the command first, which is the abort the manual documents for
P as well as for I, T and W.

events.title: Trace MONA's I (intelligent copy) command end to end
events.message:
Trace MONA's I (intelligent copy) command end to end

The whole command is 36 bytes and contains exactly one decision, which
is the "intelligent" part the manual names: compare First against To.
If First >= To the destination lies below the source and a forward LDIR
is safe; if First < To the destination overlaps above, so both pointers
are advanced to the far end and LDDR runs backwards. BC arrives from
INPUT_FIRST_LAST as Last-First and is incremented to the count.

Verified by running it rather than by reading: copying &5000..&500F to
&5004 reproduces the block intact instead of smearing the leading bytes
through it, and the reverse overlap picks LDIR.

The abort turns out not to live in this command at all. INPUT_FIRST_LAST
checks Last >= First and, when it is not, resets SP to MONA's stack and
redisplays rather than returning - so the documented "aborted if the
start address is greater than the end address" is inherited by every
command that asks for a range: I, P, T and W.

events.title: diag: fix the paltrace encoding, log the icon-grid CLUT guards
events.message:
diag: fix the paltrace encoding, log the icon-grid CLUT guards

Encoding bug in the Nova paltrace (mine): r/g/b are 0..255 but were packed into
decimal 1e4/1e2 fields, so r>=100 spilled into the index field — the card log
duly showed index 8 twice and indices 16/17 from a probe that only records
below 16. Bit-pack instead (idx<<24 | r<<16 | g<<8 | b). The call SEQUENCE from
that run is still sound and useful: seven full 0..255 installs plus small ranges
at 208/176/184, i.e. the UI range is rewritten wholesale several times.

icontrace now logs the four guards of the icon-grid palette install (bind
handle, outer set, item-0 colour table, ph[7]&15), because a real-hardware run
proved the install NEVER RUNS on the live path — 49 cells blit with a valid art
handle and no CLUTstart line is emitted.

Also kept: the l09dc clamp now DROPS palette entries below index 32 instead of
sliding the table up to meet 32 (sliding installs every colour one index above
the pixels using it). Verified non-regressive on the working case, but it is
defensive — NOT the cause here, since the block is never reached.

Three theories eliminated by evidence this round, recorded so they are not
re-tried: (1) art failing to load — the handle is valid and no cell is refused;
(2) HEIRS shipping its own DUNGCOM — HEIRS.DSN contains no DUNGCOM art, both
paths bind the same root DUNGCOM.TLB; (3) sprite pixels resolving to black —
the histogram was sampling an EMPTY grid, not coloured sprites.

What the hardware photo actually shows: one cell renders, as a mask-only
SILHOUETTE, and the other 48 draw nothing. Silhouette = the mode-1 two-plane
composite (l2d4e, commit 5574a36b) not running — the same failure that commit
originally fixed.

Local repro secured: -DFRUA_CHARGEN boots jt574, the REAL "Create Character"
entry, straight to the PICK screens. The FRUA_BODY harness that has been
passing all along calls jt573 (the review screen) directly and never walks this
path, which is why it could not see the bug.

events.title: Run MONA's own disassembler over every opcode
events.message:
Run MONA's own disassembler over every opcode

optable.py decodes MONA's tables statically. This does the opposite:
tools/disasm_run.py executes the real decoder in the emulator and reads
the rendered text out of the line buffer, so the output is what MONA
actually prints - including the prefix handling and operand emitters,
none of which are stored as data.

Against the static decode the live run agrees on 250/252 base entries,
the two exceptions being JR and DJNZ, where the live decoder resolves
the relative displacement to an absolute address.

It also corrects two claims I had inferred from the tables rather than
observed:

- The undocumented SLL does not print with a blank mnemonic. CB 30..37
  are routed to the invalid-opcode path and come out as NOP flagged with
  an asterisk.
- DDCB does not "print only the documented form". When the register
  field is not 6 the prefix is dropped altogether, so DD CB 05 00 prints
  as RLC B rather than anything involving IX.

Cross-checked against tools/z80dis.py: 247/256 base, 248/256 CB, 56/56
ED, 197/256 DD agree, with the remainder being MONA's own limits - 8 SLL
slots and 72 unused ED opcodes flagged invalid, IXh/IXl shown as H/L,
and the DDCB copy forms.

diag: two field probes for the hardware-only char-gen / Nova reports

Both #ifdef-gated and verified to compile out of the shipping builds (0 refs in
the no-flag objects), because both bugs only appear on real hardware.

FRUA_ICONTRACE (jt57): the char-gen body-icon grid renders BLACK via the live
path on ST-Low AND Nova, while the FRUA_BODY harness draws all 49 icons
correctly on ST-Low and Falcon — so the harness (which seeds its own record,
calls jt573 directly, and never repaints: its loop is jt920, a PROBE-only stub)
is not reaching the situation. jt57 is the chokepoint every cell blits through
and it returns silently on a null art handle — "the icon grid just stays empty",
exactly the symptom. Count calls vs null handles and log the handle, which
splits an art-LOADING failure from a drawing/palette one. Known-good baseline
(harness, ST-Low): 49 calls / 0 null / handle 917170.

FRUA_NOVA_PALTRACE (nova_set_palette): the menu's hotkey letters paint CORRECTLY
and then go black on a redraw. A wrong hw_inverse table cannot do that — it
would be wrong on the first paint too — so log every palette write (first,
count) plus the RGB landing on indices 0..15, to catch whatever overwrites the
UI colours between the paints. Suspect: the full 256-entry clut 129 install,
which the boot log shows happening twice; ST survives it because hw_palette = 0
forces a re-quantise that re-derives valid slots, while Nova (hw_palette = 1)
has nothing that recovers a clobbered entry.

Also recorded: the char-gen race/class picker is NOT a bug. DOS shows the same
red headings and red selection dots the Nova build renders, so the 256-colour
path is faithful; ST-Low's cyan headings are its 16-colour quantiser.
