events.title: buggyboy/remaster: draw the name-entry alphabet in the results differential
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: draw the name-entry alphabet in the results differential

The results screen was ALREADY byte-compared against recreate across every
mode, rank and leg (test_results_screen_matches) - and still missed the black
box, purely on DATA: the default hi-score table's names are "...", so the
name-entry alphabet never reached the glyph blitter from there. The draw was
covered; the character set was not.

Two windows of the table's initials fields now tile 'A'..'`' (the top one
ending ON the delete sentinel), drawn and byte-compared. Mutation-verified:
restoring FONT_BYTES = 0x600 reddens exactly the window that draws '`' (23
bytes) and leaves the other green - i.e. this test catches the shipped bug
directly, which nothing else did.

Review fixes folded in (both were real holes in the first cut):
- The window guard was a tautology: "the last window ends at the top char" is
  true by construction of NAME_WINDOWS. Now asserts GAP-FREENESS, which is
  the property that can actually break (a smaller table silently leaves a
  hole in the middle of the alphabet).
- `footprint > 0` cannot show the alphabet was drawn: both sides read the same
  seeded table, and the initials are ~250 bytes of a ~9600-byte footprint
  dominated by the background fill, so a screen that never blitted the last
  row would agree with the reference and pass. (results.c's RS_MAX_ROWS is not
  pinned to HS_ROWS, so that is reachable.) The test now changes ONLY the
  window's top character and requires the REFERENCE output to move, proving
  the row carrying it is really blitted. Sensitivity-verified: aiming that
  probe at a row the screen does not draw fails the assertion.

Docs: two coverage traps generalised in PORTING.md - a differential can be
pinned on the wrong DATA (ask which values the fixture contains, not just
which paths run), and mutation testing lies when the edit preserves file size
(Python validates .pyc on mtime+size, so a same-length constant edit applied
and reverted within one filesystem second can leave the MUTATED bytecode in
place; it also baked a truncated fixture_font, which the shipped-fixture
assertion caught).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: hoist the prefix asset binding into shared code
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: hoist the prefix asset binding into shared code

The play-test bugs were not "does the shell compile" (that is the build gate,
69a6332) but "does the shell wire the arenas the way the original did".
`make test` cannot answer that by compiling game_main.c for the host - it is
full of TOS seams. The answer is to move each binding DECISION into shared
code the shell AND the harness both call, so a wrong decision is wrong on
both sides and the composed-frame differential sees it.

rm_bind_gobj_prefix_assets (src/gameplay.c, declared in game.h) now owns the
whole GobjPrefixAssets bundle - the one where every alias in this port lives:
- marker_recs = rm_ring_decay_base(ring_st): the decay arena IS the object
  dispatcher's flag grid (this is the alias whose absence left a kicked
  roadside object writing to a dead buffer, animating nothing).
- anim_color = the HUD's fuel-mask table.
- the two buf_a anim-word mirrors, at RM_GOBJ_ANIM_MIRROR{1,2}_OFF, moved
  from render/atari/game_frame.h into game.h so there is one definition.

Callers now: game_main.c, equiv._ComposedScene, and equiv.compare_gobj_prefix.
The three const table pointers stay the caller's to resolve, since only it
knows its own base - the shell walks its obj-low blob, the harness points into
the 68k image, and they agree because OBJ_LOW_BASE + OBJ_LOW_X == A_X by
construction (gen_game_fixture.py's low()).

Why this is the real fix: the harness now EXECUTES the shell's binding code
instead of re-implementing it. Mutation-verified - dropping the bias inside
the binder fails four tests, where before the harness had its own (also
wrong) binding and saw nothing.

Pins:
- test_game_fixture asserts the shell binds through the binder AND pins the
  ARGUMENTS: anim_color is a pass-through, so a shell handing the prefix a
  private colour buffer would otherwise "use the binder" while silently
  breaking the fuel-mask alias on hardware (mutation-verified).
- The two mirror offsets are pinned game.h <-> adapter.py across the language
  boundary, like the ring-block geometry.

Review fixes folded in: zero-init the shell's bundle so it matches the
ctypes-zeroed harness struct if a field is ever added; drop game_main.c's now
empty game_frame.h include; correct that header's banner (one bench-only
constant left, and a note that a real shell wants rm_ring_decay_base); name
the macros in the struct's field comments instead of repeating their values.

Scope, honestly: the OTHER bundles (HudAssets most of all) carry their offsets
in the GENERATED game_fixture.h, which src/ would have to include to bind
them - pulling every baked array into the host .so. Hoisting those needs
gen_game_fixture.py split into a defines header and an arrays header. Until
then, bind bundle-by-bundle, starting with whichever holds an alias.

make test 723 passed; make gate clean both ways; make golden 5/5 MATCH.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: harness gap #2 — the on-target build is a test gate
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: harness gap #2 — the on-target build is a test gate

`make test` compiled the game shell for NOBODY: render/atari/game_main.c
(1721 lines - every asset binding, the frame loop, every TOS seam) is in
neither the host .so (SRC is src/*.c) nor bench.elf (bench_build.sh links a
17-file src/ subset), and four more src/ files (frame/flow/intermission/
results) are in the host .so but not in bench.elf. build_game.sh compiled
all of them; nothing in the gate ever RAN it. A shell that did not compile
therefore reached origin TWICE in one session with the suite green.

Gate:
- `make test` now depends on GATE.PRG + GATEMEAS.PRG: full cross-compile +
  link + .PRG wrap. Two builds because src/blitter_{selftest,sweep,census}.c
  compile only under their own measurement flags; those three combine into
  one extra build, so between them every .c in the project is covered
  (src/render.c excepted - a dead Phase-A stub linked by neither).
- Both go through build_game.sh rather than restating its flags; a third
  copy of the cross flags is exactly the drift the gate exists to catch.
  Gate-only .PRG names + GAME_NO_STAGE=1 so the shipping BUGGYBOY.PRG and
  the Hatari drive are never touched.
- `make golden` promotes the Hatari end-to-end (5 legs, ~20 s) to a named
  target for pre-promotion runs. Verified: 5/5 MATCH, which also confirms
  today's four play-test fixes on a 68000.
- Mutation-verified: a typo'd constant in game_main.c now fails `make test`
  at the build step, before pytest runs.

Incrementality (the trap adding the gate exposed):
- build_game.sh and bench_build.sh re-run gen_sound_fixture.py
  unconditionally, so build/sound_data.h's mtime bumped every build and
  every target depending on it was out of date the moment it finished.
  bench.elf had been rebuilding on every `make test` for exactly this
  reason, unnoticed. Fixed at the root: fixture_lib.write_if_changed()
  skips identical writes, used by all three generators. `make test` on an
  unchanged tree now rebuilds nothing (~21 s, same as before the gate).
- The first attempt (order-only prerequisites) was reverted: it "worked"
  only by dropping the rebuild coverage that made the dependency worth
  declaring. Caught by the pre-commit review.
- GATE_DEPS declares what a script-built target easily under-declares: the
  generators, the harness modules the fixture is baked from (test/adapter.py
  bakes the asset windows - an adapter change is what shipped the truncated
  font fixture), and render/atari/*.h, which neither existing wildcard
  covered. An under-declared gate certifies a binary it did not rebuild.
- Order-only chain serialises the three m68k builds (they share fixed-name
  intermediates in render/atari/build/, so `make -j` could wrap one build's
  .bin into another's .PRG - a green gate that validated nothing). `golden`
  joins the chain since run_golden.py shells out to the same script.

Scope, honestly: this catches "the shell does not compile / does not link".
It would NOT have caught any of the four play-test bugs - those were valid
C. Executing the shell's bindings host-side stays the job of hoisting them
into shared code (rm_draw_frame, then the ring/decay geometry in game.h).

Suite: 723 passed, unchanged.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: close harness gap #1 — shared ring/decay aliasing
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: close harness gap #1 — shared ring/decay aliasing

REPAIRS THE BUILD: dcafb21 committed game_main.c's use of
RM_RING_ST_BLOCK_BYTES / RM_RING_DECAY_BIAS / rm_ring_decay_base without
the include/game.h that defines them, so the m68k game build did not
compile at that commit. This lands the header half.

Harness gap #1 was: the marker-decay binding lives in game_main.c, which
`make test` never compiles, so the fix for the missing kicked-object
animation shipped pinned only by reading. Closed not by compiling the shell
host-side but by removing the opportunity to disagree.

- The aliasing geometry moved OUT of the shell into include/game.h:
  RM_RING_DECAY_BIAS / RM_RING_DECAY_SPILL / RM_RING_ST_BLOCK_BYTES and
  rm_ring_decay_base(). One definition of "the dispatcher's grid and the
  prefix's decay arena are ONE padded block".
- equiv._ComposedScene had been binding marker_recs into the image while its
  own dispatcher read a private unpadded ring_st - the harness independently
  reproducing the shell's bug, which is exactly why the composed differential
  was blind to it. It now allocates the same padded block.

Pins (all mutation-verified):
- test_marker_decay_writes_reach_the_dispatcher_grid: the decay's walked
  marker must arrive in the grid THROUGH THE POINTER THE DISPATCHER IS GIVEN
  and make that slot word negative (what triggers the SPECIAL pass). Asserted
  via scene.ring_st, not the test's own block - reading the block let the bias
  cancel out of the arithmetic and passed with the grid mis-based.
- A directed armed-decay drive (no free drive kicks an object).
- test_game_fixture: the shell's own allocation (game_main.c is never
  compiled by make test, so without this a build that drops the bias stays
  green), game.h's RM_RING_ST_BLOCK_BYTES macro BODY (dropping a term would
  otherwise pass), and the seed constants against MARKER_DECAY_ARM /
  GOBJ_MARKER_STRIDE.
- bench_main.c: a note that its separated arenas are deliberate and must not
  be copied into a real shell.

What it caught immediately: with the arenas correctly aliased the composed
frame still diverges on 2 of 27 sampled frames of the decay drive. That is
EXPOSED by the fix, not caused by it - bound separately the same drive
diverged on 25 of 27, i.e. the old harness was noise. Asserted as an exact
count rather than xfail'd: a binary xfail cannot tell "still failing for the
documented reason" from "failing because someone unbound the arenas" (under
the bias mutation the drive goes to 27 of 27 and an xfail stays green).
Prime suspect is a harness artifact - the composed scene re-serializes the
grid every frame while the shell and the original only do so on a course
advance. Recorded in STATUS.md, unresolved.

Docs: PORTING.md gains the closure and the rule it generalises (when two
subsystems must see the same bytes, the aliasing geometry belongs in shared
code, not in each caller); STATUS.md records the gap, the pins and the
divergence.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: fix 4 shell-binding bugs found by play-test
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: fix 4 shell-binding bugs found by play-test

Two visible faults were reported ("no animation when the buggy kicks a
roadside object"; "a black box for the character during high-score name
entry"). Both were the same class, and sweeping for that class found two
more. NONE was in src/ - every ported core stays byte-exact. All four sat
in the layer `make test` does not compile (render/atari/game_main.c) or in
the fixture windows it consumes, where the harness builds its own bindings
instead of the shell's, so the suite was green and the game was wrong.

Fixes:
- marker-decay arena: GobjPrefixAssets.marker_recs pointed at a private BSS
  block while the dispatcher read ring_st. In the original both are the one
  grid at A_obj_markers (decay base = grid - 8), so the kicked-object
  animation wrote nowhere; the object still vanished and still scored, which
  is why it read as "the animation is missing". ring_st is now a padded
  block and the prefix gets the biased base.
- font window: FONT_BYTES was 0x600, one glyph short of the name-entry
  delete sentinel '`' (0x60). On target the blitter read the next fixture as
  glyph pixels, and an all-zero (mask, ink) row REPLACES the cell with
  colour 0 - the black box. Now one derived FONT_BYTES; the duplicate
  FONT_GLYPH_BYTES is gone.
- live globals frozen: objlist.bonus_timer / p24_flag were derived once in
  start_leg, so the 5-flag bonus window never clamped an object type and the
  p24 gate never re-read the checkpoint-bumped score digit. Both refreshed
  in rm_draw_frame, where the original reads them.
- aliased global split: 0x18d12 is rev_reload AND lean_frame, so the poke at
  both its sites restarts the lean overlay. It had been skipped on the
  reasoning that "no compared surface reads lean_frame" - false,
  draw_buggy_hi reads it every frame. Now PlayerState.lean_frame_reload ->
  rm_apply_player -> SpriteState.lean_frame.

Harness (the reason these hid):
- equiv._ComposedScene no longer REPRODUCES the shell's staleness for
  bonus_timer / p24_flag - reproducing a bug on both sides is exactly what
  stops a differential from seeing it.
- test_composed_frame: directed bonus-window drive (no free drive opens the
  window). test_player: both rev_reload poke sites. test_game_fixture: the
  font window derived from flow.c's HS_CHAR_DEL + the glyph stride pinned to
  text.h across the language boundary + the shipped fixture length, and the
  marker-decay padding pinned to the addresses and the prefix walk.
- test_text now fuzzes up to the top glyph instead of stopping one short.
- All mutation-verified: each fix's removal reddens its own test and no other.

Docs:
- PORTING.md: "The shell-binding trap" - the four defects, the generalised
  rules, and the alias sweep over addrs.h (4 addresses carry two names; only
  0x18d12 was broken).
- STATUS.md: the fix table plus two honest residuals on the decay wire (the
  clears do not survive a course advance since ring_st is a derived mirror;
  the low pad is seg_data[12] in the original, not filler).
- names.txt: the dual role at 0x18d12.

buggyboy/remaster: SOUND slice 3 — the game ships WITH sound on target

Shell (render/atari):
- vbl_sound: the 50 Hz VBL pump — when vbl_enable is RUNNING and no trigger
  mutation is in flight, writes rm_refresh's YM2149 (reg,val) stream to
  0xffff8800/02; parked = silence, exactly the original's parked vector.
  Installed as _vblqueue[0] PRESERVING the displaced TOS entries (TOS's
  per-VBL Dosound stepper drives the beeps), via one Supexec; conterm
  cleared (TOS key-click). Symmetric UNINSTALL on the quit path restores
  SYS_VBLQUEUE/SYS_NVBLS so Pterm can't leave TOS jumping into freed TPA.
- Real XBIOS Dosound over the baked lists (sound_dosound.h, split from
  sound_data.h so the shell doesn't carry SND_CONST); unconditional in
  game_main.c so a dropped -DRM_SOUND_TARGET fails at link, not mutely.
- race_start_countdown: stop_music(BEEP)x3 + GO, 51 Vsyncs apiece
  (wait_vbl_set_offset @0x102ee), at race entry like main @0x10226.
- op_wait_music_off: spin on rm_sound_music_on polling FRESH input per
  Vsync — skippable at name entry (0x25bc), NOT at game over (0x2406);
  Crawio key drain at the tail (0x25de). os.s gains Dosound + Supexec.

  rm_sound_lock/unlock carry compiler barriers so -flto can't reorder the
  publish; contract documented in sound.h. No-ops on host/bench builds —
  the differential .so is behavior-identical.

events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: PERF30 A2 measured sizing — the naive design is dead, objshift2 is the prize

Instrumented all three fine-x engines over composed 600-frame drives on all
five legs, recording DISTINCT source bytes per engine (spans overcount):
- objshift2 (the 56 ms fixed pass) reads only 3.0 KB of LEG-INVARIANT sprite
  data and re-shifts it 3,240x per leg — the ideal pre-shift target: a
  boot-time full pix+mask table is ~98 KB compacted.

  table ~360 KB — memory-marginal; masks-only ~72 KB.
- The naive '16 phases of every roadside sprite' is dead: ~458 KB compacted,
  ~1.4 MB offset-preserving. The rm_scroll_prebuild precedent does NOT
  transfer cleanly (its 16-bit offset-preserving window can't hold the 32-bit
  straddled masked form).
- RAM verdict: objshift2-full fits a 1 MB ST beside the 389 KB arena +
  screens; BOTH full does not; on 512 KB only masks-only objshift2 (~49 KB)
  fits. A real pre-shift build implies a 1 MB machine.
- Correctness constraint recorded: objshift's per-call colour fill applies
  AFTER the shift — tables must store pre-colour pix + rotated mask, keeping
  the per-plane &-fill and the RMW at blit time.

Proposals only — no blitter code changed (instrumentation reverted).

equivalence test per the test_mode2_scroll_prebuild pattern), then
objshift masks-only or fold into A3.

Fresh cycle-accurate gap table (2026-07-23, current code — the recent hoists
moved nothing): three stages are 78% of the gate frame (the two masked object
blitters 107 ms + render_road 51 ms). Per-stage proposals in three tiers —
A same-pixels-faster-code (value-passing blitters, pre-shifted compiled
sprites, per-band road writers, hand-asm cores), B same-pixels-different-
algorithm (road display list, HUD static/dynamic split), C explicit fidelity/

interlaced scenery, an STE-blitter build) — each with estimated savings

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: joystick support — the shell parses IKBD packets
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: joystick support — the shell parses IKBD packets

Reconstruction:
- The shell's IKBD ISR (os.s) is now a packet parser: headers 0xF6..0xFF get
  their payload length from a protocol table; ONLY the final byte of a 0xFD
  both-sticks report (joystick 1, the ST game port) is stored to joy_state —
  every other payload is swallowed, so packet bytes can never corrupt the
  scancode arrays. kbd_install pins the IKBD into joystick interrogation mode
  (0x15) alongside mouse-off, so only interrogate replies arrive; read_input
  sends the original's per-frame 0x16 interrogate (read_joystick @0x12110) via
  Ikbdws — the raw ACIA poke the arcade port used bus-errors from user mode
  (found by the flow trace, PC=0x1b150), a supervisor/user difference the
  original never faced.
- Priority merge mirrors recreate input.c:32 exactly: stick bits (0x8f mask)
  win; keyboard arrows/space are the fallback only when the stick is idle.
  F1-F5/R/Esc/Q stay keyboard-only, as in the original. The stick drives the
  race, leg-select nav/fire, and name entry through the one shared input word.
- Gotcha paid for once, now assembler-enforced: os.s .bss must stay even-sized
  (tos.ld SUBALIGN(1) packs downstream globals directly after) — a trailing
  .even replaces the hand pad; the odd-size case address-errored at boot.

Harness:
- 532 tests green; BUGGYBOY.PRG builds; golden MATCH (input is never polled
  before the frame-0 dump); GAME_FLOW_AUTO trace 19 records, unchanged — its
  race loop drives the interrogate + ISR every frame, pinning no-hang /
  no-bus-error / no keyboard corruption. STATED HONESTLY: the headless reply is
  all-zero, so the joystick DECODE path is verified only by the manual
  stick-in-hand run (hatari --joy1 keys); joy_state is sticky on a lost reply

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: port game_update §12's course object/marker ring
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: port game_update §12's course object/marker ring

Section 12 scrolls one grid of 0x20-byte rows, one row per distance band, and
refills the far end from the next packed course record. RoadPose.seg_data was
already row -1 of that grid; this ports rows 0..13 as CourseRing.

The consequence that mattered: each band's marker word is a live course value,
not the baked table it was modelled as. build_road_geometry stamps it into the
HIGH (flag) word of every control long the band covers -- render_road's
blit-variant bits plus the EDGE_* shoulder flags §10 reads back. Freezing that
column froze the road's flags after the first frame. The road half-width is the
control long's LOW word and never came from here, despite the original's
road_width_src name.

Reconstruction:
- CourseRing/CourseRow (include/game.h); EDGE_* hoisted out of player.c, since
  the ring is where those flags are born.
- rm_road_course_advance gains the ring: scroll, refill (select mask -> type
  codes, animation-run expansion, marker fixups, the slot-1 -> slot-13 echo),
  and the no-record age path.
- rm_build_road_geometry takes the ring instead of RoadSource.width_src, so a
  live input can no longer be mistaken for a table it is safe to snapshot once.

Harness:
- compare_leg_drive stops handing the road control table over: it is now a
  compared result, and the ring is compared band by band. The drives hand over
  exactly one thing (the crash arming) instead of two.
- test_course_ring.py: bands 0-11 byte-exact over free-running 600-frame drives
  x 3 scripts x legs 0-4, plus a pin test for the C/Python constant mirrors.

Coverage, found by mutation rather than by reading:
- Branch counters must derive from the record consumed, not the band produced.
  525 of the 554 animation codes re-select the slots the expansion writes and
  overwrite them with the same bytes, so deleting the whole expansion left the
  suite green; the slot-13 echo counter had the identical flaw.
- Two branches a leg start cannot reach are pinned by seeding read_pos onto a
  real record (test_ring_hard_to_reach_branches). A third, MARKER_KIND_SIDES,
  fires for 0 of 5120 records -- left honestly unpinned and noted in STATUS.

Deferred (noted in PORTING.md, not folded in): build_road_geometry writes 2-6
bytes past ctrl (pre-existing); the demo still holds the ring twice, so the
scenery does not stream yet; band 11's marker aliases buggy_gate/fg_gate.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: latch IKBD key presses so short taps are not dropped
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: latch IKBD key presses so short taps are not dropped

The demo polls held-key state once per frame, and a frame here costs ~84 ms
(~12 fps). A tap shorter than that had its make AND break both arrive between
two polls, so key_down[] was already back to 0 when the loop read it and the
press vanished. Esc typically needed three presses to quit.

Fix
- os.s: the IKBD handler now also sets key_hit[scancode] on a MAKE. Unlike
  key_down it is never cleared by the break — only by the C that consumes it,
  so no press can be missed between polls. The handler saves d1/a1 as well as
  d0/a0 now that it writes them (save and restore lists verified to match).
- demo_main.c: take_key_hit() consumes the latch. Momentary keys (Esc, Q, R)
  read it; held keys (arrows, Space) keep reading key_down[], which is what
  steering and throttle actually want. R therefore becomes edge-triggered:
  one restart per press instead of repeating while held.

Instrumentation (same commit: it is what diagnosed the bug, and two hunks in
main() interleave it with the fix, so splitting would leave a commit that does
not build)
- -DDEMO_TRACE=N logs per-frame course state (read_pos, row_ctr, speed, rpm,
  collision_lock, hud_crash_timer, view_wrapped) so a headless drive can show
  whether the course actually advances on-target.
- -DDEMO_KEYLOG plus -Wa,--defsym,KBD_RAWLOG=1 logs every raw byte the ACIA
  delivered, in arrival order, before it is read as a scancode. That log is
  what proved the fault: three Esc presses (01 81 | 01 81 | 01), only the last
  honoured, with no stray packet bytes anywhere in the stream. It also refuted
  the earlier theory that mouse/joystick packets were corrupting key_down[].

Not verified in play: the latch is diagnosed and reasoned from the captured
byte stream, but no interactive run has confirmed Esc/Q/R since. make test does
not reach on-target input, so no automated check covers it.

- Plus the crash-adjacent branches the script needs to be reachable and correct:

  init_leg with no warmup. The candidate is seeded once and then drives itself

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: fix the defects the workflow code review found
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: fix the defects the workflow code review found

Max-effort review of 674505e..HEAD returned 11 findings. Three CONFIRMED ones
contradicted claims made in the previous commits' messages, so those are called
out first.

Correctness:
- run_hatari.py staged COURSES.DAT/GRAPHICS.GRA for EVERY .PRG, but only
  build_demo.sh copies them and disk/ is gitignored — so `build.sh &&
  run_hatari.py` (the documented HUD flow) died on a clean checkout. The earlier
  "HUD.PRG MATCH" passed only because disk/ was already populated by a demo
  build. Now staged per-.PRG, and verified by emptying disk/ first.
- The GRAPHICS.GRA guard had a header-sized floor and no real protection: a file
  truncated ANYWHERE past the header sailed through, and rle_decode had no output
  bound, so it walked out of the arena. The prior commit claimed this was
  "verified on Hatari" — the test only truncated BELOW the floor, which the floor
  caught for the wrong reason. Bound the decoder itself at both ends and return
  false; a size check at the call site cannot do this job, since a file of any
  length can carry an unterminated stream.
- Fread's count (0x3f500) exceeded the arena's remaining room by 37 KB, so an
  over-long file overran the block before any validation ran. Replaced with
  RM_GFX_READ_MAX, derived from the arena geometry.
- read_file accepted handle 0. GEMDOS reserves 0/1/2 and never returns them from
  Fopen; handle 0 is the exact failure os.s's own new comment documents, and it
  makes Fread read the keyboard. Now `<= 0`.
- assets_load.py bounded COURSES.DAT's copy but not GRAPHICS.GRA's, so an
  over-long file memmoved past the ctypes block and corrupted the CPython heap.

Harness:
- test/test_assets_bounds.py — new. Malformed-input cases including the mid-file
  truncation the old test missed, each asserting a trailing canary survives.
- test_python_constants_match_assets_h pins assets_load.py's 8 mirrored
  constants against include/assets.h by parsing it (CLAUDE.md §5). It caught its

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: keep the file-I/O trap wrappers together and first
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: keep the file-I/O trap wrappers together and first

Adding Fopen/Fread for the asset load wedged Cconws between Fread and Fwrite,
splitting the file-I/O block. That block being contiguous and immediately after
_start is not cosmetic: putting other wrappers ahead of or between them made
Hatari's GEMDOS-HD hand back handle 0 (stdin) from Fopen in a large .PRG, so
Fread read the keyboard and the graphics unpack spun forever waiting for an end
marker it would never see. Diagnosing that cost a long session in recreate's
game_os.s, whose layout this file mirrors.

Move Cconws down with the other console wrappers and record the rule in the
header comment so the next wrapper does not re-break it.

The demo happened to work either way at its current size — the original failure
was size-correlated — so this removes a latent trap rather than fixing a live
one. DEMO.PRG and HUD.PRG both still MATCH, and the truncated-asset guard still
refuses bad files.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: on-target demo draws the full object pipeline
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: on-target demo draws the full object pipeline

The interactive DEMO.PRG now runs remaster's WHOLE Phase-A render pipeline on a
real 68000 — road + ground + foreground sprite + roadside object list + scaled
object + player buggy + HUD — and its first frame is byte-identical to
recreate's g_build_road_geometry + g_render_road + g_blit_road_scroll +
g_draw_game_objects + g_draw_hud (run_demo.py prints MATCH). Arrow keys still
steer live.

Demo:
- demo_main.c sequences the draw_game_objects tree in recreate's order (prefix,
  ground, fg sprite, pass 1, draw_object, pass 2, then the fixed pass + buggy
  ordered by the view) and keeps the object state in step with the live pose.
- gen_demo_fixture.py bakes the object arenas (buf_a records, the buf_c
  sprite/graphics arena, and the STATIC+bss table blob the dispatcher reads)
  plus the object/sprite/ground/prefix scalars, and adds g_draw_game_objects to
  the golden pipeline.

Aliased globals the split model has to reproduce (each caused a real on-target
diff, all documented in render/atari/README.md):
- anim_color == fuel_mask (0x17f08): the prefix's animated colour IS the HUD's
  phase-6a fuel mask -> one mutable buffer shared by both.
- obj_xoff_tbl == road_width_tbl + 2 (0x18f26): the dispatcher's x-offset table
  is the freshly built control table -> rebound to `ctrl` each frame.
- ground_view_off == obj_scan_off (0x18c58): one value (view_flags * 0xdd).

Also: ObjListCtx.px must be rebound to the frame's buffer each frame (we
alternate two screen buffers) — it was left NULL, so every object-list pixel
was written to address 0 instead of the screen; that was the last 1103-byte
under-draw. Screen buffers carry a SCREEN_OVERDRAW tail because
draw_game_objects writes off-screen sprite fragments well past the visible
32000 bytes.

Harness:
- DEMO_EXTRA_CFLAGS + DEMO_DUMP_STAGE cut the frame short after a chosen stage,
  so a headless run bisects an on-target divergence to one stage (that is how
  the NULL px was found: stages 0-2 matched, pass 1 carried the whole diff).

events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: blit_road_scroll fast top fill -> matches hand-asm

Profiling the pre-rotated blit showed the 13 KB constant top fill (the plane
pattern above the road band) was ~78% of the remaining cost, and GCC compiled it
to move.l #imm,(a0) (operand refetched every store, 20 cyc) in an indexed loop.

- src/scroll.c: fill via a post-increment pointer unrolled 8x, with the constant
  laundered into a register (asm barrier, no-op on host) so the stores are
  move.l dN,(a0) (12 cyc). blit_road_scroll 19.33 -> 11.98 ms (0.36x recon, ~1.02x
  the original hand-asm — the full 2.84x gap is now closed). Byte-identical.
- test/test_scroll.py: cover all 5 legs (was 0/2/4) — 40 cases, all byte-exact.
- STATUS.md: perf table (pipeline ~84 ms; remaster 0.76x recon).

Verified: full host suite 142/142; demo still MATCHes on the 68000.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: optimize blit_road_scroll via pre-rotated playfield
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: optimize blit_road_scroll via pre-rotated playfield

blit_road_scroll was the worst C-vs-asm ratio (2.84x the original): recreate
rotates every plane-word every frame (20x20x4 = 1600 variable-count rol.l). Since
the fine shift is constant across a frame and the playfield is static per leg, we
precompute instead.

- src/scroll.c: rm_scroll_prebuild() builds the 16 fine-shift pre-rotated copies of
  the playfield once (copy 0 == the raw playfield, which the edge seam reuses for
  its masked wrap blend); rm_blit_road_scroll() now plain-copies contiguous columns
  from copy[shift] — no per-word rotate. 33.55 -> 19.33 ms on the 68000 (0.58x the
  recon, ~1.64x the original, down from 2.84x). Byte-identical to the verified core.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: demo at -O2, double-buffered (no tear, no shift)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: demo at -O2, double-buffered (no tear, no shift)

Two on-target fixes to the interactive demo:
- build_demo.sh: -Os -> -O2 (matching recon) so the blit primitives inline; this
  ~halves the render cost (see tools/bench.py). The single-frame output is
  unchanged (still MATCHes golden on the 68000).
- demo_main.c: double-buffer the display. The old single-buffer memcpy to the live
  screen every frame tore badly at ~10 fps; now we render off-screen and flip the
  video base at the vblank via Setscreen. The two buffers are aligned to 256 bytes
  at RUNTIME (the ST shifter only uses the high/mid base bytes, so a non-256-aligned
  base is rounded down -> the image shifted); link-time alignment wasn't enough
  because the GEMDOS load base needn't be 256-aligned.
- os.s: add Cconis (non-blocking key poll), Vsync, and Setscreen trap wrappers.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: per-function 68000 cycle bench vs recon (+ machine model)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: per-function 68000 cycle bench vs recon (+ machine model)

Adds a cycle-accurate perf comparison of the remaster render cores against
recreate's recon, both cross-compiled to m68k and run under Musashi on the SAME
staged leg-1 frame.

- tools/bench.py: loads bench.elf (remaster) + recon game.elf, runs each stage via
  emu.run_bench, prints instructions/cycles/ms and the remaster/recon ratio; also
  benches g_render_road_machine (the byte-exact register/goto model).
- render/atari/bench_main.c + bench_build.sh: zero-work bench_<fn> entry wrappers
  that call each core with structs staged from the demo fixture; build to bench.elf
  at -O2 (matching recon).
- render/atari/gen_demo_fixture.py: extract staged_image() so the fixture bake and
  the bench measure the identical frame (else frame content skews the ratios).
- STATUS.md: perf section with results.

Findings: remaster is 0.96x the recon overall — on par or ahead per stage —
render_road 0.91x, and 0.89x vs the machine model (GCC optimises the native-pointer
C better than the hand-threaded transcription). The earlier "2x slow" was purely
-Os not inlining the blit primitives; -O2 fixes it. Remaining gap is algorithmic.

  steer loop, first-frame dump for the headless check.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: extract plane.h cell ops (fill / and / overlay)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: extract plane.h cell ops (fill / and / overlay)

The HUD repeated three two-line patterns that all operate on one ST "cell" (the
two plane-longs at `a` and `a`+4), differing only in the transform: plain fill,
AND-with-mask, and masked overlay. The overlay was moreover identical to text.c's
blit_row. Collapse all of them into a shared plane.h:

  cell_fill(px, at, lo, hi)                  -> wr32 both halves
  cell_and(px, at, mask)                     -> AND both halves
  cell_overlay(px, at, mask, ink, lo, hi)    -> (bg & mask) | (ink & fill)

Every 2-line write pair in hud.c is now one named op; text.c's blit_row is gone
(uses cell_overlay). No behavior change (pure refactor) — full suite 30 green.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: take Framebuffer* in the render primitives
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: take Framebuffer* in the render primitives

The dst buffer was uint8_t *px — the same type as the font/string/asset
pointers, so nothing stopped a wrong pointer being passed as the framebuffer.
Take Framebuffer* instead: the type now says exactly what it is, and the
compiler rejects passing an asset buffer as the draw target. (A bare pointer
typedef would read nicely but give no such safety — it converts freely to/from
any uint8_t*.) rm_glyph_run + the HUD phase functions take Framebuffer*; the
one-word leaf helpers (blit_row, overlay_word) stay raw addresses.

test_text binds the first arg as POINTER(Framebuffer) to match. Full suite 30
green (pure type change; codegen identical).
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: add Offset / Plane4 semantic types
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: add Offset / Plane4 semantic types

uint32_t was overloaded for two distinct roles that read identically: a byte
offset/cursor into a buffer, and a 4-plane 16px longword (two plane words). Add

events.title: S34+S35: case-insensitive asset lookup, Android touch fixes, Amiga sound repair
events.message:
S34+S35: case-insensitive asset lookup, Android touch fixes, Amiga sound repair

Case-sensitive filesystems (Linux, Android, R36S) never found SWOS files whose
capitalisation differed from our hardcoded literals, so the game reported "no
data" even when the files were in the right folder. Windows dev machines cannot
reproduce it. DataPaths gains ResolveFile/ResolveDir (exact case first, then a
case-insensitive probe returning the real path); every SWOS data lookup now goes
through it: the boot gate, TEAM.* enumeration, the grafs atlases, pitch variants,
charset, CD cue/img resolution and the .RAW sample index.

Amiga in-match sound had never been play-tested and was wrong three ways, all
verified by decoding SFX.SNG against the original 68k:
  - a goal played instrument 36, which in the original is only ever the
    near-miss "ooooh"; goals and misses were literally the same sound. Goals,
    penalties and full time now play the song-6 roar (instr 28 + 27).
  - the crowd bed ran at 8000 Hz instead of 16574 Hz, over an octave low on the
    quietest sample in the bank, so there was effectively no crowd.
  - the module's volume ramp was ignored, so reactions ended on a hot sample and
    were audibly chopped; the decay is now baked into the PCM.
Full time was silent on Amiga (win/lose/draw samples are PC-only).

Android had two inescapable dead ends: pausing hid the touch overlay while
nothing on a touch device could emit ui_cancel, and the full-time screen waited
on a keyboard-only ui_accept. The pad now stays up while paused (icon quits,
fire resumes) and every fire tap raises a discrete accept. Menu touch zones use
the bare bar instead of the match grace strip, which had been swallowing the
option rows' arrows and flipping the options page instead of changing a value.

Import/UX:
  - BOTH floppies are required: SFX.IN2 lives on disk 1, so "only disk 2 is
    used" was wrong and cost users all Amiga sound. Wording corrected, and the
    importer no longer short-circuits on graphics alone, so adding the missing
    disk later actually completes the import (bank probe invalidated after).
  - SOUND option always toggles instead of silently refusing an unavailable
    choice, and boot auto-selects a source that exists.
  - First-run screen prints on-screen diagnostics (searched paths, .adf counts,
    storage reachability, which of graphics/teams is missing) so reports from
    Android and handhelds are actionable.

Android storage: extraction output moves to the app-private dir; the public drop
folder stays in Download/OpenSWOS. Android export presets sign with the Godot
keystore so release exports are installable.

GFX_Promo/ (111 MB of personal media) added to .gitignore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: port glyph blitter (text_body)

buggyboy/remaster: port glyph blitter (text_body)

The shared glyph body recreate's HUD text/gauge/bar draws all converge on,
as one native primitive rm_glyph_run(). Font glyphs are 1bpp 16-byte cells;
a character pair packs into one 4-plane cell (char1 -> high byte of the
(mask,ink) words, char2 -> low byte), ink masked by the two colour planes.

Verified in isolation against recreate's own entry points (whole-framebuffer
byte-exact, not just coverage): recreate exports g_draw_hud_bar and
g_draw_hud_gauge0, which both hit this body — 960 fuzz cases (8 chunks x 2
modes x 60), random strings/offsets/fills/backgrounds, incl. the char2==0
last-cell glyph-0x2f substitution. test parametrized by chunk for xdist.

Unblocks HUD phases 6b/7 (gauge cluster); phase 7 still needs the dst/string
cursor chaining + draw_dashboard + buf_c before it lands.

events.title: buggyboy: cycle-accurate per-frame benchmark (original vs recon)
events.message:
buggyboy: cycle-accurate per-frame benchmark (original vs recon)

Measure the in-race pipeline's 68000 cost under Musashi, no Hatari needed,
to quantify why the reconstruction runs slower on a stock ST.

Harness:
- shim: tally each instruction's cycles (osh_num_cycles); add trap-free
  osh_run_bench to run our cross-compiled m68k recon functions (their OS-trap
  vectors sit inside the recon .text, so osh_run's vector install would corrupt
  them). emu: expose `cycles`, add run_bench.
- tools/bench_frame.py + `make bench`: stage a real mid-race frame, then time
  each pipeline function twice — the original machine code (emu.run) and the
  recon cross-compiled to m68k (game.elf, the BUGGY.PRG code, via run_bench).

Finding (stable across legs/frames): recon is ~2.1x slower than the original.
draw_game_objects + render_road dominate absolute cost; blit_road_scroll has
the worst efficiency gap (~2.8x, a move.l (a1)+,(a0)+ copy GCC doesn't match).
A compiler-efficiency gap, not an algorithmic regression (behaviour is verified
byte-identical). hatari --cpuclock 16 covers it.

Docs:
- README: Benchmarking section.

events.title: buggyboy: fix tunnel palette + 3 real game_update divergences
events.message:
buggyboy: fix tunnel palette + 3 real game_update divergences

Reconstruction (src/game_update.c):
- Mode-4 palette-fade must Setpalette the RACE palette (0x17fa2), not the
  0x17fb0 scratch base. The original stages the record into 0x17fb0.. then
  `suba #$18,a0` rewinds A0 to 0x17fa2 before the trap; the staging writes
  overlap race_palette regs 5/7-11 (a partial in-race fade), so reg0 stays
  black. Loading the +7-shifted scratch (reg0=tan) turned the tunnel
  background tan and shifted every colour -- the reported bug.
- Section-G spin/fx select read obj-0x1c/-0x1b; should be obj-2/-1 (a1 =
  obj+0x1e after the fx-block copy, then `suba #$20`) -- mis-selected the fx.
- fx_block_2e: byte store where the original's last write is `move.w`
  (word 0x003e).
- Section-H horizon-event dispatch passed d5=0; should be horizon_row /
  horizon_row+2 so handlers clear the obj_active/event_type slots (state
  drifted over real play otherwise).

Verification:
- make test green (272). The three image-affecting fixes were found by a
  game_update-vs-oracle differential over the real leg-0 course data (the
  random-data suite never triggered them). The mode-4 Setpalette target is
  off-image, so invisible to the whole-image oracle; verified by a Hatari
  memory snapshot -- recon vs original had byte-identical game state, but the
  recon's hardware palette held the +7 scratch while the original's held race.

Docs:
- STATUS.md: game_update row records the four palette-pass fixes.

Deferred:
- No harness test covers the real-course-data divergences; a real-course
  game_update differential test is a follow-up.

The differential harness compares the memory image, so it is blind to two kinds of
sound/OS trigger: off-image effects (Dosound writes the chip; play_event_tune's
INITTUNE only lands when unguarded) and fuzz-unreached branches. Both shipped
real bugs this session (countdown/idle beeps missing, checkpoint/collision/leg-end
jingles wrong) because the trigger was invisible to the diff.

Add a tool that finds them: the Musashi shim now tracks executed PCs
(osh_cov_*, gated off — zero cost to a normal run); test/conftest.py dumps each
xdist worker's coverage when COVGAP_DIR is set; tools/coverage_gap.py runs the
suite in parallel, merges the coverage, and reports every call site to a sound/OS
sink (Dosound/INITTUNE/INITFX/play_event_tune/handle_marker/stop_music) that no
test executed. Knowingly read-verified sites are allowlisted (coverage_gap_allow.txt
with reasons); the tool exits non-zero on a NEW gap.  runs it.

Seeded the allowlist with the 7 current gaps (the leg-start countdown, the
game_update event jingles corrected this session, and the high-score jingles) —
all read-verified from the disassembly / on-target psg traces. Runs in ~read the
suite's wall-clock (coverage overhead is negligible); differential suite unchanged
(261 pass), conftest is inert without COVGAP_DIR.

Docs: on-target-execution.md diagnostic toolkit.

buggyboy: fix wrong event jingles (checkpoint/leg-end/collision)

The jingle when driving over a branch (and at checkpoints / leg completion) was
wrong on-target — our reconstruction played tune 0 (the leg-select confirm) where
the original plays distinct tunes. game_update's checkpoint/collision/score-marker

bonus armed)=tune 6 @0x11a92. These three branches are fuzz-unreached, so
play_event_tune's INITTUNE never lands under test and the tune id is off-image to
the differential harness — they'd been left at placeholder 0.

GU_TUNE_LEG_END / GU_TUNE_COLL_MARK). Confirmed the other game_update tune ids
(GU_SCORE_TUNE=8, GU_CKPT_TUNE=9, GU_EVT_TUNE_A=a) ARE diff-verified (changing them
fails test_event_*), so this is the complete set of unverified tune-id guesses.

events.title: buggyboy: play engine idle + crash sounds on-target (Dosound A0 list)
events.message:
buggyboy: play engine idle + crash sounds on-target (Dosound A0 list)

Follow-up to the countdown fix. The game's sound EFFECTS (not the REFRESH-driven
music) are all XBIOS Dosound command lists that stop_music/stop_music_chk hand to
TOS in A0: the leg-start countdown (0x18bba/0x18bca), the engine idle when
stationary (0x18ba2, a repeating-envelope tone), the collision/spin sound
(0x18b78), and the crash sound (0x18b92). Dosound writes the YM2149 directly, so
the differential harness never saw the A0 list and the reconstruction dropped it
on every stop_music call — leaving all these effects silent on-target.

Thread the list faithfully (it is the original's A0):
- g_stop_music / g_stop_music_chk take a list_off and issue it via a new g_dosound
  seam (no-op in os.c for the .so; real XBIOS 32 in game_main.c, gated on hw_ready).
- Pass the right A_dosound_* list at each call site: game_update idle/collide,
  draw_crash_fx crash, game_main countdown (now routed through g_stop_music instead
  of a separate Dosound call).
- addrs.h: the five A_dosound_* list offsets.

Off-image, so the differential suite is unchanged (261 pass); test_stop_music
updated for the new signature. Verified headlessly (hatari --trace psg_write):
engine idle now emits reg13=0x0e (repeating envelope) continuously at speed 0,
alongside the 4 countdown beeps (reg13=0x00).

Docs: names.txt (dosound_idle/collide/crash), STATUS.md stop_music row,
memory note buggyboy-sound-architecture.

events.title: buggyboy: play the leg-start countdown beeps on-target (XBIOS Dosound)
events.message:
buggyboy: play the leg-start countdown beeps on-target (XBIOS Dosound)

The leg-start '3-2-1-go' countdown was silent in the playable PRG. It is not
produced by the game's own VBL music driver (REFRESH) but by TOS's XBIOS Dosound
engine: stop_music (0x12ec4), after parking the VBL sound vector, issues
Dosound(A0); main (0x1021c) hands it a beep command list on each of the four
race-start settle frames (3x 0x18bba then 0x18bca). All of it is off-image
(Dosound writes the YM2149 directly), so the differential harness never saw it —
the calls were dropped as no-ops and the VBL install had replaced TOS's _vblqueue
(dropping its Dosound stepper).

Reconstruction (PRG-only; cores + differential suite untouched, 261 pass):
- game_os.s: real Dosound XBIOS-32 wrapper.
- game_main.c: preserve TOS's _vblqueue entries after our handler (mirrors
  main 0x101b8) so TOS's per-VBL Dosound stepper runs; issue Dosound(beep/go)
  at the four settle frames (mirrors main 0x1021c-0x10250).
- game_main.c: clear conterm (0x484) to silence the TOS key-click (a separate
  divergence: present in ours, absent in the original which clears it @0x101dc).

Verified headlessly (hatari --trace psg_write): 4 beep sequences now drive the
YM hardware envelope (reg8=0x10, reg7=0xfe) at leg start.

Docs: names.txt (dosound_beep/go lists + stop_music note); on-target-execution.md
gains a fifth bug class (off-image OS services relied on for output); render/atari
README note.

events.title: buggyboy: inline the screen-fill cell copy (snappy leg-select menu)
events.message:
buggyboy: inline the screen-fill cell copy (snappy leg-select menu)

screen_fill_span/_rect copied each 8-byte colour cell with a memcpy call, so a
full-screen fill was ~1900 jsr-memcpy calls (3 stack pushes + cleanup each),
every frame. draw_leg_results full-screen-clears on every leg-select frame, so
this dominated the menu's frame time and made arrow-key stepping sluggish (the
3-frame auto-repeat felt slow at the depressed frame rate).

Copy the cell inline as two longwords via the be32/wr32 accessors (native move.l
on the 68000, byte-order-safe on the little-endian test host). The inner loop is
now two move.l per cell, no call. Speeds up every fill (menu, results, HUD,
race backgrounds). All 253 differential tests stay byte-identical; verified on
Hatari: leg-select is now as snappy as the original.

events.title: buggyboy: fix Crawio wrapper reading high word of its arg (F-keys, ESC)
events.message:
buggyboy: fix Crawio wrapper reading high word of its arg (F-keys, ESC)

The Crawio wrapper did `move.w 4(%sp)` to fetch its `short w` argument, but the
C ABI passes `short` in a 4-byte slot — on big-endian m68k the value sits in the
LOW word (6(%sp)), so it read the high word (0x0000) instead of 0x00ff. GEMDOS
Crawio(0) writes a NUL char and returns 0, so every console poll silently did
nothing: leg-select F1-F5 (console scancode) and the in-race ESC-to-quit both
went through it and were dead. Read the longword and push its low word, the same
idiom Fcreate/Fopen already use. Verified on Hatari: F1 starts a leg, ESC quits.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: buggyboy: make the on-target PRG run at ~ST speed (native-endian access)
events.message:
buggyboy: make the on-target PRG run at ~ST speed (native-endian access)

The playable PRG ran ~4x too slow on a stock 8 MHz ST — menu and race alike,
independent of render_road. Root cause: the big-endian image accessors
(be16/be32/wr16/wr32 in machine.h) compiled to a byte-by-byte lsl-#8 shuffle
on EVERY multi-byte access in every draw/blit routine. Those helpers exist to
preserve the 68000's byte order on the little-endian test host, but the m68k
target is itself big-endian, so there they are just aligned move.w/move.l.

Fixes (PRG-only; the differential harness is untouched — 253 tests still green):
- machine.h: #if __BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__ -> native aligned
  load/store on-target; keep the byte assembly on the little-endian host so the
  verified behaviour is byte-identical. Kills the shuffle (PRG ~40% smaller).
- game_build.sh: -O2 (was -Os) + -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns (stop GCC
  turning the hand-written mem* loops into self-calls).
- game_main.c: long-word memcpy/memset when aligned.

Also fixes the apparent screen-shift, which was frame-overrun tearing: with the
frame back inside the 20 ms vblank budget, flip_screen latches cleanly.

Tooling:
- oracle shim/emu: expose osh_num_insns() — per-run instruction count for
  perf profiling (read-only, additive; how render_road/menu costs were measured).

Docs: render/atari/README Performance note (endian gotcha + --cpuclock), and a
machine.h pointer in recreate/README.

events.title: buggyboy: 256-align the display buffers at runtime + drop debug ifdefs
events.message:
buggyboy: 256-align the display buffers at runtime + drop debug ifdefs

The ST video shifter can only display from a 256-byte-aligned base (low 8 address
bits ignored). physbase_tbl held image+offset, but GEMDOS loads image at an
arbitrary (non-256) address, so the displayed base was truncated ~24 bytes below
the drawn data. Round each buffer's runtime address up to a 256 boundary. Also
removed the NO_IKBD/NO_SND/SKIP_ATTRACT bisection ifdefs now that the game runs.

events.message:
buggyboy: playable PRG shim + toolchain fixes (boots, loads, unpacks on ST)

Builds the whole verified reconstruction into a runnable GEMDOS .PRG (game_main.c
game loop + game_os.s traps/hardware), extending the static-screen render/atari path.
Now boots on real TOS in Hatari, loads COURSES.DAT/GRAPHICS.GRA (handle 64), and
completes g_unpack_graphics on-target. Remaining: a hang in the in-race render frame
loop (tracked next).

Reconstruction:
- game_main.c: mirrors decomp.c main() — user-mode file load + unpack, then Super()
  for the hardware phase; strong overrides of the (now weak) no-op boundary glue
  (g_flip_screen video-base flip, g_wait_vbl_set_offset, g_xbios_setpalette,
  g_set_rez/read_joystick/install_handlers IKBD path, g_load_graphics); VBL sound
  driver via _vblqueue; SMOKE build (-DSMOKE=N) for headless framebuffer verification.
- game_os.s: GEMDOS/XBIOS wrappers + IKBD joystick-packet handler. File-I/O wrappers
  MUST precede the control wrappers or Hatari GEMDOS-HD returns handle 0 (stdin).
- src/screen.c, src/road.c: mark g_flip_screen / g_wait_vbl_set_offset BB_WEAK so the
  PRG can override them; harness .so keeps one definition (253 tests still green).

Harness/toolchain:
- tos.ld: ALIGN(256) before .bss + .bss (NOLOAD) SUBALIGN(1) so a 256-aligned image
  symbol can't push .bss past text+data (was silently corrupting BSS on-target).
- mkprg.py: pad text to _bss_start so GEMDOS places BSS exactly after text+data.

events.title: buggyboy: add COURSES.DAT course editor + verified road/game viewers
events.message:
buggyboy: add COURSES.DAT course editor + verified road/game viewers

A new projects/buggyboy/editor/ toolkit to decode, edit and visualise
COURSES.DAT, built on the verified reconstruction (libbuggyboy.so).

Decode / edit (stdlib only):
- course_format.py  file<->memory map + 8-byte record decoder (constants
  mirrored from the verified C, each tagged with its source symbol)
- course_file.py    patch-in-place editor: markers, mask, control(rows/slope),
  scroll table, dashboard track pixels; backup-on-save, lossless round-trip
- roadprofile.py    decode the road elevation profile (segment slope + rows)
  and the roadside-object slots from the record stream
- decode_course.py  CLI stream/scroll/marker dump

Findings (empirical, pinned by tests): each 8-byte record = 15-bit select
mask + control (rows = (b&0xf8)>>3, slope = (b&7)-3) + marker word (bit15 =
event; runs = continuous features). Elevation is in the file; the horizontal
curve is runtime steering state (not in the file).

Visualise (drives the verified cores via ctypes):
- tui.py       curses editor: record browser, live dashboard-map paint,
  road elevation profile w/ live slope edit, PNG + live in-terminal 3rd-person
- roadview.py  render_road -> PNG/ASCII; GameSession drives init_leg +
  game_update + draw_frame (the whole verified game)
- roadwin.py   playable pygame window: held keys -> game_update/draw_frame,
  authentic road + object sprites + buggy + HUD (real pixels)

test_roundtrip.py: 14 tests (identity + edit round-trips, map/profile decode,
render pipeline); optional pygame/.so tests skip cleanly when absent.

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify game_update @ 0x1110e (89/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify game_update @ 0x1110e (89/91)

The per-frame in-race game-logic driver — the root of the three remaining
orchestrators (intermission + init_playfield both call it). No OS traps and it
returns each frame, so it verifies run-to-rts against the Musashi oracle despite
being the largest single function (2452 bytes, ~50 state globals + 7 tables).

Reconstruction (src/game_update.c, sections mirror the decomp)
- 1-11 (common path): pending-marker gate + engine-sound; input; fire ->
  dashboard-variant anim; bonus-time countdown; lean-anim + spin overrides;
  crash/auto-steer script vs live steering; engine-RPM/speed model + EGFREQ;
  scroll speed + view-flags wrap; wheel position + lean; road-curve integration,
  edge clamp, off-road crash; then build_road_geometry + return.
- 12 (course advance, view-wrap frames): collision probe, road_seg_data +
  road_curve_tbl shuffles, packed course-record unpack (control-code expansion),
  sprite-mode dispatch (scroll/palette), fx-block rebuild, event-jump-table
  dispatch, and the checkpoint/collision/score markers.
- gu_dispatch_event: table-driven event-jump-table dispatch to the evt_* family
  (evt_flag_gate alt entries; score-message groups A/B/C with per-entry gate +
  delta -> add_score + play_event_tune(8); checkpoint counters).

Test (test/test_game_update.py, ~580 cases; poison off — game_update is a
stateful RMW function, so the plain whole-image diff is the correct check)
- common-path fuzz (400); course else/pull/modes/crash/course fuzz; event
  dispatch idx 1-23. Full suite green (243 passed).

Fixes from code review: the fx-block base clear is clr.l (not a word); the
edge clamp uses lsr.w (unsigned); the score-message dispatch handles idx 14-23
distinctly (not collapsed into one handler).

Residuals (read-verified): sprite-mode 6 (object-display palette-swap
recw-0x7db4 write), the probe_collision D1-return path, and the idx 6/12
evt_flag_gate d7=6 variant.

events.title: buggyboy: shard the 5 heavy fuzz/blit tests across xdist workers (3.4m -> 1.8m)
events.message:
buggyboy: shard the 5 heavy fuzz/blit tests across xdist workers (3.4m -> 1.8m)

Harness:
- The 5 tests that dominated the suite (100-183s each) were single pytest items,
  so xdist couldn't split them and one gated the whole parallel run. Shard each
  by separating case generation from checking: a generator replays the one seeded
  RNG stream (cheap) and a `chunk`-parametrized test runs only iterations where
  `i % FUZZ_CHUNKS == chunk`. Coverage is byte-identical (round-robin is an exact
  partition of the iteration range); re-seeding per chunk would change inputs.
    - test_obj_blit_engine::test_bare_fuzz            (183s, /8)
    - test_obj_blit_engine::test_bare_widths_every_fine_x (107s, parametrized by fine_x)
    - test_blit_objshift_w2::test_fuzz                (156s, /8)
    - test_blit_objshift::test_fuzz                   (155s, /8)
    - test_blit_objshift2::test_fuzz                  (153s, /8)
  Full suite 3m24s -> 1m50s. Sub-8s fuzz tests left un-sharded (an order of
  magnitude below the parallel floor; sharding would add worker overhead + diff).

Docs:

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify draw_object_list @ 0x1306e (88/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify draw_object_list @ 0x1306e (88/91)

Reconstruction
- The per-frame roadside-object display-list dispatcher (register-glue). Two
  nested loops walk the object list; each object's a3 flag word gates a SPECIAL
  pass (record @buf_a+0x21d0+d6, only when the word is negative) and a NORMAL
  pass keyed on the low 6 bits (type -> record @buf_a+0x8a0+type*0xd0+d6). Each
  record yields colour, a buf_c-relative src long, rows-1, a vertical seed byte,
  the obj_type_jumptable index, and per-object x/dst offsets; the resolved
  handler is jsr'd. a0/a3/d2/d3/d4/d6 are saved/restored around the jsr, so the
  per-object vertical + x dst adjustments are temporary.
- Handlers wired: noop (bare rts), objsprite t1/t2/t4/w88, the t4+t1 stub
  @0x131ac, and the handler_lo mid-entries 0x1466a (0x98) / 0x144b2 (0x90, via
  the g_blit_objshift_w2 family). obj_handler_lo shared by both mid-entries.
- Decode note: prg_dis mis-renders the vertical-position muls.w/mulu.w as
  `and.w ...,a7`; the real math is (vseed-rows).b * view_flags >> 4 * width.
- d6 is sign-extended into the record base (adda.w), matching the 68000; the
  real caller (draw_game_objects tail) always passes d4=0 (one outer row).

Test
- test_object_list.py: isolating cases for every handler + jump-table index,
  the vertical offset, per-object x/dst offsets, the bonus-window type clamp,
  and the special pass; a 400-seed 15-object fuzz over the real d4=0 case; and

events.title: buggyboy: add render_road two-layer equivalence render tool
events.message:
buggyboy: add render_road two-layer equivalence render tool

render/render_road.py feeds an identical input image to both render_road forms
(g_render_road, the idiomatic default; g_render_road_machine, the byte-exact
anchor), de-interleaves each Atari low-res framebuffer to a PNG, and diffs them
pixel-for-pixel — a visual companion to the differential test. Confirms 0
framebuffer bytes differ between the layers.

A listening tool (like render_screen.py), not part of the differential contract;
PNGs land in the gitignored out/render/. The staged input is SYNTHETIC: the real
per-scanline road geometry (road_width_src / road_seg_data) is dynamic game state
that game_update computes while driving and is zero in a cold image, so the
picture is flat perspective bands, not a gameplay road. Once the frame pipeline
is reconstructed (or a live frame is captured), real road state drops into the
same code path to draw the actual road.

  decode; pad a final partial screen so it still renders.

buggyboy: reconstruct + verify update_highscore (66/91, checkpoint)

Phase 3 of the input-oracle work (HARNESS.md) — and simpler than the plan. The tail
of the real function is the interactive name-entry loop (busy-polls the IKBD, Vsyncs,
waits on MZFLAG), which can't run to rts. Rather than model all that, the candidate
implements only the deterministic prefix and the oracle is stopped at the two prefix

  ('0'->'/'); rank the new 6-digit score against the leg's 9-row table by a byte-wise

  one (overlapping copy, high-to-low, 12 of each 0xe-byte row), and insert the 12-byte
  score+name record. This populates highscore_table -> the results screen's SCORE/NAME
  rows. Decoded with capstone (m68k); the shift/insert pointer walk is exact.

events.title: buggyboy: IKBD memory model + verify read_joystick (60/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: IKBD memory model + verify read_joystick (60/91)

Phase 1 of the input-oracle work (HARNESS.md). read_joystick busy-waits the IKBD
6850 ACIA's TDRE bit at $fffffc00 then sends the 0x16 joystick-interrogate command;
under the oracle it used to spin forever because reads above the 1 MiB image returned
0, so the bit was never set.

- oracle/shim.c: model IKBD_STATUS ($fffc00 on the 24-bit bus) as always TDRE-ready,
  so the wait loop terminates. The command write to IKBD_DATA lands above the image
  and is dropped by the existing bounds check (no capture needed — input state is
  scripted as an image global, see HARNESS.md), so read_joystick has no image effect.
- src/os.c: g_read_joystick — no-op glue (like xbios_setscreen).
- test/test_input.py: run-to-rts, empty whole-image diff (reaching rts is the check).

events.title: recreate: add attribution (poison) pass to catch coincidental passes (#3)
events.message:
recreate: add attribution (poison) pass to catch coincidental passes (#3)

The plain diff proves final-image equivalence, so a candidate can pass by
coincidence: it never writes a byte the oracle wrote, but that byte already
held the oracle's value (an output landing in a zeroed/base region). Add an
opt-in attribution pass that removes the coincidence.

  - harness._attribution_check: re-run both cores on a copy of the input
    where every oracle-written byte is poisoned (its normal final value,
    inverted). A byte the candidate fails to write stays canary instead of
    matching, so the omission surfaces. Gated on differential(poison=True)
    and only after the plain pass is clean (safe for leaf functions;
    poisoning a control-steering output could perturb a complex run).
  - test_poison_catches_coincidental_write: a stub writing 0x00 over a
    zeroed byte with a do-nothing candidate passes the plain diff but is
    caught with poison=True (proves the guard fires).
  - Enable poison on the leaf tests whose outputs aren't pre-seeded:
    add_score edge cases (score_str HUD digits) and the screen fills
    (zeroed draw buffer). README notes the pass.

events.title: recreate: cross-validate Musashi against a real 68000 (ISA conformance, #5)
events.message:
recreate: cross-validate Musashi against a real 68000 (ISA conformance, #5)

The differential suite proves each function matches Musashi; this certifies
Musashi itself against an independent, hardware-validated 68000 (Hatari's
WinUAE core), so "verified against Musashi" means "verified against a real
68000" for the instruction mix BuggyBoy uses.

  - oracle/isa_conformance.py: 277 self-contained, position-independent
    instruction snippets (inputs = immediates, flags captured with move sr
    immediately after the tested op, result saved via (a5)+). Runs the
    identical bytes on Musashi (emu.run) and real TOS (headless Hatari) and
    compares result + defined CCR bits. Classes: byte/word/long memory RMW
    (the class Unicorn mis-handled), asr/lsr/lsl/rox/ro, ext, movea.w,
    muls/mulu/divs/divu, add/sub/addx/subx, cmp.b+Scc, swap/neg.
  - tos_probe.py: extract run_tos_program() (reused by both harnesses).
  - test/test_isa_vs_tos.py: skips without Hatari/TOS; else asserts 277/277.

Result: all 277 match. The only core divergence found was N/Z after a
DIVS/DIVU overflow, which the 68000 PRM defines as *undefined* — so it is
excluded from the CCR comparison (result and the defined V flag still agree).
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: recreate: vet diff exclude bands against the oracle's stack extent (#6)
events.message:
recreate: vet diff exclude bands against the oracle's stack extent (#6)

An exclude band suspends the byte-for-byte guarantee for its range, so a
band that dropped a real (non-stack) divergence would pass silently. Vet
every band before use:

  - oracle (shim.c) now tracks the deepest stack pointer reached (min_a7),
    exposed via emu.run's out_regs.
  - _vet_exclude_bands (A) requires the band to extend past min_a7 — a band
    entirely below where A7 descended cannot be stack; (D) rejects a named
    global (names.txt) sitting *below* min_a7 — provably not stack.

Verifying it surfaced a real subtlety: _start relocates its stack across
trace_pc@0x1b040, so a naive "reject any named global" is wrong — a global
the stack sits *over* is legitimately reused as scratch. The check allows
named globals at/above min_a7 and only refuses ones below it. Empirically
the _start band's below-stack bytes are untouched, so it stays sound.

test_exclude_band_guards pins all three cases (A fires, D fires, reuse ok).
events.author: ganneheim

The fill and blit tests only fed small, clean values, so the word-vs-long
register handling was asserted by construction (& 0xffff in the test), never
verified against the oracle. The disassembly shows these are word ops:
fill uses lsl.w #3 (colour) + sign-extended adda.w (offset) + dbf (count);
the blit glue takes width/x/row_offset/rows as int16/uint16. So the high 16
bits must be ignored and the colour offset sign-extends (0x1000<<3 = 0x8000).

  - harness.hi_garbage(rng, low_word): pack a low word with random high bits;
    shared by both tests (one definition, not copied).
  - test_screen: full-range colour + high-garbage counts/offsets in the fuzz,
    plus test_register_masking pinning the lsl.w/dbf/adda.w edges (colour
    sign flip, high word ignored) with explicit values.
  - test_blit: splat random high bits on the four word registers (width, x,
    row_offset, rows) while a6/fills stay full 32-bit.

Verified against the asm first (no wider domain that would diverge); all green.
Other suites left as-is: test_road already targets 16-bit overflow, test_events
enumerates discrete branches, test_graphics feeds random source to the shifts.

events.title: recreate: widen add_score fuzz to the full byte domain
events.message:
recreate: widen add_score fuzz to the full byte domain

The score fuzz only exercised ASCII digits (0x30..0x39), leaving the
signed-carry edge untested. The disassembly shows the per-digit carry is
a signed cmp.b/bpl against '9' with a manual sub.b #10 (no BCD/decimal-
adjust op anywhere in the binary), so the reconstruction's
(int8_t)('9' - digit) < 0 should hold for every byte, not just digits.

  - test_fuzz now draws full-range bytes (0..255) for score and delta;
    score/delta live in fixed 6-byte buffers, so any value is memory-safe.
  - test_boundary_bytes pins the carry decision at each digit position for
    bytes straddling the flip (0x39/0x3a), the int8 sign boundary
    (0x7f/0x80), the blank-walk char (0x30), and the extremes, plus
    add.l/.w wraparound cases.

add_score is now verified byte-equivalent across the whole input domain.

events.title: recreate: cross-check the OS trap model against real TOS (headless Hatari)
events.message:
recreate: cross-check the OS trap model against real TOS (headless Hatari)

Anchor the deterministic shim (shim.c + os.h) to a genuine TOS ROM so its
hand-modeled semantics are validated against real hardware, not just
asserted.

Harness:
  - oracle/tos_probe.py assembles a small GEMDOS program that runs Malloc,
    Getrez and a sequence of Freads, writes a fixed-layout record to a
    GEMDOS drive, and Pterm0s. It auto-runs headless under Hatari (SDL
    dummy video, --fast-forward) and reads the record back from the host
    dir — no debugger/breakpoint/load-address needed. Mshrink prologue so
    Malloc has a free pool.
  - test/test_os_vs_tos.py compares the capture to the shim: exact-value
    calls (Getrez low-res, Fread bytes + cursor/EOF counts) must match to
    the byte; Malloc's machine-dependent address is checked as the
    invariant the shim also honors (even-aligned, non-overlapping, odd
    size rounded up to even). Skips when Hatari or a TOS ROM is absent
    (the ROM isn't redistributable).

Docs:
  - README OS-trap section documents the two test layers.
  - docs/tos-os-calls.md adds the reusable headless-Hatari technique.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: recreate: pin the OS trap model's semantics with shim-contract tests
events.message:
recreate: pin the OS trap model's semantics with shim-contract tests

The existing OS tests validate the reconstructed wrappers through the
differential harness but never stress the shim's own semantics at the
edges. Add five tests that drive tiny hand-assembled 68k stubs through
the oracle to pin shim.c + os.h directly:

  - Malloc bump-allocation + odd-size rounding to even
  - Fread cursor advance, partial read at EOF, zero past EOF
  - Fopen reopen rewinds the cursor
  - Fread on a closed handle is rejected (emu.run raises, not silently served)
  - Fopen of an unstaged file is rejected

A regression in these semantics now fails here instead of silently
inside a caller's differential test.

events.title: buggyboy-sound: add C64 SID transcode of the YM2149 stream
events.message:
buggyboy-sound: add C64 SID transcode of the YM2149 stream

Play BuggyBoy's tunes and effects on a Commodore 64 SID (reSID-fp /
pyresidfp) by transcoding the same per-frame YM register stream the
existing renderer captures. `sound_player.py --synth sid` writes
out/sound/*_sid.wav beside the YM references.

Mapping: YM square -> SID 50% pulse; YM noise -> SID noise, clocked from
the YM noise rate (SID clocks its LFSR from the voice frequency, so using
the stale tone period would silence noise FX); per-channel YM volume and
hardware envelope -> per-voice software amplitude scaling (SID has no
per-voice volume, and this stands in for YM's hardware-envelope "buzz").
Output is AC-coupled and faded in to mimic the real C64 and drop reSID's
reset transient. The envelope AM advances by the samples reSID actually
emits per frame, so it stays aligned to the audio with no drift.

Faithful port of the ST arrangement/timing in SID timbre; not a re-scored
native C64 tune.

events.title: Comment the endgame chain; settle the Competence Rating formula
events.message:
Comment the endgame chain; settle the Competence Rating formula

Competence Rating (RatingScore, ex-'EndgameFlag') decoded exactly:
  crew term  = sum of 2 x strength over live human crew (no Android)
  room term  = +1 per room with damage < 20 (34 rooms max)
  oxygen term= 2 x leading digit of the oxygen counter
capped at 100. Which terms an ending adds distinguishes outcomes:
alien killed = crew+rooms+oxygen; escape/crew-lost/oxygen-out with
destruct armed = crew+oxygen; ship exploded = oxygen only; alien
survives to Earth = 0.

Also: five endgame entry points documented with their exact screen
texts; PrintDeadRoster/PrintAndroidReveal/PrintRating (ASCII
count-out with the RatingHundred '10' patch); item pickers and

The 'sprite-class identity match' story in CrewAction4_Handler /

actor's current ROOM, so all of these are plain room co-location
checks. Rewrote those headers; GatherSameClassSlots ->

- CrewHitsAlien/CrewHitsAndroid guards are strength>=2 AND morale>=2

  (not a 'corridor scan position'). Net = single-use (netting also
  destroys it); trackers shatter but still wound; extinguishers only
  scare; harpoon kills attacker+bystanders and adds 15 room damage;

  'corridor index') — 6+ wounds with a dormant Android sets

events.title: Decode the 238 encounter marker: press-time RmveGrille->ATTACK swap
events.message:
Decode the 238 encounter marker: press-time RmveGrille->ATTACK swap

The stub cluster at $B2B9-$B31D is the hostile-in-room menu logic,
run by RoomModeDispatch before EVERY mode-0/1 action dispatch:

- ForceAttackRowIfHostile ($B2C0): in the room view, when the alien
  (slot 0) — or, once AlienActiveFlag is $FF, the alien-target/Android
  slot — is in the viewed actor's room, the special row (cell 13) is
  forced to 52 'ATTACK' and redrawn. If the press landed on 49
  'RmveGrille', the mirror byte is set to 238: the swap happened under
  the cursor within the same key release.
- SpecialRowAction ($B306): 238 -> restore 52 but still start the
  timed grille removal — the player's original intent is honoured;

events.title: Bootstrap Godot project + adf/rnc/team decoders + variant abstraction
events.message:
Bootstrap Godot project + adf/rnc/team decoders + variant abstraction

Three CLI tools and a Godot project that proves the PC/Amiga variant
abstraction works end-to-end:

- tools/adf-extract: pure-C# Amiga DD ADF reader (OFS + FFS). Verified
  against both SWOS Amiga floppies (125 files extracted, OFS Standard,
  volumes "SWOS" and "SWOS2").
- tools/rnc-decode: RNC ProPack v1 decoder. Both Amiga SWOS executables
  (165735 and 168061 bytes packed) decompress with CRC OK to 351596 and
  357226 bytes respectively. Implementation follows aybe/RNCUnpacker's
  model: 2-byte init, eager refill (bitcount < 16), p starts at offset 0.
- tools/team-decode: SWOS PC/Amiga TEAM.* parser. Verified team header
  (coach offset +0x24 not +0x26 as some specs claim), 3-bit-nibble skill
  packing, decimal nation-code filename suffix. ARSENAL TEAM.008 yields
  ARSENE WENGER as coach and Bergkamp with all-8 P/S/H/T/C/Sp/F.
- game/: Godot 4.6.2 + C# (.NET 9) project with IAssetSource interface
  and concrete PcAssetSource + AmigaAssetSource implementations. Game
  builds + runs headless, loading 1730 PC teams and 1616 Amiga teams from
  the local reference data — both yielding identical first team
  (ALBPETROL PATOS / FATMIR DOGANI / LEONARD HASA) which proves the
  format truly is shared across variants.

Tooling itself is held in .tools/godot/ (portable, gitignored). Original
SWOS data dirs stay gitignored. CLAUDE.md and READMEs updated to match
working build/run commands.
